modules.title: Properties of the field strength
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The structural theorems about the electromagnetic field strength in the jet
algebras of QED: antisymmetry, the expression of the field strength through
the potential coordinates, and the **Bianchi identity**

`∂_λ F_{μν} + ∂_μ F_{νλ} + ∂_ν F_{λμ} = 0`,

the homogeneous half of Maxwell's equations.  In the jet algebra the Bianchi
identity is exact and purely combinatorial: each term is a difference of
second-derivative coordinates, and the six coordinates cancel in pairs because
multiset addition is commutative — Clairaut's theorem is built into the
indexing.

This file contains no definitions, only theorems about the fields of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`.

## ii. Key results

- `Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_antisymm`,
  `JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_antisymm` : antisymmetry of the field strength.
- `JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_eq_sub` : the field strength through the
  potential coordinates, `F_{μν} = ∂_μ A_ν - ∂_ν A_μ`.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_bianchi`,
  `JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_bianchi` : **the Bianchi identity**.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The field strength in the photon jet algebra
  - A.1. Antisymmetry
  - A.2. The Bianchi identity
- B. The field strength in the QED jet algebra
- C. The total derivative on the fields

## iv. References

The fields are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`.  The inhomogeneous half of
Maxwell's equations is dynamical (it needs the variation of the Lagrangian)
and is not part of the jet-algebra kinematics.

sections.text:
## A. The field strength in the photon jet algebra

### A.1. Antisymmetry

### A.2. The Bianchi identity

Each field strength is a difference of two second-derivative coordinates; the
cyclic sum produces six coordinates which cancel in pairs, because the
multisets `s + {μ} + {ν}` and `s + {ν} + {μ}` are equal.

## B. The field strength in the QED jet algebra

The theorems of section A, transported through the inclusion of the photon
factor into the QED jet algebra.
## C. The total derivative on the fields

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_antisymm
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_antisymm (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength s μ ν = -fieldStrength s ν μ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_self
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_self (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength s μ μ = 0

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_bianchi
declarations.doc:
**The Bianchi identity** `∂_lam F_{μν} + ∂_μ F_{ν lam} + ∂_ν F_{lam μ} = 0`
in the photon jet algebra: the homogeneous Maxwell equations hold exactly,
for every derivative order `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_bianchi (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (lam μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength (s + {lam}) μ ν + fieldStrength (s + {μ}) ν lam +
      fieldStrength (s + {ν}) lam μ = 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_eq_sub
declarations.doc:
The field strength is the antisymmetrised derivative of the potential,
`∂_s F_{μν} = ∂_s ∂_μ A_ν - ∂_s ∂_ν A_μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_eq_sub (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength s μ ν = A (s + {μ}) ν - A (s + {ν}) μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_antisymm
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_antisymm (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength s μ ν = -fieldStrength s ν μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_self
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_self (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength s μ μ = 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_bianchi
declarations.doc: **The Bianchi identity** in the QED jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_bianchi (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (lam μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength (s + {lam}) μ ν + fieldStrength (s + {μ}) ν lam +
      fieldStrength (s + {ν}) lam μ = 0

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_singleton_eq_jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The first-order field-strength jet is the total derivative of the
zeroth-order one, in the photon jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_singleton_eq_jetDeriv
    (ρ μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength {ρ} μ ν =
      Photon.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv ρ (Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength 0 μ ν)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_A
declarations.doc:
The total derivative appends the derivative index to the photon jet
coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_A (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jetDeriv ρ (A s μ) = A (s + {ρ}) μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_ψ
declarations.doc:
The total derivative appends the derivative index to the electron jet
coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_ψ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    jetDeriv ρ (ψ s α) = ψ (s + {ρ}) α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_barψ
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_barψ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    jetDeriv ρ (barψ s α) = barψ (s + {ρ}) α

modules.title: Properties of the γ matrices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The defining properties of the Dirac γ matrices of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`, in
the chiral representation:

* the **Clifford algebra relation** `γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`, which
  makes the Dirac operator a square root of the wave operator;
* the hermiticity properties `(γ⁰ γ^μ)† = γ⁰ γ^μ` and
  `(γ^μ)† = γ⁰ γ^μ γ⁰`, which make the Dirac Lagrangian hermitian;
* the factorisation `γ⁰ γ^μ` of the contraction matrices of the kinetic term.

This file contains no definitions, only theorems about the fields of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`.

## ii. Key results

- `JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_mul_add_swap` : **the Clifford algebra relation**.
- `JetAlgebra.kineticGamma_eq_gammaMatrix_mul` : the contraction matrices of
  the kinetic term are `γ⁰ γ^μ`.
- `JetAlgebra.kineticGamma_conjTranspose` : the contraction matrices are
  self-adjoint.
- `JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_conjTranspose` : `(γ^μ)† = γ⁰ γ^μ γ⁰`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Pauli anticommutators
- B. The Clifford algebra relation
- C. Hermiticity

## iv. References

The γ matrices are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`; the Pauli matrices are
those of `Physlib.Relativity.PauliMatrices`.

sections.text:
## A. The Pauli anticommutators

The two block identities behind the Clifford relation:
`σ^μ σ̄^ν + σ^ν σ̄^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1` and `σ̄^μ σ^ν + σ̄^ν σ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`,
with `σ̄^μ = η_{μμ} σ^μ` (no sum).  Both reduce to the anticommutation
relations of the Pauli matrices.
## B. The Clifford algebra relation
## C. Hermiticity

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.pauliMatrix_mul_smul_add_swap
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliMatrix_mul_smul_add_swap (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    σ μ * (η ν ν • σ ν) + σ ν * (η μ μ • σ μ) =
      (2 * η μ ν) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.smul_pauliMatrix_mul_add_swap
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_pauliMatrix_mul_add_swap (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (η μ μ • σ μ) * σ ν + (η ν ν • σ ν) * σ μ =
      (2 * η μ ν) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_mul_add_swap
declarations.doc:
**The Clifford algebra relation** of the Dirac γ matrices:
`γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`.  This is the algebraic identity that
makes the Dirac operator a square root of the wave operator, and hence the
Dirac equation relativistic.
declarations.statement:
lemma gammaMatrix_mul_add_swap (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    gammaMatrix μ * gammaMatrix ν + gammaMatrix ν * gammaMatrix μ =
      (2 * η μ ν) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_sq
declarations.doc: The square of a γ matrix: `(γ^μ)² = η^{μμ} 1` (no sum).
declarations.statement:
lemma gammaMatrix_sq (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    gammaMatrix μ * gammaMatrix μ =
      (η μ μ) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_anticommute
declarations.doc: The γ matrices of distinct indices anticommute.
declarations.statement:
lemma gammaMatrix_anticommute {μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3} (h : μ ≠ ν) :
    gammaMatrix μ * gammaMatrix ν = -(gammaMatrix ν * gammaMatrix μ)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_inl_zero
declarations.doc: `γ⁰` in the chiral representation is the block off-diagonal identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma gammaMatrix_inl_zero :
    gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0) = Matrix.fromBlocks 0 1 1 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.kineticGamma_eq_gammaMatrix_mul
declarations.doc: The contraction matrices of the kinetic term are `γ⁰ γ^μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma kineticGamma_eq_gammaMatrix_mul (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    kineticGamma μ = gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0) * gammaMatrix μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.kineticGamma_conjTranspose
declarations.statement:
lemma kineticGamma_conjTranspose (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (kineticGamma μ)ᴴ = kineticGamma μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_zero_conjTranspose
declarations.doc: `γ⁰` is self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma gammaMatrix_zero_conjTranspose :
    (gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0))ᴴ = gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix_conjTranspose
declarations.doc: The hermiticity relation of the γ matrices, `(γ^μ)† = γ⁰ γ^μ γ⁰`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gammaMatrix_conjTranspose (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (gammaMatrix μ)ᴴ =
      gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0) * gammaMatrix μ * gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0)

modules.title: Gauge invariance of quantum electrodynamics
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The gauge-theoretic theorems of QED, culminating in the gauge invariance of
the QED Lagrangian, `gaugeAction_lagrangian`.  The chain of results
decomposes exactly as in the physics texts:

* on the photon jet algebra the gauge transformations form a group acting by
  affine shifts (`Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_comp`), and the field
  strength and the Maxwell term are invariant because the shift of `∂_s A_μ`
  is symmetric in the derivative indices — Clairaut's theorem is built into
  the multiset indexing (`Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_fieldStrength`);
* the electron coordinates rotate by the phase and its conjugate, and the
  trivial gauge jet acts trivially (`Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_trivial`);
* the covariant derivative is covariant, `D_μ ψ ↦ ū D_μ ψ`, because the
  photon shift `∂_μ χ` cancels the derivative `∂_μ ū = -i e (∂_μ χ) ū` of
  the phase (`gaugeAction_covDψ`);
* every charge-neutral fermion bilinear is invariant because the phases of
  the electron and its conjugate cancel by unitarity
  (`gaugeAction_mul_phase_cancel`);
* the Lagrangian, being built from invariant pieces, is invariant
  (`gaugeAction_lagrangian`).

This file contains no definitions, only theorems about the jet algebras of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`, the fields of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`
and the Lagrangian of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`.

## ii. Key results

- `Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_comp`, `Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_zero` :
  the photon gauge transformations form a group acting on the photon jet
  algebra.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_fieldStrength`,
  `Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_maxwellTerm` : gauge invariance of the field
  strength and the Maxwell term.
- `Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_trivial`, `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_trivial` :
  the trivial gauge jet acts trivially.
- `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_A`, `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ψ_zero`,
  `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ψ_singleton` (and the `barψ` versions) : the action
  on the jet coordinates of QED.
- `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_covDψ`, `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_covDbarψ` : gauge
  covariance of the covariant derivatives.
- `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_diracKineticTerm`,
  `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_electronMassTerm` : gauge invariance of the terms
  of the Lagrangian.
- `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_lagrangian` : **gauge invariance of the QED
  Lagrangian**.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gauge group acting on the photon jet algebra
  - A.1. Gauge invariance of the field strength and the Maxwell term
- B. The trivial gauge jet acts trivially
- C. The action on the jet coordinates of QED
  - C.1. The photon coordinates
  - C.2. The electron coordinates
  - C.3. The field strength and the Maxwell term
- D. Gauge covariance of the covariant derivatives
- E. Gauge invariance of the Lagrangian
  - E.1. Cancellation of the phases in fermion bilinears
  - E.2. Invariance of each term
  - E.3. Invariance of the QED Lagrangian

## iv. References

The jet algebras and gauge actions are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`, the
fields in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields` and the Lagrangian in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`.

sections.text: ## A. The gauge group acting on the photon jet algebra

### A.1. Gauge invariance of the field strength and the Maxwell term

The field strength is gauge invariant, and the reason is exactly that
multiset addition is commutative: the two shifts are `∂_s ∂_μ ∂_ν χ` and
`∂_s ∂_ν ∂_μ χ`, indexed by `s + {μ} + {ν}` and `s + {ν} + {μ}`.  Clairaut's
lemma is built into the indexing.

## B. The trivial gauge jet acts trivially

The key combinatorial fact: in the Leibniz sum over the antidiagonal of `t`,
the splitting `(0, t)` occurs exactly once, so an indicator supported at the
zero multiset picks out the identity.

## C. The action on the jet coordinates of QED

### C.1. The photon coordinates

The photon coordinate shifts by a *constant* of the jet algebra, the jet
`∂_s ∂_μ χ` of the gauge function; in the full algebra the constant is the
scalar multiple `(∂_s ∂_μ χ) • 1`.

### C.2. The electron coordinates

The electron (charge `-1`) rotates by the conjugate phase, its conjugate
(charge `+1`) by the phase; on first-order jets the Leibniz rule feeds the
first derivative of the phase into the zeroth-order coordinate.

### C.3. The field strength and the Maxwell term

Both invariances are inherited from the photon jet algebra, where the proof
is the commutativity of multiset addition.

## D. Gauge covariance of the covariant derivatives

Under a gauge transformation the photon coordinate shifts by `∂_μ χ` while
the first-order electron coordinate picks up the derivative
`∂_μ ū = -i e (∂_μ χ) ū` of the phase by the Leibniz rule; the two
contributions cancel and the covariant derivative rotates like the field
itself.

## E. Gauge invariance of the Lagrangian

### E.1. Cancellation of the phases in fermion bilinears
### E.2. Invariance of each term
### E.3. Invariance of the QED Lagrangian

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_comp
declarations.doc:
Photon gauge jets compose by addition: the gauge transformations form a
group acting on the photon jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_comp (c₁ c₂ : GaugeJet) :
    (gaugeAction c₁).comp (gaugeAction c₂) = gaugeAction (c₁ + c₂)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_zero
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeAction_zero : gaugeAction 0 = AlgHom.id ℝ JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_fieldStrength
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_fieldStrength (c : GaugeJet) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    gaugeAction c (fieldStrength s μ ν) = fieldStrength s μ ν

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_maxwellTerm
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeAction_maxwellTerm (c : GaugeJet) : gaugeAction c maxwellTerm = maxwellTerm

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_trivial
declarations.doc:
The trivial gauge jet acts trivially on the electron jet algebra: the
gauge action is unital.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_trivial (e : ℝ) :
    gaugeAction (GaugeJet.trivial e) = AlgHom.id ℂ JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_trivial
declarations.doc:
The trivial gauge jet acts trivially on the QED jet algebra: the gauge
action is unital.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_trivial (e : ℝ) :
    gaugeAction (GaugeJet.trivial e) = AlgHom.id ℂ JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_mul
declarations.doc: The electron gauge actions compose through the monoid of gauge jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_mul {e : ℝ} (g₁ g₂ : GaugeJet e) :
    (Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction g₁).comp (Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction g₂) =
      Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction (g₁ * g₂)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeActionPhoton_comp
declarations.doc:
The complexified photon gauge actions compose by addition of the gauge
jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeActionPhoton_comp (c₁ c₂ : Photon.JetAlgebra.GaugeJet) :
    (gaugeActionPhoton c₁).comp (gaugeActionPhoton c₂) =
      gaugeActionPhoton (c₁ + c₂)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_mul
declarations.doc:
**The gauge actions compose through the monoid of gauge jets**: the QED
gauge action is a monoid action on the jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_mul {e : ℝ} (g₁ g₂ : GaugeJet e) :
    (gaugeAction g₁).comp (gaugeAction g₂) = gaugeAction (g₁ * g₂)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_mul_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_mul_apply {e : ℝ} (g₁ g₂ : GaugeJet e) (x : JetAlgebra) :
    gaugeAction (g₁ * g₂) x = gaugeAction g₁ (gaugeAction g₂ x)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_A
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the photon jet coordinate: the affine shift
`∂_s A_μ ↦ ∂_s A_μ + ∂_s ∂_μ χ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_A {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    gaugeAction g (A s μ) = A s μ + (g.χjet (s + {μ}) : ℂ) • 1

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ψ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ψ_zero {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ψ 0 α) = star (g.phase 0) • ψ 0 α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_barψ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_barψ_zero {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (barψ 0 α) = g.phase 0 • barψ 0 α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ψ_singleton {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ψ {μ} α) =
      star (g.phase 0) • ψ {μ} α + star (g.phase {μ}) • ψ 0 α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_barψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_barψ_singleton {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (barψ {μ} α) =
      g.phase 0 • barψ {μ} α + g.phase {μ} • barψ 0 α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_fieldStrength
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_fieldStrength {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    gaugeAction g (fieldStrength s μ ν) = fieldStrength s μ ν

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_maxwellTerm
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_maxwellTerm {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    gaugeAction g maxwellTerm = maxwellTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_covDψ
declarations.doc:
**Gauge covariance of the covariant derivative**: `D_μ ψ` rotates by the
conjugate phase, exactly like `ψ` itself.  The shift of the photon
coordinate cancels the derivative of the phase.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_covDψ {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (covDψ e μ α) = star (g.phase 0) • covDψ e μ α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_covDbarψ
declarations.doc:
Gauge covariance of the conjugate covariant derivative: `D_μ ψ̄` rotates
by the phase, exactly like `ψ̄` itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_covDbarψ {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (covDbarψ e μ α) = g.phase 0 • covDbarψ e μ α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_mul_phase_cancel
declarations.doc:
A product of a factor rotating by the phase and a factor rotating by the
conjugate phase is gauge invariant: the phases cancel by unitarity.  This is
the reason every charge-neutral fermion bilinear of QED is gauge
invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_mul_phase_cancel {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) {x y : JetAlgebra}
    (hx : gaugeAction g x = g.phase 0 • x)
    (hy : gaugeAction g y = star (g.phase 0) • y) :
    gaugeAction g (x * y) = x * y

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_diracKineticTerm
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_diracKineticTerm {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    gaugeAction g (diracKineticTerm e) = diracKineticTerm e

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_diracKineticTermBar
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_diracKineticTermBar {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    gaugeAction g (diracKineticTermBar e) = diracKineticTermBar e

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_electronMassTerm
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_electronMassTerm {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    gaugeAction g electronMassTerm = electronMassTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
**Gauge invariance of the QED Lagrangian.**  The Maxwell term is invariant
by the symmetry of the photon shift in its derivative indices, the kinetic
term by the covariance of the covariant derivative, and the mass term by the
unitarity of the phase.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_lagrangian {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (m : ℝ) :
    gaugeAction g (lagrangian e m) = lagrangian e m

modules.title: Completeness of the field strength for gauge invariance
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The classification of the gauge invariants of the photon jet algebra:
**an element of the photon jet algebra is invariant under every gauge
transformation if and only if it is a polynomial in the derivatives
`∂_s F_{μν}` of the field strength** —
`gaugeInvariant_iff_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength`.

One direction is the gauge invariance of the field strength.  For the other,
the gauge action translates all jet coordinates with the same symmetrized
index class `s + {μ}` by a common arbitrary amount, so an invariant is a
polynomial in differences of same-class coordinates
(`MvPolynomial.mem_adjoin_range_X_sub_X_of_forall_aeval_add_eq`), and every
such difference is a derivative of the field strength.

This is the abelian counterpart of the fixed-algebra theorems of
`Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeBosons.Gluons.JetCompleteness`.

This file contains no definitions, only theorems about the jet algebras of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`.

## ii. Key results

- `Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeInvariant_iff_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength` : **the
  gauge invariants of the photon jet algebra are exactly the polynomials in
  the derivatives of the field strength**.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The symmetrized-index class projection
- B. Differences of same-class coordinates are field strengths
- C. The completeness theorem

## iv. References

The class projection is defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`; the
translation-invariance engine is `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.MvPolynomialTranslation`;
the non-abelian analogue is
`Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeBosons.Gluons.JetCompleteness`.

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.indexClass_dA
declarations.statement:
lemma indexClass_dA (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (JetGenerators.dA s μ).indexClass = s + {μ}

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.indexClass_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma indexClass_ne_zero (j : JetGenerators) : j.indexClass ≠ 0

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.indexClass_classProj
declarations.doc:
Erasing the class representative and putting it back as the Lorentz index
preserves the class.
declarations.statement:
lemma indexClass_classProj (j : JetGenerators) :
    j.classProj.indexClass = j.indexClass

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.classProj_idem
declarations.doc: The class projection is idempotent.
declarations.statement: lemma classProj_idem (j : JetGenerators) : j.classProj.classProj = j.classProj

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.classProj_eq_classProj_iff
declarations.doc:
Two jet coordinates have the same class projection exactly when they lie
in the same symmetrized-index class.
declarations.statement:
lemma classProj_eq_classProj_iff (j j' : JetGenerators) :
    j.classProj = j'.classProj ↔ j.indexClass = j'.indexClass

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.coord_sub_classProj
declarations.doc:
A jet coordinate minus the canonical coordinate of its class is a
derivative of the field strength.
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_sub_classProj (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (h : (JetGenerators.dA s μ).classProj ≠ JetGenerators.dA s μ) :
    (X (JetGenerators.dA s μ) : JetAlgebra) - X ((JetGenerators.dA s μ).classProj) =
      fieldStrength (s.erase (classRep (s + {μ}))) (classRep (s + {μ})) μ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength_mem_range
declarations.doc: Every field-strength jet lies in the range of the field-strength family.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_mem_range (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength t μ ν ∈ Set.range (fun p :
        Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) =>
        fieldStrength p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeInvariant_iff_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength
declarations.doc:
**Completeness of the field strength for gauge invariance**: an element of
the photon jet algebra is invariant under every gauge transformation if and
only if it is a polynomial in the derivatives `∂_s F_{μν}` of the field
strength.  The field strength does not just provide *some* gauge invariants
— it generates *all* of them.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeInvariant_iff_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength (x : JetAlgebra) :
    (∀ c : GaugeJet, gaugeAction c x = x) ↔
      x ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℝ (Set.range fun p :
        Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) =>
        fieldStrength p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)

modules.title: The QED Lagrangian
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Lagrangian of quantum electrodynamics as an element of the QED jet
algebra:

`L = - 1/4 F_{μν} F^{μν} + i ψ̄ γ^μ D_μ ψ - m ψ̄ ψ`,

with `D_μ ψ = ∂_μ ψ + i e A_μ ψ` the covariant derivative of the electron
(electric charge `-1`) and the γ matrices taken in the chiral (Weyl)
representation.  Here `ψ̄` denotes the conjugate jet coordinates `ψ†`; the
`γ⁰` of `ψ̄ = ψ† γ⁰` is kept explicitly in the contraction matrices
`γ⁰ γ^μ` and `γ⁰`.

This file contains only definitions; the gauge invariance of every term and
of the full Lagrangian is proved in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GaugeInvariance`.

## ii. Key results

- `JetAlgebra.diracKineticTerm`, `JetAlgebra.diracKineticTermBar` : the Dirac
  kinetic terms `i ψ̄ γ^μ D_μ ψ` and `-i (D_μ ψ̄) γ⁰ γ^μ ψ`.
- `JetAlgebra.electronMassTerm` : the Dirac mass term `ψ̄ ψ`.
- `JetAlgebra.diracCurrent` : the Dirac current `J^μ = ψ̄ γ^μ ψ`.
- `JetAlgebra.lagrangian` : the QED Lagrangian.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Dirac kinetic terms and the mass term
- B. The QED Lagrangian
- C. B'. The equations of motion

## iv. References

The fields are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`; gauge invariance is proved in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GaugeInvariance`.

sections.text: ## A. The Dirac kinetic terms and the mass term
## B. The QED Lagrangian

## C. B'. The equations of motion

The Euler–Lagrange equations of the QED Lagrangian, as elements of the jet
algebra whose vanishing expresses the equations of motion.  Deriving them
*variationally* from `lagrangian` requires a variational calculus on the jet
algebra, which is future work; here they are definitions, and
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.CurrentCoupling` proves the Noether identity that the
divergence of the Dirac current is a combination of them.

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.diracKineticTerm
declarations.doc:
The Dirac kinetic term `i ψ̄ γ^μ D_μ ψ = i ψ†_α (γ⁰ γ^μ)_{αβ} (D_μ ψ)_β`
of the electron.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diracKineticTerm (e : ℝ) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.diracKineticTermBar
declarations.doc:
The conjugate Dirac kinetic term
`-i (D_μ ψ̄) γ⁰ γ^μ ψ = -i (D_μ ψ̄)_α (γ⁰ γ^μ)_{αβ} ψ_β`; the hermitian form
of the kinetic term is the average of `diracKineticTerm` and this term.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diracKineticTermBar (e : ℝ) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.electronMassTerm
declarations.doc:
The Dirac mass term `ψ̄ ψ = ψ†_α (γ⁰)_{αβ} ψ_β` of the electron.  This is
the dimension-three term available because the electron is a Dirac fermion:
its two Weyl components have the same electric charge, so the bilinear
pairing them against the conjugate components is charge neutral.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def electronMassTerm : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.diracCurrent
declarations.doc:
The Dirac current `J^μ = ψ̄ γ^μ ψ = ψ†_α (γ⁰ γ^μ)_{αβ} ψ_β` of the
electron: the Noether current of the `U(1)_em` phase symmetry.  Its coupling
`- e J^μ A_μ` to the photon is the entire interaction of QED — this is the
jet-algebra counterpart of the current coupling of
`Physlib.Electromagnetism.Dynamics`; see `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.CurrentCoupling`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diracCurrent (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.diracEquation
declarations.doc:
The Dirac-equation element `γ⁰ (i γ^μ D_μ - m) ψ`, row `α`: its vanishing
is the interacting Dirac equation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diracEquation (e m : ℝ) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.diracAdjEquation
declarations.doc:
The adjoint Dirac-equation element `i (D_μ ψ̄) γ⁰ γ^μ + m ψ̄ γ⁰`,
column `β`: its vanishing is the interacting adjoint Dirac equation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diracAdjEquation (e m : ℝ) (β : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.qedMaxwellEquation
declarations.doc:
The QED Maxwell-equation element `∂_μ F^{μν} - e J^ν`: its vanishing is
the inhomogeneous Maxwell equation sourced by the Dirac current.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def qedMaxwellEquation (e : ℝ) (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lagrangian
declarations.doc:
The QED Lagrangian
`L = - 1/4 F_{μν} F^{μν} + i ψ̄ γ^μ D_μ ψ - m ψ̄ ψ`
with electric coupling `e` and electron mass `m`, as an element of the QED
jet algebra.  Evaluated on an honest electromagnetic potential, the first
term is the Maxwell Lagrangian of `Physlib.Electromagnetism`; see
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Evaluation`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lagrangian (e m : ℝ) : JetAlgebra

modules.title: Lorentz invariance of quantum electrodynamics
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Lorentz-theoretic theorems of QED, culminating in the Lorentz invariance
of the QED Lagrangian, `lorentzAction_lagrangian`.  The chain of results:

* the covering map `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup` intertwines the conjugation
  of the covariant Pauli matrices with the Lorentz transformation of their
  index; combined with the defining property `Λ η Λᵀ = η` of the Lorentz
  group this yields the two contraction identities of the spinor
  representation (`sum_lorentz_inv_conjTranspose_pauli_conj` and
  `sum_lorentz_inv_eta_pauli_conj`), which assemble block-diagonally into
  the contraction identity of the kinetic matrices `γ⁰ γ^μ`
  (`sum_kineticGamma_contraction`);
* the jet coordinates of QED transform as tensors and spinors
  (`lorentzAction_A_zero`, `lorentzAction_ψ_singleton`, …), and the covariant
  derivative transforms exactly like the first-order jet
  (`lorentzAction_covDψ`);
* the Maxwell term is invariant because `Λ⁻¹ η (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ = η`
  (`Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_maxwellTerm`), the mass term because the
  spinor representation preserves `γ⁰`
  (`spinorRep_conjTranspose_gammaZero_spinorRep`), and the kinetic term by
  the contraction identity;
* the Lagrangian, being built from invariant pieces, is invariant
  (`lorentzAction_lagrangian`).

This file contains no definitions, only theorems about the jet algebras of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`, the fields of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`
and the Lagrangian of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`.

## ii. Key results

- `sum_kineticGamma_contraction` : the Lorentz contraction identity of the
  matrices `γ⁰ γ^μ` under the spinor representation.
- `spinorRep_conjTranspose_gammaZero_spinorRep` : the spinor representation
  preserves `γ⁰`.
- `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_A_zero`, `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ψ_zero`,
  `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ψ_singleton`, … : the transformation laws of the
  jet coordinates.
- `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_covDψ` : Lorentz covariance of the covariant
  derivative.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_maxwellTerm`,
  `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_maxwellTerm` : Lorentz invariance of the Maxwell
  term.
- `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_electronMassTerm`,
  `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_diracKineticTerm` : Lorentz invariance of the
  fermionic terms.
- `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_lagrangian` : **Lorentz invariance of the QED
  Lagrangian**.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Contractions of the Minkowski metric with a Lorentz transformation
- B. The intertwining identities of the spinor representation
  - B.1. Conjugation of the covariant Pauli matrices
  - B.2. The two block identities
  - B.3. The contraction identity of the kinetic matrices
  - B.4. The spinor representation preserves `γ⁰`
- C. The transformation laws of the jet coordinates
- D. Lorentz invariance of the Maxwell term
- E. Lorentz covariance of the covariant derivative
- F. Lorentz invariance of the fermionic terms
- G. Lorentz invariance of the QED Lagrangian

## iv. References

The Lorentz actions are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`; the corresponding
machinery for the lepton–gauge sector is
`Physlib.Particles.LeptonGaugeSector.JetAlgebra.LorentzAction`.

declarations.name: QED.sum_eta_inv_inv
declarations.doc:
The defining property of the Lorentz group in index form: contracting two
rows of `Λ⁻¹` with the Minkowski metric reproduces the metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_eta_inv_inv (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (τ τ' : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ μ, η μ μ * ((Λ⁻¹).1 τ μ * (Λ⁻¹).1 τ' μ) = η τ τ'

declarations.name: QED.pauliSelfAdjoint'_coe
declarations.doc: The covariant Pauli matrices are `σ̄^μ = η_{μμ} σ^μ` (no sum).
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliSelfAdjoint'_coe (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' μ).1 = η μ μ • σ μ

declarations.name: QED.kineticGamma_eq_fromBlocks_pauliSelfAdjoint'
declarations.doc:
The kinetic matrices through the covariant Pauli matrices:
`γ⁰ γ^μ = ((σ̄^μ, 0), (0, η_{μμ} σ̄^μ))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma kineticGamma_eq_fromBlocks_pauliSelfAdjoint' (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    JetAlgebra.kineticGamma μ =
      Matrix.fromBlocks (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' μ).1 0 0
        (η μ μ • (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' μ).1)

declarations.name: QED.sl2c_conj_pauliSelfAdjoint'
declarations.doc:
Conjugating a covariant Pauli matrix by `N : SL(2,ℂ)` transforms its
index by the image of `N` in the Lorentz group; this is the defining
property of the covering map.
declarations.statement:
lemma sl2c_conj_pauliSelfAdjoint' (N : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    N.1 * (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' μ).1 * N.1ᴴ =
      ∑ ν, (Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup N).1 ν μ •
        (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' ν).1

declarations.name: QED.sum_fromBlocks
declarations.doc: A block matrix summed over the diagonal blocks.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_fromBlocks {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (A : ι → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) (D : ι → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    ∑ i ∈ s, Matrix.fromBlocks (A i) 0 0 (D i) =
      Matrix.fromBlocks (∑ i ∈ s, A i) 0 0 (∑ i ∈ s, D i)

declarations.name: QED.sum_lorentz_inv_conjTranspose_pauli_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_lorentz_inv_conjTranspose_pauli_conj (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (τ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ μ, ((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ μ •
        (M.1ᴴ * (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' μ).1 * M.1) =
      (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' τ).1

declarations.name: QED.sum_lorentz_inv_eta_pauli_conj
declarations.doc:
The right Weyl block: transporting the index of `η_{μμ} σ̄^μ` with
`Λ(M)⁻¹` cancels the conjugation by `(M⁻¹)†`, through `Λ⁻¹ η (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ = η`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_lorentz_inv_eta_pauli_conj (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (τ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ μ, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ μ * η μ μ) •
        ((M⁻¹).1 * (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' μ).1 * ((M⁻¹).1)ᴴ) =
      η τ τ • (PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint' τ).1

declarations.name: QED.sum_lorentz_inv_spinorRep_kineticGamma
declarations.doc:
The matrix form of the contraction identity: transporting the vector index
of `γ⁰ γ^μ` with `Λ(M)⁻¹` cancels the conjugation by the spinor
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_lorentz_inv_spinorRep_kineticGamma (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (τ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ μ, ((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ μ •
        ((Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M)ᴴ * JetAlgebra.kineticGamma μ *
          Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M) =
      JetAlgebra.kineticGamma τ

declarations.name: QED.sum_kineticGamma_contraction
declarations.doc:
**The contraction identity of the Dirac kinetic term**: the index form of
`∑_μ (Λ⁻¹)_{τμ} S(M)† (γ⁰ γ^μ) S(M) = γ⁰ γ^τ`.  This is the identity that
makes `i ψ̄ γ^μ D_μ ψ` a Lorentz scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_kineticGamma_contraction (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (τ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α' β' : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    ∑ μ, ∑ α, ∑ β, JetAlgebra.kineticGamma μ α β *
        (star (Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M α α') *
          (((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ μ : ℝ) : ℂ) *
            Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M β β')) =
      JetAlgebra.kineticGamma τ α' β'

declarations.name: QED.spinorRep_conjTranspose_gammaZero_spinorRep
declarations.doc:
The spinor representation preserves `γ⁰`: `S(M)† γ⁰ S(M) = γ⁰`.  This is
the identity that makes the Dirac mass term `m ψ̄ ψ` a Lorentz scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma spinorRep_conjTranspose_gammaZero_spinorRep (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    (Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M)ᴴ * JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0) *
      Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M = JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0)

declarations.name: QED.sum_gammaZero_contraction
declarations.doc: The index form of `S(M)† γ⁰ S(M) = γ⁰`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_gammaZero_contraction (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (α' β' : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    ∑ α, ∑ β, JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0) α β *
        (star (Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M α α') *
          Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M β β') =
      JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix (Sum.inl 0) α' β'

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_A_zero
declarations.doc: The photon jet coordinate transforms as a covector.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_A_zero (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    lorentzAction M (A 0 μ) =
      ∑ ν, ((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • A 0 ν

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_A_singleton
declarations.doc: The first-order photon jet coordinate transforms as a two-tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_A_singleton (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (ρ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    lorentzAction M (A {ρ} μ) =
      ∑ τ, ∑ ν, ((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ ρ *
          ((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • A {τ} ν

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ψ_zero
declarations.doc: The electron jet coordinate transforms in the spinor representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_ψ_zero (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (ψ 0 α) =
      ∑ β, Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M α β • ψ 0 β

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_barψ_zero
declarations.doc:
The conjugate electron jet coordinate transforms in the conjugate spinor
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_barψ_zero (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (barψ 0 α) =
      ∑ β, star (Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M α β) • barψ 0 β

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ψ_singleton
declarations.doc:
The first-order electron jet coordinate transforms as a spinor with a
covector derivative index.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_ψ_singleton (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (ψ {ρ} α) =
      ∑ τ, ∑ β, (((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ ρ : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M α β) • ψ {τ} β

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_barψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_barψ_singleton (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (barψ {ρ} α) =
      ∑ τ, ∑ β, (((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ ρ : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          star (Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M α β)) • barψ {τ} β

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_fieldStrength_zero
declarations.doc: The formal field strength transforms as an antisymmetric two-tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_fieldStrength_zero (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    lorentzAction Λ (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) =
      ∑ a, ∑ b, ((Λ⁻¹).1 a μ * (Λ⁻¹).1 b ν) • fieldStrength 0 a b

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_maxwellTerm
declarations.doc:
**Lorentz invariance of the Maxwell term** in the photon jet algebra:
the two metric contractions absorb the four transformation matrices through
`Λ⁻¹ η (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ = η`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_maxwellTerm (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) :
    lorentzAction Λ maxwellTerm = maxwellTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_maxwellTerm
declarations.doc:
**Lorentz invariance of the Maxwell term** in the QED jet algebra,
inherited from the photon jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_maxwellTerm (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    lorentzAction M maxwellTerm = maxwellTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_covDψ
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivative transforms exactly like the first-order jet
coordinate: as a spinor with a covector derivative index.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_covDψ (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (e : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (β : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (covDψ e μ β) =
      ∑ τ, ∑ β', (((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ μ : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep M β β') • covDψ e τ β'

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_electronMassTerm
declarations.doc:
**Lorentz invariance of the Dirac mass term**: the spinor phases of the
electron and its conjugate cancel through `S(M)† γ⁰ S(M) = γ⁰`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_electronMassTerm (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    lorentzAction M electronMassTerm = electronMassTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_diracKineticTerm
declarations.doc:
**Lorentz invariance of the Dirac kinetic term**: the transformation of
the two spinor slots and the derivative slot cancels through the contraction
identity of the matrices `γ⁰ γ^μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_diracKineticTerm (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (e : ℝ) :
    lorentzAction M (diracKineticTerm e) = diracKineticTerm e

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
**Lorentz invariance of the QED Lagrangian.**  The Maxwell term is
invariant through `Λ⁻¹ η (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ = η`, the kinetic term through the
contraction identity of `γ⁰ γ^μ` under the spinor representation, and the
mass term through `S(M)† γ⁰ S(M) = γ⁰`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_lagrangian (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (e m : ℝ) :
    lorentzAction M (lagrangian e m) = lagrangian e m

modules.title: Mass dimensions in quantum electrodynamics
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The mass-dimension bookkeeping of QED, through the mass-weight scaling of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic` (the algebra map multiplying each jet coordinate by `c`
to twice its mass dimension): the photon has dimension one, the electron
`3/2`, and each derivative adds one.  The theorems of this file identify the
composite fields and the terms of the Lagrangian as eigenvectors of the
scaling:

* the covariant derivative `D_μ ψ` is homogeneous of weight five — this is
  the statement that the electric coupling `e` is dimensionless, which is
  what makes QED renormalizable;
* the Maxwell term and the Dirac kinetic term have weight eight (mass
  dimension four), and the mass term weight six (dimension three);
* consequently `L(e, c² m)` scales to `c⁸ L(e, m)`: the Lagrangian has mass
  dimension four with the electron mass a coefficient of dimension one.

This file contains no definitions, only theorems.

## ii. Key results

- `JetAlgebra.massScale_A_zero`, `JetAlgebra.massScale_ψ`, … : the scaling of
  the jet coordinates.
- `JetAlgebra.massScale_covDψ` : the covariant derivative is homogeneous of
  weight five; the coupling is dimensionless.
- `JetAlgebra.massScale_maxwellTerm`, `JetAlgebra.massScale_diracKineticTerm`,
  `JetAlgebra.massScale_electronMassTerm` : the weights of the terms.
- `JetAlgebra.massScale_lagrangian` : **the QED Lagrangian has mass dimension
  four**.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The scaling of the jet coordinates
- B. Homogeneity of the field strength and the covariant derivative
- C. The weights of the terms of the Lagrangian
- D. The mass dimension of the QED Lagrangian

## iv. References

The scaling maps are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`; the corresponding
grading for the lepton–gauge sector is
`Physlib.Particles.LeptonGaugeSector.JetAlgebra.MassDim`.

sections.text: TODO: Upgrade the mass-weight scaling to a genuine filtration by submodules, following
TODO: `LeptonGaugeSector.JetAlgebra.MassDim` (`MassWeightLESubmodule`), together with the
TODO: derivative-order and fermion-parity gradings needed for classification arguments.

## A. The scaling of the jet coordinates

The photon-level scaling of the field strength and the Maxwell term, used to
lift the weight of the Maxwell term to the QED jet algebra.
## B. Homogeneity of the field strength and the covariant derivative

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.massScale_fieldStrength_zero
declarations.doc: The photon-level field strength has mass dimension two.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_fieldStrength_zero (c : ℝ) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    massScale c (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) = c ^ 4 • fieldStrength 0 μ ν

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.massScale_maxwellTerm
declarations.doc: The photon-level Maxwell term has mass dimension four.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_maxwellTerm (c : ℝ) :
    massScale c maxwellTerm = c ^ 8 • maxwellTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_A
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_A (c : ℝ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    massScale c (A s μ) = (c : ℂ) ^ (2 + 2 * Multiset.card s) • A s μ

declarations.statement:

    massScale c (ψ s α) = (c : ℂ) ^ (3 + 2 * Multiset.card s) • ψ s α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_barψ
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_barψ (c : ℝ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    massScale c (barψ s α) = (c : ℂ) ^ (3 + 2 * Multiset.card s) • barψ s α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_A_zero
declarations.doc: The photon jet coordinate has mass dimension one.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_A_zero (c : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    massScale c (A 0 μ) = (c : ℂ) ^ 2 • A 0 μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_ψ_zero
declarations.doc: The electron jet coordinate has mass dimension `3/2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_ψ_zero (c : ℝ) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    massScale c (ψ 0 α) = (c : ℂ) ^ 3 • ψ 0 α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_barψ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_barψ_zero (c : ℝ) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    massScale c (barψ 0 α) = (c : ℂ) ^ 3 • barψ 0 α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_ψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_ψ_singleton (c : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    massScale c (ψ {μ} α) = (c : ℂ) ^ 5 • ψ {μ} α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_barψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_barψ_singleton (c : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    massScale c (barψ {μ} α) = (c : ℂ) ^ 5 • barψ {μ} α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_fieldStrength_zero
declarations.doc: The field strength has mass dimension two.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_fieldStrength_zero (c : ℝ) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    massScale c (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) = (c : ℂ) ^ 4 • fieldStrength 0 μ ν

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_covDψ
declarations.doc:
**The covariant derivative is homogeneous**, of the same weight as the
plain derivative: the electric coupling `e` is dimensionless.  This is the
power-counting statement behind the renormalizability of QED.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_covDψ (c : ℝ) (e : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    massScale c (covDψ e μ α) = (c : ℂ) ^ 5 • covDψ e μ α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_covDbarψ
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_covDbarψ (c : ℝ) (e : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    massScale c (covDbarψ e μ α) = (c : ℂ) ^ 5 • covDbarψ e μ α

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_maxwellTerm
declarations.doc: The Maxwell term has mass dimension four.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_maxwellTerm (c : ℝ) :
    massScale c maxwellTerm = (c : ℂ) ^ 8 • maxwellTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_diracKineticTerm
declarations.doc: The Dirac kinetic term has mass dimension four.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_diracKineticTerm (c : ℝ) (e : ℝ) :
    massScale c (diracKineticTerm e) = (c : ℂ) ^ 8 • diracKineticTerm e

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_diracKineticTermBar
declarations.doc: The conjugate Dirac kinetic term has mass dimension four.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_diracKineticTermBar (c : ℝ) (e : ℝ) :
    massScale c (diracKineticTermBar e) = (c : ℂ) ^ 8 • diracKineticTermBar e

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_electronMassTerm
declarations.doc: The Dirac mass term has mass dimension three.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_electronMassTerm (c : ℝ) :
    massScale c electronMassTerm = (c : ℂ) ^ 6 • electronMassTerm

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
**The QED Lagrangian has mass dimension four.**  Rescaling all fields by
their mass weights takes `L(e, c² m)` to `c⁸ L(e, m)`: the coupling `e` is
dimensionless and the electron mass is a coefficient of dimension one, so
every term of the Lagrangian is renormalizable.
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_lagrangian (c : ℝ) (e m : ℝ) :
    massScale c (lagrangian e (c ^ 2 * m)) = (c : ℂ) ^ 8 • lagrangian e m

modules.title: Down-type singlets
modules.doc:
The basis of the down-type singlet `(3, 1)_{-2}`, its Lorentz and gauge actions on components,
and the gauge weights of the components.

## i. Overview

The Standard Model down-type singlet is a right-handed Weyl spinor in the `(3, 1)_{-2}`
representation. Here charges are normalized as `6Y`, so `-2` is the usual hypercharge
`Y = -1/3`. Its value space `DownSinglet`, the Lorentz action `DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup` and
the gauge action `DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI` are in
`Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.Fermions.DownSinglet`. The Weyl factor carries the Lorentz
index and the three-dimensional factor the colour index. The absence of a weak factor makes it
an `SU(2)` singlet.

This file writes both actions on the basis of spinor–colour tensors, together with their dual,
conjugate and conjugate-dual forms, which are what a component of a down-singlet symbol needs.
The centre `-1` of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `-1`, as on any single Weyl-spinor index. The gauge torus
acts diagonally on the basis, with the colour weights and hypercharge `-2`.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.basis` : the basis of spinor–colour tensors.
- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_apply_basis`,
  `StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_apply_basis` : the Lorentz and gauge actions on the
  basis, with their dual and conjugate forms.
- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_neg_one` : the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `-1`.
- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.valueGaugeWeight` : the gauge weights of the basis, with
  `StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_gaugeTorusGen_basis`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The basis
- B. The Lorentz action on components
- C. The gauge action on components
- D. The gauge weights of the components

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The basis

The basis of `DownSinglet` is the tensor product of the right-handed Weyl basis and the standard
colour basis.

## B. The Lorentz action on components

The Lorentz group moves only the spinor index. Dualising inverts and transposes the coefficient
matrix, and conjugating stars it.

## C. The gauge action on components

The gauge group moves only the colour index, up to the hypercharge scalar.

## D. The gauge weights of the components

The gauge torus acts diagonally on the basis of `DownSinglet`. The weights are recorded by
`DownSinglet.valueGaugeWeight`, and pass to the dual and conjugate-dual coordinate
functionals with the expected signs.

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.basis
declarations.doc: A basis on the down singlets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def basis : Module.Basis (Fin 2 × Fin 3) ℂ DownSinglet

declarations.doc: The down-singlet space is finite-dimensional.
declarations.statement: instance : Module.Finite ℂ DownSinglet

declarations.doc: The down-singlet space is free.
declarations.statement: instance : Module.Free ℂ DownSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.basis_eq_mk
declarations.doc: The down-singlet basis vector as an explicit spinor–colour tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_eq_mk (k : Fin 2) (c : Fin 3) : basis (k, c) =
    ⟨Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ c⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the down-singlet basis. The colour index is inert and the spinor
index transforms by the entrywise conjugate matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_basis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup Λ (basis j) = ∑ β, star (Λ.1 β j.1) • basis (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The down-singlet coordinate functionals transform contragrediently, by the entrywise
conjugate of the inverse matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup.dual Λ (basis.dualBasis j) =
      ∑ β, star ((Λ⁻¹).1 j.1 β) • basis.dualBasis (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_conj_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the conjugate down-singlet basis. The coefficients are the
conjugates of those of the down-singlet action, that is, the matrix itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_apply_basis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup.conj Λ ((Basis.conj basis) j)
      = ∑ β, Λ.1 β j.1 • (Basis.conj basis) (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_conj_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc: The conjugate down-singlet coordinate functionals transform by the inverse matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup.conj.dual Λ ((Basis.conj basis).dualBasis j) =
      ∑ β, (Λ⁻¹).1 j.1 β • (Basis.conj basis).dualBasis (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_neg_one
declarations.doc:
The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the down-singlet space by `-1`. The value space carries a
single Weyl-spinor index, and `-1` is not the identity on a half-integer spin.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzGroup_neg_one : repLorentzGroup (-1) = -LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup_conj_neg_one
declarations.doc:
The centre acts on the conjugate down-singlet space by `-1` as well, conjugation not moving
a real sign.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_neg_one : repLorentzGroup.conj (-1) = -LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the down-singlet basis. The spinor index is inert and the colour index
transforms by the `SU(3)` matrix, scaled by the hypercharge factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply_basis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (basis j) =
      ∑ c, (star g.toU1.1 ^ 2 * g.toSU3.1 c j.2) • basis (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The down-singlet coordinate functionals carry the contragredient gauge action, by the
hypercharge and `SU(3)` factors of the inverse group element, transposed.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_dual_dualBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI.dual g (basis.dualBasis j) =
      ∑ c, (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 2 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2 c) • basis.dualBasis (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the conjugate down-singlet basis has the coefficients of the
down-singlet action, conjugated.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_conj_apply_basis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI.conj g ((Basis.conj basis) j) =
      ∑ c, star (star g.toU1.1 ^ 2 * g.toSU3.1 c j.2) • (Basis.conj basis) (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The conjugate down-singlet coordinate functionals carry the conjugate of the
contragredient gauge action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_dualBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g ((Basis.conj basis).dualBasis j) =
      ∑ c, star (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 2 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2 c) •
        (Basis.conj basis).dualBasis (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.valueGaugeWeight
declarations.doc: The gauge weight of the down-singlet basis, the colour weights and hypercharge `-2`.
declarations.statement: def valueGaugeWeight (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) : GaugeWeight

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_gaugeTorusGen_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge torus acts diagonally on the basis of `DownSinglet`, with the weights
`DownSinglet.valueGaugeWeight`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_gaugeTorusGen_basis (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (DownSinglet.basis j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (DownSinglet.valueGaugeWeight j) i) •
        DownSinglet.basis j

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual action of the gauge torus on the coordinate functionals of `DownSinglet` negates
the weights.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.dual (gaugeTorusGen i) (DownSinglet.basis.coord j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ (-(GaugeWeight.coord (DownSinglet.valueGaugeWeight j) i))) •
        DownSinglet.basis.coord j

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual of the conjugate action of the gauge torus on the coordinate functionals
of the conjugate of `DownSinglet`. The two negations cancel and the weights are those of
the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual (gaugeTorusGen i)
      (((Basis.conj DownSinglet.basis)).coord j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (DownSinglet.valueGaugeWeight j) i) •
        ((Basis.conj DownSinglet.basis)).coord j

modules.title: The infinitesimal gauge action on the down-type singlet
modules.doc:
The explicit `(3, 1)_{-2}` action of the gauge algebra on the down-type singlet, and its agreement
with the matter field.

## i. Overview

The infinitesimal `(3, 1)_{-2}` action of the gauge algebra on the down-type singlet, its
compatibility with the Lorentz action, and its identification with the action of the gauge
algebra of the matter field `DownSinglet.matterField`.

## ii. Key results

- `DownSinglet.colourEnd` : the endomorphism of the down singlet defined by a `3 × 3` complex
  matrix acting on the colour index, with the Weyl factor untouched.
- `DownSinglet.actionMatrix` : the matrix of the infinitesimal action of a gauge algebra
  element.
- `DownSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction` : the infinitesimal `(3, 1)_{-2}` action.
- `DownSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentzGroup` : the gauge action commutes with the
  Lorentz action.
- `DownSinglet.matterField_repAlgebra_gaugeAlgebraEquiv` : the action of the gauge algebra
  of the matter field is `DownSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of the gauge algebra
- B. The gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action
- C. The matter field

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The action of the gauge algebra

The infinitesimal `(3, 1)_{-2}` action of the gauge algebra on the down-type singlet:
the colour part of the algebra element acts on the colour index and the hypercharge
part scales, both through the physicists' factor of `i`, matching the group action
`(star u) ^ 2 • U₃` infinitesimally.
## B. The gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action
## C. The matter field

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.colourEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the down singlet defined by a `3 × 3` complex matrix acting on
the colour index, with the Weyl factor untouched.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colourEnd (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    DownSinglet →ₗ[ℂ] DownSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.colourEnd_apply_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_apply_mk (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) (v : DownSinglet) :
    colourEnd A v
      = valLinEquiv.symm
          (Module.End.lTensorAlgHom ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)) Fermion.RightHandedWeyl
            (Matrix.toLpLinAlgEquiv 2 A) (valLinEquiv v))

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.colourEnd_add
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_add (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    colourEnd (A + B) = colourEnd A + colourEnd B

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.colourEnd_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_smul (z : ℂ) (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    colourEnd (z • A) = z • colourEnd A

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.actionMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the infinitesimal `(3, 1)_{-2}` action of a gauge algebra element on
the colour index, `i` times the colour part shifted by `i` times `-2` the
hypercharge.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def actionMatrix (c : GaugeAlgebra) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal action of the gauge algebra on the down-type singlet, the
derivative of the `(3, 1)_{-2}` action of the gauge group, real-linear in the
algebra slot and complex-linear in the value slot.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeAlgebraAction :
    GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] DownSinglet →ₗ[ℂ] DownSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal gauge action on the down-type singlet acts on the colour factor, the
Lorentz action on the Weyl factor, so the two commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentzGroup (c : GaugeAlgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (v : DownSinglet) :
    DownSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction c (DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup Λ v) =
      DownSinglet.repLorentzGroup Λ (DownSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction c v)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.colourEnd_eq_valEnd
declarations.doc: The colour endomorphism of a matrix is the endomorphism of the matrix representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_eq_valEnd (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    colourEnd A = MatrixRep.valEnd tensorEquiv A

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.derivMat_gaugeRep_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc: The action matrix of the matrix representation on `gaugeAlgebraEquiv c` is `actionMatrix c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_gaugeRep_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    derivMat gaugeRep (gaugeAlgebraEquiv c) = actionMatrix c

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_repAlgebra_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The action of the gauge algebra of the matter field of the down-type singlet, on the
image of `gaugeAlgebraEquiv`, is `gaugeAlgebraAction`.
declarations.statement:
lemma matterField_repAlgebra_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    matterField.repAlgebra (gaugeAlgebraEquiv c) = gaugeAlgebraAction c

modules.title: The down-type singlet as a matter field
modules.doc:
The down-type singlet `(3, 1)_{-2}` as a matter field of the Standard Model global
gauge group.

## i. Overview

The target space `DownSinglet` is normed by the coordinates of its basis. A down-type singlet
is a right-handed Weyl spinor with a colour index, and the global gauge group acts on it by the
fundamental representation of `SU(3)` twisted by the power `-2` of the hypercharge phase. This
is the charge `-2` twist of the fundamental representation of the colour factor, which gives a
matter field of mass weight three. Its action of the global gauge group, on the image of
`StandardModel.gaugeGroupEquiv`, is the existing action
`StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI`.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField` : the down-type singlet as a matrix matter
  field of `StandardModel.globalGaugeGroup`.
- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_repAlgebra` : its action of the gauge algebra.
- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_rep_gaugeGroupEquiv` : its action of the gauge
  group is `StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI`.
- `StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_lorentzContinuous`,
  `StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_gaugeLorentzCommute` :
  its Lorentz action is continuous and commutes with its gauge action.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The normed structure
- B. The gauge representation
- C. The matter field

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The normed structure

The target space is normed by the largest modulus of its coordinates in its basis.
## B. The gauge representation
## C. The matter field

declarations.doc: The down singlets as a right-handed Weyl spinor with a colour index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tensorEquiv : DownSinglet ≃ₗ[ℂ] Fermion.RightHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] (Fin 3 → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.tensorEquiv_symm_tmul
declarations.doc: The inverse of the identification `tensorEquiv` on a pure tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorEquiv_symm_tmul (s : Fermion.RightHandedWeyl) (w : Fin 3 → ℂ) :

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.gaugeRep
declarations.doc:
The representation of the global gauge group on the colour index of the down-type
singlet, the fundamental representation of `SU(3)` twisted by the power `-2` of the
hypercharge.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeRep : globalGaugeGroup.group →ₜ* (Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ)ˣ

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField
declarations.doc:
The down-type singlet `(3, 1)_{-2}` as a matter field of the Standard Model
global gauge group, with its right-handed Lorentz action.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def matterField : globalGaugeGroup.MatterField

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_V
declarations.doc: The target space of the matter field is the down singlets.
declarations.statement: lemma matterField_V : matterField.V = DownSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_repAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The action of the gauge algebra of the matter field is the action matrix of its matrix
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma matterField_repAlgebra (c : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra) :
    matterField.repAlgebra c = MatrixRep.valEnd tensorEquiv (derivMat gaugeRep c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.matterField_repLorentz
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action of the matter field is that of the right-handed Weyl
spinor.
declarations.statement:
lemma matterField_repLorentz :
    matterField.repLorentz = MatrixRep.repLorentz tensorEquiv Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.rep
