declarations.doc:
The bracket on the gauge algebra, `I` times the matrix commutator on the `su(3)` and `su(2)`
factors and zero on the commutative `u(1)` factor. The factor of `I` is what makes the
bracket of two hermitian matrices hermitian again. It is also why the bracket is only
`ℝ`-bilinear, not `ℂ`-bilinear.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Bracket GaugeAlgebra GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.bracket_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toSU3Matrix (a b : GaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toSU3Matrix =
      Complex.I • (a.toSU3Matrix * b.toSU3Matrix - b.toSU3Matrix * a.toSU3Matrix)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.bracket_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toSU2Matrix (a b : GaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toSU2Matrix =
      Complex.I • (a.toSU2Matrix * b.toSU2Matrix - b.toSU2Matrix * a.toSU2Matrix)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.bracket_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toU1Value (a b : GaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toU1Value = 0

declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : LieRing GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap
declarations.doc:
The linear map by which one gauge group element acts on the gauge algebra in the
adjoint action. It is conjugation by the corresponding unitary on the `su(3)` and `su(2)`
factors, and the identity on the commutative `u(1)` factor.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjointMap (g : GaugeGroupI) : GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU3Matrix (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMap g a).toSU3Matrix = g.toSU3.1 * a.toSU3Matrix * star g.toSU3.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU2Matrix (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMap g a).toSU2Matrix = g.toSU2.1 * a.toSU2Matrix * star g.toSU2.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toU1Value (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMap g a).toU1Value = a.toU1Value

declarations.doc:

corresponding unitary on the `su(3)` and `su(2)` factors, and the trivial action on the

declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjoint : Representation ℝ GaugeGroupI GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjoint_toSU2Matrix

modules.title: The standard basis of the gauge algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The standard basis of the gauge algebra of the Standard Model, indexed by
`Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1`: the eight Gell-Mann matrices on the `su(3)` factor, the three
Pauli matrices on the `su(2)` factor, and `1` on the `u(1)` factor.

In this basis the adjoint action of the gauge group is the block-diagonal matrix
`adjointMatrix`, whose blocks are the trace pairings of the basis elements with their
conjugates; `adjoint_stdBasis` and `toMatrix_adjoint` identify its action with the
adjoint action.

## ii. Key results

- `adjointMatrix`
- `adjoint_stdBasis` : the adjoint action of the gauge group acts on the standard basis through
  `adjointMatrix`
- `toMatrix_adjoint` : the matrix of the adjoint action in the standard basis is `adjointMatrix`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Gell-Mann matrices
- B. Coordinates in the Gell-Mann and Pauli bases
- C. The Gell-Mann basis of the su(3) factor
- D. The Pauli basis of the su(2) factor
- E. The basis of the u(1) factor
- F. The standard basis of the gauge algebra
- G. The adjoint action in the standard basis
- H. Orthogonality of the adjoint matrix

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The Gell-Mann matrices

The Pauli matrices `σ1`, `σ2`, `σ3` embedded along the three coordinate planes of
`Fin 3`, together with the normalised traceless diagonal matrix.

## B. Coordinates in the Gell-Mann and Pauli bases

The coordinates of a traceless hermitian matrix in the Gell-Mann and Pauli bases, read
off from its entries; they coincide with the trace pairings
`2⁻¹ * (trace (T k * M)).re` with the basis matrices.
## C. The Gell-Mann basis of the su(3) factor
## D. The Pauli basis of the su(2) factor
## E. The basis of the u(1) factor
## F. The standard basis of the gauge algebra

## G. The adjoint action in the standard basis

In the standard basis the adjoint action of a gauge group element is the block-diagonal
matrix `adjointMatrix`: the `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks pair the basis elements with
their conjugates through the trace, and the `u(1)` entry is `1`.

## H. Orthogonality of the adjoint matrix

The adjoint action preserves the trace pairing of the standard basis, so `adjointMatrix`
is an orthogonal matrix. Multiplicativity turns the star of a group element into the
transpose of its matrix, and the two combine to the orthogonality relation.

declarations.doc: The Gell-Mann matrices are hermitian.

    star (gellMannMatrix k) = gellMannMatrix k

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix_trace
declarations.doc: The Gell-Mann matrices are traceless.

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_smul_gellMannMatrix
declarations.doc: A combination of the Gell-Mann matrices, entry by entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_smul_gellMannMatrix (g : Fin 8 → ℝ) :
    ∑ k, g k • gellMannMatrix k =
      !![((g 2 + (Real.sqrt 3)⁻¹ * g 7 : ℝ) : ℂ),
          ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((g 3 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 4 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I;
        ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((-g 2 + (Real.sqrt 3)⁻¹ * g 7 : ℝ) : ℂ),
          ((g 5 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 6 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I;
        ((g 3 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 4 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((g 5 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 6 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((-2 * (Real.sqrt 3)⁻¹ * g 7 : ℝ) : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_smul_pauliMatrix_inr
declarations.doc: A combination of the three Pauli matrices `σ1`, `σ2`, `σ3`, entry by entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_smul_pauliMatrix_inr (g : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    ∑ i, g i • pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) =
      !![((g 2 : ℝ) : ℂ), ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I;
        ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I, ((-g 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.pauliMatrix_inr_star

    star (pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i)) = pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.entry_symm_of_star_eq
declarations.doc: The entries of a hermitian matrix are conjugate-symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_symm_of_star_eq {n : ℕ} {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (hself : star M = M)
    (i j : Fin n) : M j i = (starRingEnd ℂ) (M i j)

declarations.name: StandardModel.diag_re_of_star_eq
declarations.doc: The diagonal entries of a hermitian matrix are real.
declarations.statement:
lemma diag_re_of_star_eq {n : ℕ} {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (hself : star M = M)
    (i : Fin n) : M i i = ((M i i).re : ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of a gauge group element in the standard basis:
block diagonal, with the `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks the trace pairings
`2⁻¹ * (trace (T a * g T b g⁻¹)).re` of the basis elements with the conjugated basis
elements, `1` on the `u(1)` entry, and `0` between different factors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointMatrix (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    Matrix (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inl_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inl_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (a b : Fin 8) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl a) (Sum.inl b)
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (gellMannMatrix a *
          (g.toSU3.1 * gellMannMatrix b * star g.toSU3.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inl_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inl_inr (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : Fin 8) (x : Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl a) (Sum.inr x) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (x : Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) (b : Fin 8) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr x) (Sum.inl b) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (i j : Fin 3) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl i)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl j))
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) *
          (g.toSU2.1 * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) * star g.toSU2.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inr (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) (u : Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl i)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inr u)) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (u : Fin 1) (j : Fin 3) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inr u)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl j)) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inr (g : GaugeGroupI) (u v : Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inr u)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inr v)) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjoint_stdBasis
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of the gauge group acts on the standard basis through
`adjointMatrix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_stdBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (b : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    adjoint g (stdBasis b) = ∑ a, adjointMatrix g a b • stdBasis a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.toMatrix_adjoint
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action in the standard basis is `adjointMatrix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_adjoint (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix stdBasis stdBasis (adjoint g) = adjointMatrix g

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_mulVec_repr
declarations.doc:
The action of `adjointMatrix` on coordinates in the standard basis corresponds to
the adjoint action of the gauge group on the gauge algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_mulVec_repr (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMatrix g).mulVec (stdBasis.repr a) = ⇑(stdBasis.repr (adjoint g a))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjoint_dualMap_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual adjoint action on the dual standard basis: the coordinate functions
transform through the rows of `adjointMatrix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_dualMap_coord (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    (adjoint g).dualMap (stdBasis.coord a)
      = ∑ b, adjointMatrix g a b • stdBasis.coord b

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_mul
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action turns a product in the gauge group into the
product of the corresponding matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_mul (g h : GaugeGroupI) :
    GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix (g * h)
      = GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g * GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix h

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_one
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action of the identity is the identity matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma adjointMatrix_one : GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix (1 : GaugeGroupI) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.gaugeGroup_mul_star_self
declarations.doc: The star of a gauge group element is its inverse.
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeGroup_mul_star_self (g : GaugeGroupI) : g * star g = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_star
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of the star of a gauge group element is the
transpose of the matrix of the adjoint action, since the trace pairing is symmetric
under moving the conjugation from one argument to the other.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_star (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix (star g) = (GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g)ᵀ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_mul_transpose
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action is orthogonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_mul_transpose (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g * (GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g)ᵀ = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.sum_adjointMatrix_inl_row_mul
declarations.doc:
The rows of the `su(3)` block of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal. The matrix is
block diagonal, so orthogonality of the whole matrix restricts to each block.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_adjointMatrix_inl_row_mul (g : GaugeGroupI) (c d : Fin 8) :
    ∑ a : Fin 8, adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl c) (Sum.inl a) *
      adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl d) (Sum.inl a) = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.sum_adjointMatrix_inr_inl_row_mul
declarations.doc: The rows of the `su(2)` block of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_adjointMatrix_inr_inl_row_mul (g : GaugeGroupI) (c d : Fin 3) :
    ∑ a : Fin 3, adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl c)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl a)) *
      adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl d)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl a))
      = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inv_apply
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of the inverse of a gauge group element is the
transpose of the matrix of the adjoint action.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inv_apply (g : GaugeGroupI) (a b : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g⁻¹ a b = adjointMatrix g b a

modules.title: The root decomposition of the gauge algebra
modules.doc:
The root and Cartan directions of the gauge algebra, read as a gauge weight decomposition.

## i. Overview

The gauge torus acts on the gauge algebra by conjugation with a diagonal matrix, so it
scales the matrix entry `(j, k)` of the `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks by `d j * star (d k)`.
Off the diagonal this makes the real and imaginary parts of an entry a rotating pair. These
are the root directions, recorded by `rootIdx`, `rootEntry` and `rootWeight`. The diagonal
directions and the `u(1)` generator are fixed, and are recorded by `cartanIdx`, which is
assembled from the Cartan indices `su3CartanId` and `su2CartanId` of the individual factors.

This is the adjoint analogue of the weights carried by the matter representations, and
section E makes that a theorem. A gauge weight is a character of the torus, so the real Lie
algebra carries no gauge weight decomposition of its own. But for any complex algebra receiving
the dual adjoint action, `adjointDecomposition` decomposes the span of the resulting symbols,
and its pieces are a single root line at each of the eight nonzero weights and the span of the
four Cartan symbols at weight zero. In this sense the root decomposition and the gauge weight
decomposition of the adjoint are the same thing.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootIdx` : the four root directions of the adjoint.
- `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootWeight` : the gauge weight of each root direction.
- `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootEntry` : the matrix entry scaled by the torus along each root
  direction.
- `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.cartanIdx` : the four weight-zero directions, the two `su(3)`
  Cartan generators, the `su(2)` Cartan generator and the `u(1)` generator.
- `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition` : the root decomposition read as a gauge
  weight decomposition of the span of the symbols of a coadjoint map.
- `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_supp`,
  `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_rootWeight`,
  `StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_zero` : its nine weights, a single root
  line at each nonzero weight and the Cartan symbols at weight zero.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The coordinates of the standard basis
- B. The torus acts by conjugation with a diagonal matrix
- C. An entrywise scaling rotates the real pair of coordinate functionals
- D. The root and Cartan directions of the adjoint
- E. The root decomposition as a gauge weight decomposition

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The coordinates of the standard basis

The coordinates of an element of the gauge algebra in `stdBasis` are its Gell-Mann and Pauli
coefficients and the real part of its `u(1)` component.

## B. The torus acts by conjugation with a diagonal matrix

The inverses of the four torus generators have diagonal `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` factors, so their
adjoint action scales each matrix entry by a phase.
## C. An entrywise scaling rotates the real pair of coordinate functionals

## D. The root and Cartan directions of the adjoint

The `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks each contribute root directions, pairs of standard basis
indices whose coordinate functionals are the real part and minus the imaginary part of one
matrix entry. They also contribute Cartan directions, on which the torus acts trivially, and
the `u(1)` generator is fixed as well.

The Cartan directions are named one factor at a time first, by `su3CartanId` in the
Gell-Mann indices and `su2CartanId` in the Pauli indices, and `cartanIdx` assembles those
with the `u(1)` generator into the four weight-zero directions of the whole algebra. The
factorwise names are reducible, so they behave exactly like the index literals they name.

## E. The root decomposition as a gauge weight decomposition

A gauge weight is a character of the torus, so the vectors carrying one are complex,
whereas the gauge algebra is a real Lie algebra and `GaugeWeightDecomposition` asks for a
complex algebra. The relation is therefore not a statement about `GaugeAlgebra`, which
carries no gauge weight decomposition at all, but about any complex algebra receiving the
dual adjoint action. That is a real-linear map `F` out of `Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra`
intertwining the gauge action with the coadjoint one, which is how the field strength of
the gauge sector meets the adjoint.

For such an `F` the root data of section D is exactly a gauge weight decomposition of the
span of the symbols. Each root contributes the two combinations `F φ₁ ± i F φ₂` of its
paired coordinate symbols, of weights `± rootWeight r`, and each Cartan direction
contributes its symbol, of weight zero. `exists_rootIdx_or_cartanIdx` says these twelve
vectors are enough, and `adjointDecomposition` joins their lines one weight at a time.

The pieces are the identification itself. `adjointDecomposition_piece_rootWeight` and
`adjointDecomposition_piece_neg_rootWeight` give a single root line at each of the eight
nonzero weights, and `adjointDecomposition_piece_zero` gives the span of the four Cartan
symbols at weight zero. The root directions are the nonzero-weight pieces and the Cartan
directions are the zero-weight piece.

An element of the gauge algebra is the sum of the standard basis weighted by its
coordinates.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis_coord_apply
declarations.doc:
The coordinate functionals of `stdBasis` read off a gauge-algebra element's matrix
entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma stdBasis_coord_apply (y : GaugeAlgebra) (a : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    stdBasis.coord a y = stdCoeff y a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.toSU3_inv_gaugeTorusGen
declarations.doc: The `SU(3)` factor of the inverse of a torus generator is diagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU3_inv_gaugeTorusGen (i : Fin 4) :
    ((GaugeGroupI.toSU3 (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal (torusSU3Diag i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.toSU2_inv_gaugeTorusGen
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` factor of the inverse of a torus generator is diagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU2_inv_gaugeTorusGen (i : Fin 4) :
    ((GaugeGroupI.toSU2 (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal (torusSU2Diag i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU3Matrix_apply_diagonal
declarations.doc:
Conjugation by a diagonal colour factor `d` scales the entry `(j, k)` of the `su(3)`
component by `d j * star (d k)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU3Matrix_apply_diagonal {g : GaugeGroupI} {d : Fin 3 → ℂ}
    (hg : ((GaugeGroupI.toSU3 g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal d)
    (x : GaugeAlgebra) (j k : Fin 3) :
    (adjointMap g x).toSU3Matrix j k = d j * star (d k) * x.toSU3Matrix j k

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU2Matrix_apply_diagonal
declarations.doc:
Conjugation by a diagonal isospin factor `d` scales the entry `(j, k)` of the `su(2)`
component by `d j * star (d k)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU2Matrix_apply_diagonal {g : GaugeGroupI} {d : Fin 2 → ℂ}
    (hg : ((GaugeGroupI.toSU2 g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal d)
    (x : GaugeAlgebra) (j k : Fin 2) :
    (adjointMap g x).toSU2Matrix j k = d j * star (d k) * x.toSU2Matrix j k

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.torusSU3Diag_mul_star
declarations.doc: The diagonal entries of the `SU(3)` factors of the torus generators are phases.
declarations.statement:
lemma torusSU3Diag_mul_star (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 3) :
    torusSU3Diag i j * star (torusSU3Diag i j) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.torusSU2Diag_mul_star
declarations.doc: The diagonal entries of the `SU(2)` factors of the torus generators are phases.
declarations.statement:
lemma torusSU2Diag_mul_star (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2) :
    torusSU2Diag i j * star (torusSU2Diag i j) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.dualMap_pair_of_entry
declarations.doc:
If an element scales a complex coordinate `e` by `star z`, its dual action rotates the
pair of real functionals `re e` and `-im e` by `z`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootIdx
declarations.doc: The four root directions of the adjoint.
declarations.statement: def rootIdx : Fin 4 → (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) × (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootWeight
declarations.doc: The gauge weight of each root direction.
declarations.statement: def rootWeight : Fin 4 → GaugeWeight

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootEntry
declarations.doc: The matrix entry scaled by the torus along each root direction.
declarations.statement: def rootEntry : Fin 4 → GaugeAlgebra → ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.su3CartanId
declarations.doc: The Gell-Mann indices of the two Cartan directions of `su(3)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev su3CartanId : Fin 2 → Fin 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.su2CartanId
declarations.doc: The Pauli index of the Cartan direction of `su(2)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev su2CartanId : Fin 3

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.cartanIdx
declarations.doc:
The four weight-zero directions, the two `su(3)` Cartan generators, the `su(2)`
Cartan generator and the `u(1)` generator.
declarations.statement: def cartanIdx : Fin 4 → (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.coord_rootIdx_fst
declarations.doc: The first coordinate of a root pair is the real part of the root entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_rootIdx_fst (r : Fin 4) (x : GaugeAlgebra) :
    stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).1 x = (rootEntry r x).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.coord_rootIdx_snd
declarations.doc: The second coordinate of a root pair is minus the imaginary part of the root entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_rootIdx_snd (r : Fin 4) (x : GaugeAlgebra) :
    stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).2 x = -(rootEntry r x).im

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootEntry_adjointMap
declarations.doc:
The inverse of a torus generator scales the root entry by the conjugate of the character
of the root weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma rootEntry_adjointMap (r : Fin 4) (i : Fin 4) (x : GaugeAlgebra) :
    rootEntry r (adjointMap (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹ x)
      = star ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (rootWeight r) i) * rootEntry r x

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.dualMap_coord_cartanIdx
declarations.doc: The torus fixes the coordinate functional of each Cartan direction.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualMap_coord_cartanIdx (c : Fin 4) (i : Fin 4) :
    (adjointMap (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹).dualMap (stdBasis.coord (cartanIdx c))
      = stdBasis.coord (cartanIdx c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.IsCoadjointSymbol
declarations.doc:
A coadjoint symbol map, a real-linear map from the dual of the gauge algebra into a
complex algebra which intertwines the gauge action with the dual adjoint action. The
field strength of the gauge sector is one such map.
declarations.statement:
def IsCoadjointSymbol (rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B)
    (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) : Prop

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.AdjIdx
declarations.doc:
The index type of the adjoint weight vectors, four positive roots, four negative
roots and four Cartan directions.
declarations.statement: abbrev AdjIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjWeight
declarations.doc: The gauge weight carried by each adjoint weight vector.
declarations.statement: def adjWeight : AdjIdx → GaugeWeight

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjVec
declarations.doc:
The weight vectors of the adjoint in the image of a coadjoint symbol map. For each root
they are the two combinations of its paired coordinate symbols, and for each Cartan
direction the symbol itself.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjVec (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) : AdjIdx → B

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.exists_rootIdx_or_cartanIdx
declarations.doc:
The root and Cartan directions exhaust the standard basis. Every standard index is
one of the two members of a root pair, or a Cartan index.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_rootIdx_or_cartanIdx (a : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    (∃ r : Fin 4, a = (rootIdx r).1) ∨ (∃ r : Fin 4, a = (rootIdx r).2)
      ∨ ∃ c : Fin 4, a = cartanIdx c

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_pair_add
declarations.doc: The positive combination of a rotating pair of symbols is scaled by the rotation.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_pair_add (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (φ₁ φ₂ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (z : ℂ)
    (h1 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₁ = z.re • φ₁ - z.im • φ₂)
    (h2 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₂ = z.im • φ₁ + z.re • φ₂) :
    rep g (F φ₁ + Complex.I • F φ₂) = z • (F φ₁ + Complex.I • F φ₂)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_pair_sub
declarations.doc:
The negative combination of a rotating pair of symbols is scaled by the conjugate
rotation.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_pair_sub (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (φ₁ φ₂ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (z : ℂ)
    (h1 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₁ = z.re • φ₁ - z.im • φ₂)
    (h2 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₂ = z.im • φ₁ + z.re • φ₂) :
    rep g (F φ₁ - Complex.I • F φ₂)
      = (starRingEnd ℂ z) • (F φ₁ - Complex.I • F φ₂)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_fixed
declarations.doc: A symbol at a fixed coordinate functional is itself fixed.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_fixed (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (h1 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ = φ) :
    rep g (F φ) = F φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_adjVec
declarations.doc:
Each adjoint weight vector is a simultaneous eigenvector of the four torus
generators, at the character of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_adjVec (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (k : AdjIdx) (i : Fin 4) :
    rep (gaugeTorusGen i) (adjVec F k)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (adjWeight k) i) • adjVec F k

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.symbol_rootIdx_fst
declarations.doc: The first symbol of a root pair, recovered from the two weight vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_rootIdx_fst (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (r : Fin 4) :
    F (stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).1)
      = (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (adjVec F (Sum.inl r) + adjVec F (Sum.inr (Sum.inl r)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.symbol_rootIdx_snd
declarations.doc: The second symbol of a root pair, recovered from the two weight vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_rootIdx_snd (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (r : Fin 4) :
    F (stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).2)
      = (-(Complex.I / 2)) • (adjVec F (Sum.inl r) - adjVec F (Sum.inr (Sum.inl r)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.symbol_mem_iSup
declarations.doc: Every standard coordinate symbol lies in the join of the twelve weight lines.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.span_range_eq_iSup
declarations.doc: The span of the symbols is the join of the twelve weight lines.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_range_eq_iSup (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range F) = ⨆ k : AdjIdx, Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F k}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition
declarations.doc:
The root decomposition read as a gauge weight decomposition. The span of the symbols
of a coadjoint map is joined out of the twelve root and Cartan lines.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointDecomposition (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range F))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_supp
declarations.doc:
The gauge weights of the adjoint are the six `su(3)` roots, the two `su(2)` roots and
the zero weight of the Cartan and `u(1)` directions. Every one of them has vanishing
hypercharge.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_supp (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).supp
      = {((2, -1, 0, 0) : GaugeWeight), (1, 1, 0, 0), (-1, 2, 0, 0), (0, 0, 2, 0),
        (-2, 1, 0, 0), (-1, -1, 0, 0), (1, -2, 0, 0), (0, 0, -2, 0), (0, 0, 0, 0)}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece
declarations.doc:
The weight-`w` piece of the decomposition is the join of the weight lines whose weight
is `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F)
    (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece w
      = ⨆ k : AdjIdx, if w = adjWeight k then Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F k} else ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_rootWeight
declarations.doc: The piece at a root weight is the line of that root alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece_rootWeight (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (r : Fin 4) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece (rootWeight r)
      = Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F (Sum.inl r)}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_neg_rootWeight
declarations.doc: The piece at the opposite of a root weight is the line of the opposite root.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece_neg_rootWeight (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (r : Fin 4) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece (-(rootWeight r))
      = Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F (Sum.inr (Sum.inl r))}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece is the span of the four Cartan symbols, of the two `su(3)` Cartan
generators, the `su(2)` Cartan generator and the `u(1)` generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece_zero (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece 0
      = ⨆ c : Fin 4, Submodule.span ℂ {F (stdBasis.coord (cartanIdx c))}

modules.title: The adjoint matrices of `SU(2)` and `SU(3)`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`su2AdjointMatrix U` and `su3AdjointMatrix U` are the real matrices of `X ↦ U X U⁻¹` on
`su(2)` and `su(3)` in the Pauli and Gell-Mann bases, read off with the trace pairing
`(X, Y) ↦ ½ tr (X Y)`. They are the `su(2)` and `su(3)` blocks of `GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix`,
which gives their orthonormal rows and their transposition at `U⁻¹`.

## ii. Key results

- `su2AdjointMatrix` : the adjoint matrix of an element of `SU(2)`: the trace pairing of the Pauli
  basis of `su(2)` with the Pauli basis conjugated by that element
- `su2AdjointMatrix_apply` : the entries of the adjoint matrix
- `sum_su2AdjointMatrix_row_mul` : the rows of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal
- `su2AdjointMatrix_inv` : the adjoint matrix of the inverse is the transpose

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint matrix of `SU(2)`
- B. The adjoint matrix of `SU(3)`

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The adjoint matrix of `SU(2)`
## B. The adjoint matrix of `SU(3)`

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2AdjointMatrix
declarations.doc:
The adjoint matrix of an element of `SU(2)`: the trace pairing of the Pauli basis of
`su(2)` with the Pauli basis conjugated by that element.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def su2AdjointMatrix (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2AdjointMatrix_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of the adjoint matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2AdjointMatrix_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (i j : Fin 3) :
    su2AdjointMatrix U i j
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) *
          (U.1 * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) * star U.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_su2AdjointMatrix_row_mul
declarations.doc: The rows of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_su2AdjointMatrix_row_mul (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (c d : Fin 3) :
    ∑ a : Fin 3, su2AdjointMatrix U c a * su2AdjointMatrix U d a
      = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2AdjointMatrix_inv
declarations.doc: The adjoint matrix of the inverse is the transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2AdjointMatrix_inv (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (a b : Fin 3) :
    su2AdjointMatrix U⁻¹ a b = su2AdjointMatrix U b a

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix
declarations.doc:
The adjoint matrix of `U ∈ SU(3)`: the trace pairing of the Gell-Mann basis with the
Gell-Mann basis conjugated by `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def su3AdjointMatrix (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    Matrix (Fin 8) (Fin 8) ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma su3AdjointMatrix_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (i j : Fin 8) :
    su3AdjointMatrix U i j
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (gellMannMatrix i * (U.1 * gellMannMatrix j * star U.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_su3AdjointMatrix_row_mul
declarations.doc: The rows of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_su3AdjointMatrix_row_mul (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c d : Fin 8) :
    ∑ a : Fin 8, su3AdjointMatrix U c a * su3AdjointMatrix U d a
      = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix_inv
declarations.doc: The adjoint matrix of the inverse is the transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3AdjointMatrix_inv (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (a b : Fin 8) :
    su3AdjointMatrix U⁻¹ a b = su3AdjointMatrix U b a

modules.title: A cube root of unity and the factors of a gauge transformation
modules.doc:
The root of unity `ω = exp (2 π i / 3)`, and the inverses and factors of gauge transformations.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeGroup.Basic` carries the gauge group `GaugeGroupI` of
the Standard Model and its discrete quotients. One scalar recurs throughout the structure of its
non-abelian factors, the primitive cube root of unity `ω = exp (2 π i / 3)`. The element
`ω • 1` generates the centre of `SU(3)`, the cyclic colour permutation has eigenvalues the
powers of `ω`, and `diag(ω, ω²)` lies in `SU(2)`. Collected here are the facts about `ω` those
uses need. It is a primitive cube root of unity, it cubes to one, it is nonzero and of modulus
one, and its powers only see the exponent modulo three.

The colour, isospin and hypercharge laws each constrain one factor of a gauge transformation
`(U, V, t)`. The inverse of a unitary matrix is its conjugate transpose, so the entries of the
inverse of an element of `SU(3)` or `SU(2)` are the conjugated transposed entries, and the
inverse of a unitary scalar is its conjugate. The inverse of a transformation acting in one
factor alone acts in that factor alone, by the inverse. Every gauge transformation is the
product of its three factors, so an element fixed by each factor separately is gauge invariant.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity` : the primitive cube root of unity `ω = exp (2 π i / 3)`.
- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_isPrimitiveRoot` : it is a primitive cube root of unity.
- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_pow_three`, `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_pow_mod` : it cubes
  to one, so its powers only see the exponent modulo three.
- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_ne_zero`, `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_mul_star` : it is
  nonzero and of modulus one.
- `StandardModel.su3_inv_apply`, `StandardModel.su2_inv_apply` : the entries of an inverse in
  `SU(3)` or `SU(2)` are the conjugated transposed entries.
- `StandardModel.inv_su3Elt`, `StandardModel.inv_su2Elt` : the inverse of a colour or isospin
  transformation is the transformation of the inverse.
- `StandardModel.toSU3_su3Elt` and its eight companions : the three factors of a colour,
  isospin or hypercharge transformation.
- `StandardModel.forall_repGauge_eq_self` : an element fixed by each of the three factors of the
  gauge group is gauge invariant.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. A primitive cube root of unity
- B. Inverses and factors of gauge transformations

## iv. References

The gauge group and its quotients are in `Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeGroup.Basic`.

sections.text:
## A. A primitive cube root of unity

`ω = exp (2 π i / 3)` appears in both non-abelian factors: `ω • 1` generates the centre of
`SU(3)`, the cyclic colour permutation has eigenvalues the powers of `ω`, and `diag(ω, ω²)`
lies in `SU(2)`.

## B. Inverses and factors of gauge transformations

The inverse of a unitary matrix is its conjugate transpose. This section records what that says
for the entries of inverses in `SU(3)` and `SU(2)`, for unitary scalars, and for the colour and
isospin transformations `(U, 1, 1)` and `(1, V, 1)`, and the colour, isospin and hypercharge
factors of `(U, 1, 1)`, `(1, V, 1)` and `(1, 1, t)`. A gauge transformation `(U, V, t)` is the
product of these three, which turns three separate invariances into gauge invariance.

declarations.name: StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity
declarations.doc: The primitive cube root of unity `ω = exp (2 π i / 3)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def cubeRootOfUnity : ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_isPrimitiveRoot
declarations.doc: `ω` is a primitive cube root of unity.
declarations.statement: lemma cubeRootOfUnity_isPrimitiveRoot : IsPrimitiveRoot cubeRootOfUnity 3

declarations.name: StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_pow_three
declarations.doc: `ω` cubes to one.
declarations.statement: lemma cubeRootOfUnity_pow_three : cubeRootOfUnity ^ 3 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_ne_zero
declarations.doc: `ω` is nonzero, being a value of the complex exponential.
declarations.statement: lemma cubeRootOfUnity_ne_zero : cubeRootOfUnity ≠ 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_pow_mod
declarations.doc: Powers of `ω` only see the exponent modulo three.
declarations.statement:
lemma cubeRootOfUnity_pow_mod (m : ℕ) :
    cubeRootOfUnity ^ (m % 3) = cubeRootOfUnity ^ m

declarations.name: StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_mul_star
declarations.doc: `ω` has modulus one.
declarations.statement: lemma cubeRootOfUnity_mul_star : cubeRootOfUnity * star cubeRootOfUnity = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3_inv_apply
declarations.doc:
The entries of the inverse of an `SU(3)` element are the conjugated transposed
entries, the inverse of a unitary matrix being its conjugate transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3_inv_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (a b : Fin 3) :
    (U⁻¹).1 a b = conj (U.1 b a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2_inv_apply
declarations.doc:
The entries of the inverse of an `SU(2)` element are the conjugated transposed
entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2_inv_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (a b : Fin 2) :
    (U⁻¹).1 a b = conj (U.1 b a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.unitary_inv_coe
declarations.doc: The inverse of a unitary scalar is its conjugate.
declarations.statement: lemma unitary_inv_coe (t : unitary ℂ) : ((t⁻¹ : unitary ℂ) : ℂ) = star (t : ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.inv_su3Elt
declarations.doc:
The inverse of a colour gauge transformation is the colour transformation of the
inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_su3Elt (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI)⁻¹ = ((U⁻¹, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI)

declarations.name: StandardModel.inv_su2Elt
declarations.doc:
The inverse of an isospin gauge transformation is the isospin transformation of the
inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_su2Elt (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI)⁻¹ = ((1, V⁻¹, 1) : GaugeGroupI)

declarations.name: StandardModel.toSU3_su3Elt
declarations.doc: The colour factor of a colour gauge transformation.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU3_su3Elt (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    GaugeGroupI.toSU3 ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) = U

declarations.name: StandardModel.toSU2_su3Elt
declarations.doc: The isospin factor of a colour gauge transformation is trivial.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU2_su3Elt (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    GaugeGroupI.toSU2 ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.toU1_su3Elt
declarations.doc: The hypercharge factor of a colour gauge transformation is trivial.
declarations.statement:
lemma toU1_su3Elt (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    GaugeGroupI.toU1 ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.toSU3_su2Elt
declarations.doc: The colour factor of an isospin gauge transformation is trivial.
