A gauge transformation is the product of its colour, isospin and hypercharge parts, so
an element fixed by each of the three factors separately is gauge invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma forall_repGauge_eq_self {B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B] [Module ℂ B]
    {rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B} {x : B}
    (h3 : ∀ U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ, rep (U, 1, 1) x = x)
    (h2 : ∀ V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ, rep (1, V, 1) x = x)
    (h1 : ∀ t : unitary ℂ, rep (1, 1, t) x = x) (g : GaugeGroupI) : rep g x = x

modules.title: Gauge weight decompositions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The operators that may appear in a Standard Model Lagrangian are those the gauge group leaves
fixed, and finding them means searching a large space of composite operators.

The maximal torus of the gauge group is four-dimensional, and a **gauge weight** is the
quadruple of charges

  `(colour₁, colour₂, isospin, hypercharge) : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ × ℤ`,

recording how a vector scales under four chosen elements of it. Two count colour, one counts
weak isospin normalized as `2T₃`, and one counts hypercharge normalized as `6Y`. A **gauge
weight decomposition** of a submodule `V` presents it as a finitely supported family of
subspaces on each of which those four elements act by one such character.

Carrying all four charges at once costs nothing, since the four elements commute. They lie in
different factors of the product group, and the two colour elements are both diagonal, so the
four gradings are simultaneously realizable. An invariant operator is fixed by the whole gauge
group, so in particular by these four elements, so it carries zero weight and the search can
be confined to the zero-weight piece.

In the adjoint representation this grading is the root decomposition of the gauge algebra.
That identification cannot be made here, since the file recording the root data imports
this one; it is `GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition` in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.RootDecomposition`.

## ii. Key results

- `gaugeTorusGen` : the four commuting torus generators.
- `GaugeWeight` : the quadruple of charges measured against them.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition` : a finitely supported family of pure-weight subspaces with
  supremum `V`.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup` : decompositions combine one weight at a time along
  `V ⊔ V'`.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul` : weights add under multiplication, decomposing `V * V'`.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_eq_inf` : the pieces are cut out of `V` by the torus alone.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_zero_of_invariant` : a gauge-invariant element lies in the
  zero-weight piece.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero` : modulo a torus-stable
  submodule `S`, an element fixed by the four torus generators lies in the zero-weight
  piece; `mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant` is the unfolded form.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The scalar `exp i` and the torus generators
- B. The four torus generators and gauge weights
- C. Gauge weight decompositions
- D. Powers of `expI` under conjugation
- E. The torus weights of the fundamental representations
- F. The torus action on dual and conjugate bases
- G. Joins
- H. Products
- I. Invariants

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The scalar `exp i` and the torus generators

Every charge here is measured by one scalar. The unit complex number `exp i` has infinite
order, since `π` is irrational, so its integer powers are pairwise distinct and a single
element of the torus already separates all the weights in a given direction.

The torus generators are built by placing `exp i` and its inverse on a diagonal. The maximal
torus of `SU(3)` is two-dimensional, so colour is a two-component charge and needs the two
elements `diag (exp i, exp (-i), 1)` and `diag (1, exp i, exp (-i))`. Weak isospin needs one,
`diag (exp i, exp (-i))`. Each lies in its special unitary group because the diagonal entries
have modulus one and multiply to one. Hypercharge needs no matrix, since its factor of the
gauge group is already the unit circle.

The generators are elements of the group, and the purity of a weight space is recorded by a
character equation `rep g x = c • x`.

## B. The four torus generators and gauge weights

Weights are measured against four chosen elements of the maximal torus, one element per
direction, collected in `gaugeTorusGen`. Four suffice because of the separation in section A.

Both abelian charges are normalized to integers. Weak isospin is measured as `2T₃`, so the two
components of a doublet carry weights `+1` and `-1`, and hypercharge as `6Y`, the smallest
rescaling under which every Standard Model hypercharge is an integer, the quark doublet at `Y = 1/6`
becoming `6Y = 1`. Integrality is what allows every eigenvalue here to be an integer power
`(exp i) ^ k` of one scalar.

`GaugeWeight.coord` reads a weight at a given generator. It is additive, which is why charges
add when operators are multiplied, and injective, so a weight can be recovered from the four
characters by which the torus acts.

## C. Gauge weight decompositions

A gauge weight decomposition is the weight-space decomposition of a representation, with two
differences. It is recorded rather than derived, since the submodules of interest are spans of
explicitly given operators whose charges are read off directly, and it is required only to
cover `V`. Independence of the pieces is not part of the data, because it is automatic, as
section F shows.

Multiplicativity of the representation is named by `IsMulRep` and stored in the `rep_mul`
field, so that a decomposition of a product can be assembled from decompositions of the factors
with no further input. `copy` moves a decomposition across an equality of submodules, needed
because a submodule arising in practice is usually only propositionally the one for which a
decomposition was recorded.
## D. Powers of `expI` under conjugation

## E. The torus weights of the fundamental representations

The colour and isospin weights of the fundamental representations of `SU(3)` and
`SU(2)` against the torus generators.  They are the building blocks of the gauge
weights of the matter representations.

## F. The torus action on dual and conjugate bases

If the torus acts diagonally on a basis then it acts diagonally on the dual basis with
the negated weights, and on the conjugate basis with the negated weights as well — so
the conjugate-dual action carries the original weights back.

## G. Joins

If `V` and `V'` are decomposed then so is their join `V ⊔ V'`, one weight at a time. Its
weight-`w` piece is the join of the two weight-`w` pieces, and its support is the union of the
supports. A vector of the join need not have definite charge, but it is a sum of vectors that
do, which is all a decomposition claims.

The binary case `sup`, the empty case `bot`, a finite indexed family `iSup` and a join over a
proposition `iSupProp` are all the same construction. Multiplicativity of `rep` is recovered
from a summand where there is one and supplied as an argument where there is not, since `bot`
decomposes the zero submodule and the indexed forms may range over an empty family.

## H. Products

Charges add when operators are multiplied, and this section is where we prove this fact.
If the torus acts on `x` by the character of `w₁` and on `y` by the character of `w₂` then,
because `rep` respects multiplication, it acts on `x * y` by the product of the two characters,
which additivity of `GaugeWeight.coord` identifies with the character of `w₁ + w₂`. So the
weight-`w` piece of `V * V'` is spanned by products of pieces whose weights sum to `w`, and the
support of a product is the sumset of the supports.

The defining formula `mul_piece` joins over all pairs of weights in `ℤ⁴ × ℤ⁴`. Only finitely
many weights occur, so one of the two can always be eliminated against a support, and
`mul_piece_eq_sub` and `mul_piece_eq_sub'` do this against the left and the right factor. The
resulting finite joins are what make the weight pieces of a product computable.

## I. Invariants

A gauge-invariant element is fixed by the torus in particular, so it ought to have zero weight.
Making that an argument requires knowing the pieces are independent. Along one generator this
is immediate, since the pieces sit in eigenspaces of a single operator at the eigenvalues
`(exp i) ^ k`, pairwise distinct because `exp i` is not a root of unity, and eigenspaces at
distinct eigenvalues meet trivially. At rank four no single generator separates the weights, so
the argument is made one generator at a time.

What this yields is stronger than the statement about invariants. `piece_eq_inf` identifies the
weight-`w` piece with the intersection of `V` and the joint eigenspace of the four generators,
so the pieces depend only on `V` and the representation.

Zero weight is necessary but not sufficient for invariance. The torus is abelian and sees only
characters, so it cannot distinguish a true singlet from the neutral component of a higher
multiplet. Both `H†H` and `H†σ³H` carry zero weight, and only the first is gauge invariant. So
what passes `mem_zero_of_invariant` must still be checked against the non-abelian part of the
group; no grading closes that gap, since a grading sees only the abelian subgroup generated by
the elements it uses. The `Invariants` files do that check representation by representation.

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI
declarations.doc: The unitary scalar `exp i`, a point of the unit circle of infinite order.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def expI : unitary ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI_zpow_injective
declarations.doc: The powers of `exp i` are pairwise distinct, by the irrationality of `π`.
declarations.statement: lemma expI_zpow_injective : Function.Injective fun n : ℤ => ((expI : ℂ) ^ n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI_ne_zero
declarations.doc: `exp i` is nonzero.
declarations.statement: lemma expI_ne_zero : ((expI : ℂ)) ≠ 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI_inv_eq_star
declarations.doc: The inverse of `exp i` is its star.
declarations.statement: lemma expI_inv_eq_star : ((expI : ℂ))⁻¹ = star (expI : ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI_mul_conj
declarations.doc: `exp i` times its conjugate is one.
declarations.statement: lemma expI_mul_conj : (expI : ℂ) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (expI : ℂ) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.conj_mul_expI
declarations.doc: The conjugate of `exp i` times `exp i` is one.
declarations.statement: lemma conj_mul_expI : (starRingEnd ℂ) (expI : ℂ) * (expI : ℂ) = 1

declarations.name: Matrix.mem_specialUnitaryGroup_diagonal
declarations.doc:
A diagonal matrix whose entries are unit scalars with product one lies in the special
unitary group.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.Matrix.mem_specialUnitaryGroup_diagonal {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (d : n → ℂ) (hd : ∀ i, d i * star (d i) = 1) (hdet : ∏ i, d i = 1) :
    Matrix.diagonal d ∈ Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup n ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3ExpIOne
declarations.doc: The first colour torus generator, `diag (exp i, exp (-i), 1)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3ExpIOne : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3ExpITwo
declarations.doc: The second colour torus generator, `diag (1, exp i, exp (-i))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3ExpITwo : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2ExpI
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` torus element, `diag (exp i, exp (-i))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su2ExpI : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2ExpI_coe
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of the `SU(2)` torus element.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2ExpI_coe :
    (su2ExpI : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ).1
      = !![(expI : ℂ), 0; 0, star (expI : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2ExpI_inv_coe
declarations.doc:
The inverse torus element is `diag (exp (-i), exp i)`, so on a doublet the two components
are scaled by the reciprocal characters.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2ExpI_inv_coe :
    (su2ExpI⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ).1
      = !![star (expI : ℂ), 0; 0, (expI : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI_inv_coe
declarations.doc: The inverse of the unitary `exp i` is its conjugate.
declarations.statement: lemma expI_inv_coe : ((expI⁻¹ : unitary ℂ) : ℂ) = star (expI : ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3ExpIOne_inv_coe
declarations.doc: The inverse of the first colour torus generator, `diag (exp (-i), exp i, 1)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3ExpIOne_inv_coe :
    (su3ExpIOne⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ).1
      = Matrix.diagonal ![star (expI : ℂ), (expI : ℂ), 1]

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3ExpITwo_inv_coe
declarations.doc: The inverse of the second colour torus generator, `diag (1, exp (-i), exp i)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3ExpITwo_inv_coe :
    (su3ExpITwo⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ).1
      = Matrix.diagonal ![1, star (expI : ℂ), (expI : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeTorusGen
declarations.doc: The four commuting generators of the maximal torus of the gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeTorusGen : Fin 4 → GaugeGroupI

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
A gauge weight, the four exponents `(colour₁, colour₂, isospin, hypercharge)`
recording how a vector scales under `gaugeTorusGen`.
declarations.statement: abbrev GaugeWeight : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord
declarations.doc: The exponent of a gauge weight against the `i`-th torus generator.
declarations.statement: def GaugeWeight.coord (w : GaugeWeight) : Fin 4 → ℤ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_zero
declarations.doc: The exponent at the first colour generator.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_zero (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 0 = w.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_one
declarations.doc: The exponent at the second colour generator.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_one (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 1 = w.2.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_two
declarations.doc: The exponent at the isospin generator, normalized as `2T₃`.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_two (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 2 = w.2.2.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_three
declarations.doc: The exponent at the hypercharge generator, normalized as `6Y`.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_three (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 3 = w.2.2.2

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_neg
declarations.doc: The zero gauge weight has vanishing exponent against every torus generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma GaugeWeight.coord_neg (w : GaugeWeight) (i : Fin 4) :
    (-w).coord i = -(w.coord i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.zero_coord
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.zero_coord (i : Fin 4) : (0 : GaugeWeight).coord i = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_add
declarations.doc:
Weights add coordinatewise. With `zero_coord` this says `coord` is additive, which is
what makes gauge weights add under multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma GaugeWeight.coord_add (w w' : GaugeWeight) (i : Fin 4) :
    (w + w').coord i = w.coord i + w'.coord i

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_injective
declarations.doc:
A gauge weight is determined by its four exponents. This is what lets a weight be
recovered from the characters by which the torus acts; see `piece_eq_inf`.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_injective : Function.Injective GaugeWeight.coord

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsMulRep
declarations.doc:
A representation acts by algebra maps, respecting multiplication. This is the
hypothesis under which charges are additive.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsMulRep (rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B) : Prop

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsMulRep.map_one
declarations.doc:
A representation that respects multiplication respects the unit, since `g` is invertible
and so `rep g 1` is cancellable.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsMulRep.map_one {rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B} (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (g : GaugeGroupI) : rep g 1 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.starRingEnd_expI_pow
declarations.statement:
lemma starRingEnd_expI_pow (n : ℕ) :
    ((starRingEnd ℂ) (expI : ℂ)) ^ n = ((expI : ℂ) ^ n)⁻¹

declarations.name: StandardModel.starRingEnd_expI_zpow
declarations.statement:
lemma starRingEnd_expI_zpow (z : ℤ) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) ((expI : ℂ) ^ z) = (expI : ℂ) ^ (-z)

declarations.name: StandardModel.star_expI_zpow
declarations.doc: Conjugation inverts an integer power of `expI`.
declarations.statement: lemma star_expI_zpow (z : ℤ) : star ((expI : ℂ) ^ z) = (expI : ℂ) ^ (-z)

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI_zpow_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma expI_zpow_ne_zero (z : ℤ) : ((expI : ℂ) ^ z) ≠ 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.colourWeight
declarations.doc:
The colour weights of the fundamental of `SU(3)` against the two colour torus
generators.
declarations.statement: def colourWeight (c : Fin 3) : ℤ × ℤ

declarations.name: StandardModel.isoWeight
declarations.doc:
The isospin weight of the fundamental of `SU(2)` against the isospin torus
generator.
declarations.statement: def isoWeight (s : Fin 2) : ℤ

declarations.name: StandardModel.dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (ρ : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI V)
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ V) (g : GaugeGroupI) (w : ι → ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ j, ρ g (b j) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w j) • b j) (j : ι) :
    ρ.dual g (b.coord j) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ (-(w j))) • b.coord j

declarations.name: StandardModel.conj_gaugeTorusGen_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_gaugeTorusGen_basis (ρ : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI V)
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ V) (g : GaugeGroupI) (w : ι → ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ j, ρ g (b j) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w j) • b j) (j : ι) :
    ρ.conj g (Basis.conj b j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ (-(w j))) • Basis.conj b j

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition
declarations.doc:
A gauge weight decomposition of a submodule `V`, a finitely supported family of
subspaces of pure gauge weight whose supremum is `V`. Purity is recorded against the four
commuting torus generators simultaneously.
declarations.statement:
class GaugeWeightDecomposition (rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B)
    (V : Submodule ℂ B) where
  /-- The piece of gauge weight `w`. -/
  piece : GaugeWeight → Submodule ℂ B
  /-- The finite set of gauge weights that occur. -/
  supp : Finset GaugeWeight
  /-- Gauge transformations act by algebra maps. -/
  rep_mul : IsMulRep rep
  /-- Each piece is of pure gauge weight, as seen by all four torus generators. -/
  piece_le : ∀ w, ∀ x, x ∈ piece w → ∀ i,
    rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i) • x
  /-- Only the gauge weights in `supp` occur. -/
  piece_eq_bot : ∀ w ∉ supp, piece w = ⊥
  /-- The pieces exhaust `V`. -/
  iSup_piece : (⨆ w, piece w) = V

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_le_eigenspace
declarations.doc:
The weight-`w` piece lies in the eigenspace of the `i`-th torus generator at the
eigenvalue `(exp i) ^ (w.coord i)`. This is `piece_le` phrased as an inequality of
submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_le_eigenspace (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight) (i : Fin 4) :
    d.piece w ≤ Module.End.eigenspace (rep (gaugeTorusGen i)) ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_eq_zero_of_not_mem_supp
declarations.doc:
A weight outside the support has vanishing piece. This is the `piece_eq_bot` field, in
the form a `simp` set can use to discard the absent weights of a computed product.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_eq_zero_of_not_mem_supp (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight)
    (hw : w ∉ d.supp) : d.piece w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_le_self
declarations.doc: A weight piece lies inside the submodule it decomposes.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_le_self (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    d.piece w ≤ V

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.copy
declarations.doc: Transport a decomposition along an equality of submodules.
declarations.statement:
def copy (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (W : Submodule ℂ B) (hW : W = V) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep W

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.copy_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma copy_piece (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (W : Submodule ℂ B) (hW : W = V) :
    (copy d W hW).piece = d.piece

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup
declarations.doc:
The join of two gauge weight decompositions, decomposing `V ⊔ V'`. Pieces and supports
combine one weight at a time.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance sup [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V ⊔ V')

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma sup_piece [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V] [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V']
    (w : GaugeWeight) : piece rep (V ⊔ V') w = piece rep V w ⊔ piece rep V' w

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.bot
declarations.doc: The zero submodule carries the empty decomposition.
declarations.statement:
def bot (hmul : IsMulRep rep) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (⊥ : Submodule ℂ B)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.bot_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma bot_piece (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (w : GaugeWeight) : (bot hmul).piece w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.bot_supp
declarations.statement:
lemma bot_supp (hmul : IsMulRep rep) :
    (bot hmul).supp = ∅

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.spanSingleton
declarations.doc:
The span of a single simultaneous eigenvector of the gauge torus, as a
decomposition concentrated in its one weight. This is the base case from which the
decompositions of spans of weight vectors are assembled by `iSup` and `sup`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spanSingleton (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (x : B) (w : GaugeWeight)
    (hx : ∀ i, rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i) • x) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (Submodule.span ℂ {x})

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.spanSingleton_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma spanSingleton_piece (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (x : B) (w : GaugeWeight)
    (hx : ∀ i, rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i) • x)
    (w' : GaugeWeight) :
    (spanSingleton hmul x w hx).piece w'
      = if w' = w then Submodule.span ℂ {x} else ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.iSup
declarations.doc:
An indexed join of decompositions. A family of decompositions indexed by a finite type
decomposes the join, its pieces joined and its supports united one weight at a time. This is
the arbitrary-arity form of `sup`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iSup {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : (a : ι) → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V a)) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (⨆ a, V a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_iSup
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_iSup {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : (a : ι) → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V a)) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (iSup hmul d).piece w = ⨆ a, (d a).piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.iSup_supp
declarations.doc: The support of an indexed join is the union of the supports.
declarations.statement:
lemma iSup_supp {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : (a : ι) → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V a)) :
    (iSup hmul d).supp = Finset.univ.biUnion fun a => (d a).supp

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.iSupProp
declarations.doc:
A join over a proposition. `⨆ _ : p, V` is `V` when `p` holds and `⊥` otherwise, so
it is decomposed by the given decomposition or by `bot`. The argument is a function of the
proof, so the decomposition of `V` may itself depend on `p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iSupProp {p : Prop} [Decidable p]
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : p → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (⨆ _ : p, V)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
declarations.doc: The product of two gauge weight decompositions, decomposing `V * V'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance mul [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V * V')

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_supp
declarations.doc: The support of a product is the pointwise sum of the supports.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_supp [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V] [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] :
    supp rep (V * V') = supp rep V + supp rep V'

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_piece
declarations.doc:
Weights add under multiplication. The weight-`w` piece of a product is spanned by the
products of pieces whose weights sum to `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_piece [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V] [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V']
    (w : GaugeWeight) :
    piece rep (V * V') w
      = ⨆ w₁, ⨆ w₂, ⨆ _ : w₁ + w₂ = w, piece rep V w₁ * piece rep V' w₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_piece_eq_sub
declarations.doc:
The product formula with the second weight eliminated against the support of the left
factor, the right factor being read at the complement `w - w₁`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_piece_eq_sub [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] (w : GaugeWeight) :
    piece rep (V * V') w = ⨆ w₁ ∈ supp rep V, piece rep V w₁ * piece rep V' (w - w₁)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_piece_eq_sub'
declarations.doc: The mirror of `mul_piece_eq_sub`, joining over the weights of the right factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_piece_eq_sub' [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] (w : GaugeWeight) :
    piece rep (V * V') w = ⨆ w₂ ∈ supp rep V', piece rep V (w - w₂) * piece rep V' w₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_iSup_of_eigenvector
declarations.doc:
The one-generator refinement step. A vector in the span of a family graded along a
single operator, and an eigenvector of that operator at exponent `n`, lies in the span of
just those pieces at exponent `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_iSup_of_eigenvector {ι : Type*} {T : Module.End ℂ B} {p : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    {f : ι → ℤ} (hp : ∀ j, p j ≤ Module.End.eigenspace T ((expI : ℂ) ^ f j))
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ ⨆ j, p j) {n : ℤ} (hT : T x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ n) • x) :
    x ∈ ⨆ j, ⨆ _ : f j = n, p j

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_iSup_of_forall_eigenvector
declarations.doc:
The many-generator refinement. The same for a finite family of operators. A vector in
the span of the family and an eigenvector of every operator lies in the span of just those
pieces whose exponents match throughout.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_eq_inf
declarations.doc:
The pieces are canonical. The weight-`w` piece is exactly the part of `V` on which the
four torus generators act by the weight-`w` characters. See `piece_congr`.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_eq_inf (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    d.piece w
      = V ⊓ ⨅ i, Module.End.eigenspace (rep (gaugeTorusGen i)) ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_congr
declarations.doc:
The pieces depend only on the submodule. Two decompositions of equal submodules have
the same pieces, so a computation of `piece` may be carried along any equality of
submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_congr {W : Submodule ℂ B} [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep W] (hVW : V = W) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    d.piece w = d'.piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_zero_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
A gauge-invariant element sits in the zero-weight piece. Only invariance under the
four torus generators is used. The converse is false; see the warning in section F.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_zero_of_invariant (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V)
    (hV : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, rep g x = x) : x ∈ d.piece 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The torus sieve as a reduction for the four torus generators: modulo a torus-stable
submodule, their invariants in `V` lie in the weight-zero piece. Every other weight in the
support is scaled by some generator by `(exp i) ^ n` with `n ≠ 0`, a scalar other than `1`,
so its piece reduces to `⊥` by `reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul`; each piece is
carried into itself by the torus, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup` joins the pieces.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero (dV : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun i => rep (gaugeTorusGen i)) V (dV.piece 0)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
An element of `V ⊔ S` fixed by the four torus generators, for `S` closed under them,
lies in the weight-zero piece joined with `S`. This is `reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero`
unfolded, the form used to sieve a sector with `S` the part already understood. Only the
torus is used, so gauge invariance of the element and gauge stability of `S` are more than
is needed.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant {S : Submodule ℂ B}
    (dV : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V)
    (hS : ∀ (i : Fin 4) (y : B), y ∈ S → rep (gaugeTorusGen i) y ∈ S)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ i : Fin 4, rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = x) :
    x ∈ dV.piece 0 ⊔ S

modules.title: The Standard Model gauge group as a global gauge group
modules.doc:
The gauge group `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)` as block-diagonal `6 × 6` complex matrices.

## i. Overview

The global gauge group of the Standard Model is the product `SU(3) × (SU(2) × U(1))` of global
gauge groups, made of the block-diagonal matrices `diag(g₃, g₂, u)`. Its elements are the
elements of `GaugeGroupI`, through `StandardModel.gaugeGroupEquiv`. Taking the `SU(3)` block,
the `SU(2)` block and the phase `u` are continuous homomorphisms.

The representations of the three factors are pulled back along the projections to the blocks.
The `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` blocks act on the fundamental representations, and the phase `u` is the
hypercharge character. The matter fields of the Standard Model are built from these.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.globalGaugeGroup` : the global gauge group `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)`.
- `StandardModel.gaugeGroupEquiv` : its elements are those of `GaugeGroupI`.
- The instance `CompactSpace globalGaugeGroup.group` : the global gauge group is compact.
- `StandardModel.su3Block`, `StandardModel.su2Block`, `StandardModel.u1Phase` : the blocks of
  its elements, which on the image of `gaugeGroupEquiv` are the three factors
  (`StandardModel.su3Block_gaugeGroupEquiv` and its companions).
- `StandardModel.su3Fund`, `StandardModel.su2Fund` : the fundamental representations of the
  `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` factors, as continuous matrix representations of the global gauge group,
  with derivatives `StandardModel.derivMat_su3Fund` and `StandardModel.derivMat_su2Fund`.
- `StandardModel.hypercharge` : the hypercharge character, with derivative the `u(1)` entry
  (see `StandardModel.hypercharge_exp`).

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The global gauge group
- B. The blocks of the global gauge group
- C. The representations of the factors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The global gauge group

The product of the global gauge groups `SU 3`, `SU 2` and `U1`, its identification with
`GaugeGroupI` and its compactness.

## B. The blocks of the global gauge group

The `SU(3)` block, the `SU(2)` block and the phase of an element, as homomorphisms, read off
the matrix and continuous.

## C. The representations of the factors

The fundamental representations of the `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` factors are the blocks of a gauge
transformation `diag(g₃, g₂, u)`, which act by `g₃` and `g₂`. The hypercharge character is the
phase `u`, and its derivative is the entry of the `U(1)` block of a Lie algebra element.

declarations.name: StandardModel.globalGaugeGroup
declarations.doc:
The global gauge group of the Standard Model, `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)` as the
block-diagonal matrices `diag(g₃, g₂, u)` on `ℂ³ ⊕ ℂ² ⊕ ℂ`.
declarations.statement: def globalGaugeGroup : GlobalGaugeGroup (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1))

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeGroupEquiv
declarations.doc:
The gauge group `GaugeGroupI` of the Standard Model is its global gauge group, through the
block-diagonal matrices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeGroupEquiv : GaugeGroupI ≃* globalGaugeGroup.group

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeGroupEquiv_val
declarations.doc: An element of `GaugeGroupI` is the block-diagonal matrix of its three components.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeGroupEquiv_val (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    (((gaugeGroupEquiv g : globalGaugeGroup.group) : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄) =
      fromBlocks (g.1 : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) 0 0
        (fromBlocks (g.2.1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) 0 0 (scalar (Fin 1) (g.2.2 : ℂ)))

declarations.doc:
The global gauge group of the Standard Model is compact, being a product of the compact
groups `SU(3)`, `SU(2)` and `U(1)`.
declarations.statement: instance : CompactSpace globalGaugeGroup.group

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Block
declarations.doc: The `SU(3)` block `g₃` of an element `diag(g₃, g₂, u)` of the global gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3Block : globalGaugeGroup.group →* Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Block
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` block `g₂` of an element `diag(g₃, g₂, u)` of the global gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su2Block : globalGaugeGroup.group →* Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.u1Phase
declarations.doc: The phase `u` of an element `diag(g₃, g₂, u)` of the global gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def u1Phase : globalGaugeGroup.group →* ℂˣ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Block_gaugeGroupEquiv
declarations.doc: The `SU(3)` block of the image of a gauge transformation is its colour factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3Block_gaugeGroupEquiv (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    su3Block (gaugeGroupEquiv g) = (g.toSU3.1 : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Block_gaugeGroupEquiv
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` block of the image of a gauge transformation is its isospin factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2Block_gaugeGroupEquiv (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    su2Block (gaugeGroupEquiv g) = (g.toSU2.1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.u1Phase_gaugeGroupEquiv
declarations.doc: The phase of the image of a gauge transformation is its hypercharge factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma u1Phase_gaugeGroupEquiv (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    ((u1Phase (gaugeGroupEquiv g) : ℂˣ) : ℂ) = (g.toU1.1 : ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.globalGaugeGroup_val_eq_fromBlocks
declarations.doc: An element of the global gauge group is the block-diagonal matrix of its blocks.
declarations.statement:
lemma globalGaugeGroup_val_eq_fromBlocks (g : globalGaugeGroup.group) :
    ((g : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄) =
      fromBlocks (su3Block g) 0 0 (fromBlocks (su2Block g) 0 0
        (scalar (Fin 1) (u1Phase g : ℂ)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Block_eq
declarations.doc: The `SU(3)` block is the upper-left `3 × 3` block of the matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3Block_eq (g : globalGaugeGroup.group) :
    su3Block g = toBlocks₁₁ ((g : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄)

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Block_eq
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` block is the middle `2 × 2` block of the matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2Block_eq (g : globalGaugeGroup.group) :
    su2Block g = toBlocks₁₁ (toBlocks₂₂ ((g : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄))

declarations.name: StandardModel.u1Phase_eq
declarations.doc: The phase is the lower-right entry of the matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma u1Phase_eq (g : globalGaugeGroup.group) :
    (u1Phase g : ℂ) = toBlocks₂₂ (toBlocks₂₂ ((g : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄)) 0 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.continuous_globalGaugeGroup_val
declarations.doc: The matrix of an element of the global gauge group depends continuously on it.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_globalGaugeGroup_val :
    Continuous fun g : globalGaugeGroup.group => ((g : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄)

declarations.name: StandardModel.continuous_su3Block
declarations.doc: The `SU(3)` block depends continuously on the gauge transformation.
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_su3Block : Continuous fun g => su3Block g

declarations.name: StandardModel.continuous_su2Block
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` block depends continuously on the gauge transformation.
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_su2Block : Continuous fun g => su2Block g

declarations.name: StandardModel.continuous_u1Phase
declarations.doc: The phase depends continuously on the gauge transformation.
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_u1Phase : Continuous fun g => (u1Phase g : ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.continuous_toHomUnits
declarations.doc:
A continuous monoid homomorphism from the global gauge group to a monoid, which takes
values in the units, is a continuous homomorphism to the units.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_toHomUnits {M : Type} [Monoid M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    {f : globalGaugeGroup.group →* M} (hf : Continuous f) : Continuous f.toHomUnits

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Fund
declarations.doc:
The fundamental representation of the `SU(3)` factor, as a continuous representation of the
global gauge group. A gauge transformation `diag(g₃, g₂, u)` acts by `g₃`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3Fund : globalGaugeGroup.group →ₜ* (Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ)ˣ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Fund
declarations.doc:
The fundamental representation of the `SU(2)` factor, as a continuous representation of the
global gauge group. A gauge transformation `diag(g₃, g₂, u)` acts by `g₂`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su2Fund : globalGaugeGroup.group →ₜ* (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)ˣ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Fund_val
declarations.doc:
A gauge transformation acts on the fundamental representation of the `SU(3)` factor by
its `SU(3)` block.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3Fund_val (g : globalGaugeGroup.group) :
    ((su3Fund g : (Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ)ˣ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) = su3Block g

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Fund_val
declarations.doc:
A gauge transformation acts on the fundamental representation of the `SU(2)` factor by
its `SU(2)` block.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2Fund_val (g : globalGaugeGroup.group) :
    ((su2Fund g : (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)ˣ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = su2Block g

declarations.name: StandardModel.derivMat_su3Fund
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra acts on the fundamental representation of the `SU(3)` factor by its
`SU(3)` block.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_su3Fund (c : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra) :
    derivMat su3Fund c = (c : 𝕄).toBlocks₁₁

declarations.name: StandardModel.derivMat_su2Fund
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra acts on the fundamental representation of the `SU(2)` factor by its
`SU(2)` block.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_su2Fund (c : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra) :
    derivMat su2Fund c = (c : 𝕄).toBlocks₂₂.toBlocks₁₁

declarations.name: StandardModel.hypercharge
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge character of the global gauge group is the phase `u` of an element
`diag(g₃, g₂, u)`. Its derivative is the entry of the `U(1)` block of a Lie algebra
element, see `hypercharge_exp`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hypercharge : globalGaugeGroup.group →ₜ* ℂˣ

declarations.name: StandardModel.hypercharge_exp
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge character of the exponential of a Lie algebra element is the exponential of
the entry of its `U(1)` block, that is `hypercharge (exp (t c)) = exp (t z)` with `z` the
derivative of the hypercharge at `c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hypercharge_exp (c : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra) (t : ℝ)
    (g : globalGaugeGroup.group)
    (hg : ((g : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄) =
      NormedSpace.exp (t • (c : 𝕄))) :
    ((hypercharge g : ℂˣ) : ℂ) = Complex.exp (t * (c : 𝕄).toBlocks₂₂.toBlocks₂₂ 0 0)

modules.title: Families of adjoint components and their invariants
modules.doc:
Families of components with colour or isospin adjoint indices, and the trace contraction their
invariants reduce to.

## i. Overview

The Standard Model labels the adjoint indices of `su(3)` by the eight Gell-Mann matrices
`gellMannMatrix`, and those of `su(2)` by the three Pauli matrices, and moves them by the adjoint
matrices `su3AdjointMatrix` and `su2AdjointMatrix`. These are the generalized Gell-Mann matrices
`GellMann.matrix` of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.GellMann` for `N = 3` and
`N = 2` under a relabelling, `su3Label` and `su2Label`, and the adjoint matrices are the matrices
of the adjoint action in those bases (A).

A family with one adjoint index has no invariant in its span, and a family with two adjoint
indices of the same factor has its invariants reduced to the trace contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]`
(C for colour, D for isospin). These are the invariant tensors of `SuT[N, .adj]` and
`SuT[N, .adj, .adj]` of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.Invariants.AdjUnit`, read on
the components through the relabellings `relabelAdjIdx` and `relabelAdjPairIdx` of B. The lemmas
of each family live in a namespace named after its representation, `ColourAdj`, `ColourAdjAdj`,
`IsospinAdj` and `IsospinAdjAdj`.

The hypercharge factor is abelian, so its adjoint action on `u(1)` is trivial: a family with two
`u(1)` adjoint indices is moved by a hypercharge rotation not at all, and its trace contraction,
its one component, is fixed by every map that fixes the components (E).

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.su3Label`, `StandardModel.su2Label` : the Gell-Mann and Pauli labels as
  generalized Gell-Mann labels.
- `StandardModel.ColourAdj.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` : one colour adjoint index carries no
  invariant, and its isospin twin.
- `StandardModel.ColourAdjAdj.reducesInvariantsTo_span_traceContraction` : two colour adjoint
  indices reduce to the trace contraction, and its isospin twin.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Gell-Mann labels
- B. Relabelled adjoint families
- C. The colour adjoint families
- D. The isospin adjoint families
- E. The hypercharge adjoint families

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The Gell-Mann labels

The Gell-Mann and Pauli matrices are the generalized Gell-Mann matrices up to a relabelling, so
the Standard Model adjoint matrices are the matrices of the adjoint action.

## B. Relabelled adjoint families

A family indexed by the Standard Model labels of the adjoint index and moved by the Standard Model
adjoint matrices is, after relabelling, a family moved by the matrices of the adjoint action.

## C. The colour adjoint families

A family with one colour adjoint index has no invariant, and one with two has the trace
contraction alone.

## D. The isospin adjoint families

The isospin twins of the families of section C.

## E. The hypercharge adjoint families

The hypercharge factor is abelian, so its adjoint action on `u(1)` is trivial, and there is no
tensor species to relabel. A family `T : (Fin 2 → Fin 1) → B` with two `u(1)` adjoint indices is
moved by a hypercharge rotation by one factor of the `1 × 1` adjoint matrix `1` per index, which is
to say not at all, so its law is stated directly as `∀ l, f (T l) = T l`. The trace contraction
is the one component of the family, and every map fixing the components fixes it.

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3LabelFun
declarations.doc:
The labels of the Gell-Mann matrices of `su(3)` as generalized Gell-Mann labels. They are the
symmetric and antisymmetric matrices of the planes `(0, 1)`, `(0, 2)` and `(1, 2)`, and the two
diagonal matrices.
declarations.statement: def su3LabelFun : Fin 8 → GellMann.Index 3

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Label
declarations.doc: The relabelling of the Gell-Mann matrices of `su(3)` by generalized Gell-Mann labels.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3Label : Fin 8 ≃ GellMann.Index 3

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2LabelFun
declarations.doc: The labels of the Pauli matrices of `su(2)` as generalized Gell-Mann labels.
declarations.statement: def su2LabelFun : Fin 3 → GellMann.Index 2

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Label
declarations.doc: The relabelling of the Pauli matrices of `su(2)` by generalized Gell-Mann labels.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su2Label : Fin 3 ≃ GellMann.Index 2

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Label_apply
declarations.doc: The relabelling of the Gell-Mann matrices is `su3LabelFun`.
declarations.statement: lemma su3Label_apply (a : Fin 8) : su3Label a = su3LabelFun a

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Label_apply
declarations.doc: The relabelling of the Pauli matrices is `su2LabelFun`.
declarations.statement: lemma su2Label_apply (i : Fin 3) : su2Label i = su2LabelFun i

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix_eq_matrix
declarations.doc: The Gell-Mann matrices of `su(3)` are the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrix_eq_matrix (a : Fin 8) :
    gellMannMatrix a = GellMann.matrix (su3Label a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.pauliMatrix_inr_eq_matrix
declarations.doc: The Pauli matrices are the generalized Gell-Mann matrices of `su(2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliMatrix_inr_eq_matrix (i : Fin 3) :
    pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) = GellMann.matrix (su2Label i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix_eq_adjMatrix
declarations.doc:
The adjoint matrix of `SU(3)` is the matrix of the adjoint action in the Gell-Mann
basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3AdjointMatrix_eq_adjMatrix (U : SU 3) (a b : Fin 8) :

modules.title: Families of colour and isospin components and their invariants
modules.doc:
Families of components moved by the colour or isospin factor, and the contractions their invariants
reduce to.

## i. Overview

The invariant tensors of `SU(N)` are classified in `GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.Invariants`,
for equivariant maps out of the tensors of `suTensor N`. Here those results are applied to the
Standard Model. A family `T : ι → B` of components, indexed by colour or isospin labels and moved by
the colour factor `repGauge (U, 1, 1)` or the isospin factor `repGauge (1, V, 1)` of the gauge
group, is turned into the linear map `liftComponents` out of the tensors of `SU(3)` or `SU(2)` with
an explicit list of colours, and its transformation law is exactly the equivariance of that map
for the restriction of `repGauge` along the factor (A).

A law is named by how the members of the family move as vectors of `B`. Under a fundamental law
`f (T l) = ∑ a, U a l • T a`, so `T l` moves like the standard basis vector `e_l` of `ℂⁿ`; an
anti-fundamental law has `conj U` in place of `U`. The component symbols of a field are values of
an equivariant map on dual vectors, so they obey the dual of the field's law. The symbols of a
doublet or triplet field form an anti-fundamental family, and those of its conjugate a fundamental
one.

For a family with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index the invariants reduce to the delta
contraction (B). For two fundamental or two anti-fundamental indices of `SU(2)` they reduce to the
epsilon contraction (C), and for four fundamental indices of `SU(2)` to the two epsilon pairings
(D). The contractions are written out on the components, and the lemmas `map_…Contraction` take
the law a single linear map obeys, for the reductions over the whole gauge group. The lemmas of
each family live in a namespace named after its representation, `ColourFundAntiFund`,
`IsospinFundAntiFund`, `IsospinFundFund`, `IsospinAntiFundAntiFund` and `IsospinQuadFund`.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.ColourFundAntiFund.invariantReductionToSpan` : the colour invariants of a family
  with one fundamental and one anti-fundamental colour index.
- `StandardModel.IsospinFundAntiFund.invariantReductionToSpan` : its isospin twin.
- `StandardModel.IsospinFundFund.invariantReductionToSpan`,
  `StandardModel.IsospinAntiFundAntiFund.invariantReductionToSpan` : two isospin indices of the
  same kind.
- `StandardModel.IsospinQuadFund.reducesInvariantsTo_span_epsilonContractions` : four fundamental
  isospin indices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The factors of the gauge group
- B. One fundamental and one anti-fundamental index
- C. Two isospin indices of the same kind
- D. Four fundamental isospin indices

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The factors of the gauge group

The colour and isospin factors as homomorphisms into `GaugeGroupI`, along which the
representation of the gauge group is restricted.

## B. One fundamental and one anti-fundamental index

The invariants reduce to the delta contraction, for colour and for isospin.

## C. Two isospin indices of the same kind

Two fundamental or two anti-fundamental isospin indices have the epsilon contraction alone as
invariant.

## D. Four fundamental isospin indices

The invariants reduce to the two ways of pairing the four indices by epsilon.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ColourFundAntiFund.of_law
declarations.doc:

    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGauge.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents (T ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

      (liftComponents ((fun l => ∑ i, T i l) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

modules.title: The gauge algebra as the Lie algebra of the global gauge group
modules.doc:
The gauge algebra of the Standard Model is the Lie algebra of its global gauge group.

## i. Overview

The Lie algebra of the global gauge group `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)` consists of the block-diagonal
matrices `diag(X₃, X₂, X₁)` with `X₃` and `X₂` traceless anti-hermitian and `X₁` an imaginary
scalar, with the commutator as bracket. The gauge algebra `GaugeAlgebra` has the hermitian
matrices `c₃`, `c₂` and the real scalar `c₁` instead, with the bracket carrying a factor of `i`.
The two are identified through `c ↦ diag(i c₃, i c₂, i c₁)`, which is a Lie algebra
isomorphism.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraToMatrix` : the block-diagonal matrix `diag(i c₃, i c₂, i c₁)` of
  an element `c` of the gauge algebra.
- `StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraEquiv` : the Lie algebra isomorphism from `GaugeAlgebra` to the
  Lie algebra of `globalGaugeGroup`.
- `StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraEquiv_coe` : the underlying matrix of its value.
- `StandardModel.derivMat_su3Fund_gaugeAlgebraEquiv`,
  `StandardModel.derivMat_su2Fund_gaugeAlgebraEquiv`,
  `StandardModel.hypercharge_exp_gaugeAlgebraEquiv` : the derivatives of the fundamental
  representations and of the hypercharge, on the image of a gauge algebra element.
- `StandardModel.adjointRep_gaugeAlgebraEquiv` : the adjoint action of the global gauge group
  is the blockwise conjugation `GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap`.
- `StandardModel.gaugeDualToLie` : a functional on the gauge algebra transported to one on the
  Lie algebra of `globalGaugeGroup`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The block-diagonal matrix of a gauge algebra element
- B. The Lie algebra homomorphism
- C. The equivalence
- D. The fundamental representations and the hypercharge
- E. The adjoint action

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The block-diagonal matrix of a gauge algebra element

The real-linear map `c ↦ diag(i c₃, i c₂, i c₁)`, whose values are traceless anti-hermitian in
the non-abelian blocks and imaginary in the abelian one.

## B. The Lie algebra homomorphism

The factor of `i` in the bracket of `GaugeAlgebra` is what makes the map a Lie algebra
homomorphism to the commutator bracket.
## C. The equivalence

## D. The fundamental representations and the hypercharge

On the image of a gauge algebra element `c`, the derivatives of the fundamental representations
are `i c₃` and `i c₂`, and that of the hypercharge is `i c₁`. The matter fields of the Standard
Model read their infinitesimal actions off these.

## E. The adjoint action

The adjoint action of the global gauge group is blockwise conjugation on the gauge algebra, and
functionals on the gauge algebra are transported to the Lie algebra with their dual action.

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraToMatrix
declarations.doc:
The block-diagonal matrix `diag(i c₃, i c₂, i c₁)` of an element `c` of the gauge algebra,
with `c₃` and `c₂` hermitian traceless and `c₁` a real scalar.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeAlgebraToMatrix : GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] 𝕄

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraToMatrix_mem
declarations.doc:
The block-diagonal matrix of a gauge algebra element lies in the Lie algebra of the global
gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAlgebraToMatrix_mem (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    gaugeAlgebraToMatrix c ∈ globalGaugeGroup.lieAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraHom
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra homomorphism from the gauge algebra to the Lie algebra of the global gauge
group, sending `c` to `diag(i c₃, i c₂, i c₁)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeAlgebraHom : GaugeAlgebra →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraHom_injective
declarations.doc: The homomorphism from the gauge algebra is injective.
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeAlgebraHom_injective : Function.Injective gaugeAlgebraHom

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraHom_surjective
declarations.doc:
Every element of the Lie algebra of the global gauge group is the image of an element of the
gauge algebra. The `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` blocks are traceless and anti-hermitian, and the
`U(1)` block is an imaginary scalar.
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeAlgebraHom_surjective : Function.Surjective gaugeAlgebraHom

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra isomorphism from the gauge algebra of the Standard Model to the Lie algebra
of its global gauge group, sending `c` to `diag(i c₃, i c₂, i c₁)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeAlgebraEquiv : GaugeAlgebra ≃ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeAlgebraEquiv_coe
declarations.doc:
The underlying matrix of the image of `c` under `gaugeAlgebraEquiv` is
`diag(i c₃, i c₂, i c₁)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAlgebraEquiv_coe (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    ((gaugeAlgebraEquiv c : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra) : 𝕄) =
      fromBlocks (Complex.I • c.toSU3Matrix) 0 0
        (fromBlocks (Complex.I • c.toSU2Matrix) 0 0
          (Complex.I • scalar (Fin 1) c.toU1Value))

declarations.name: StandardModel.derivMat_su3Fund_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra element `gaugeAlgebraEquiv c` acts on the fundamental representation of the
`SU(3)` factor by `i c₃`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_su3Fund_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    derivMat su3Fund (gaugeAlgebraEquiv c) = Complex.I • c.toSU3Matrix

declarations.name: StandardModel.derivMat_su2Fund_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra element `gaugeAlgebraEquiv c` acts on the fundamental representation of the
`SU(2)` factor by `i c₂`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_su2Fund_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    derivMat su2Fund (gaugeAlgebraEquiv c) = Complex.I • c.toSU2Matrix

declarations.name: StandardModel.hypercharge_exp_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge of the exponential of `t` times the image of `c` is `exp (t i c₁)`, so the
derivative of the hypercharge at `gaugeAlgebraEquiv c` is `i c₁`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hypercharge_exp_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (c : GaugeAlgebra) (t : ℝ)
    (g : globalGaugeGroup.group)
    (hg : ((g : GL (Fin 3 ⊕ (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 1)) ℂ) : 𝕄) =
      NormedSpace.exp (t • ((gaugeAlgebraEquiv c : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra) : 𝕄))) :
    ((hypercharge g : ℂˣ) : ℂ) = Complex.exp (t * (Complex.I * c.toU1Value))

declarations.name: StandardModel.adjointRep_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of the global gauge group on its Lie algebra, transported along
`gaugeGroupEquiv` and `gaugeAlgebraEquiv`, is the blockwise conjugation
`GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointRep_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    globalGaugeGroup.adjointRep (gaugeGroupEquiv g) (gaugeAlgebraEquiv a) =
      gaugeAlgebraEquiv (GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap g a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.dualMap_adjointRep_comp_symm
declarations.doc:
The dual of the adjoint action of the global gauge group on a functional of the form
`φ ∘ gaugeAlgebraEquiv⁻¹` is the transport of the dual of `GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualMap_adjointRep_comp_symm (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    (globalGaugeGroup.adjointRep (gaugeGroupEquiv g)).dualMap
        (φ ∘ₗ (gaugeAlgebraEquiv.symm : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] GaugeAlgebra)) =
      ((GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap g).dualMap φ) ∘ₗ
        (gaugeAlgebraEquiv.symm : globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] GaugeAlgebra)

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeDualToLie
declarations.doc:
A functional on the gauge algebra `GaugeAlgebra`, transported along `gaugeAlgebraEquiv` to
one on the Lie algebra of the global gauge group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev gaugeDualToLie (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    Module.Dual ℝ globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra

modules.title: The antisymmetric symbol and complex conjugation in `SU(2)`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`su2Epsilon` is the antisymmetric symbol on two isospin indices: Physlib's `leviCivitaSymbol`
on `Fin 2`, normalized by `su2Epsilon 0 1 = 1`. It transforms by the determinant, so every
`U ∈ SU(2)` fixes it (`sum_su2Epsilon_mul`).

The entrywise conjugate of `U ∈ SU(2)` is `ε U ε⁻¹`, entry by entry `conj U₀₀ = U₁₁`,
`conj U₀₁ = -U₁₀`, `conj U₁₀ = -U₀₁` and `conj U₁₁ = U₀₀`. This is the pseudo-reality of
`SU(2)`. It is a different fact from `conj U = (U⁻¹)ᵀ`, which holds for every unitary `U`. The
classifiers and the Higgs sector use these identities only through explicit re-indexes by `ε`.

## ii. Key results

- `su2Epsilon` : the antisymmetric symbol `ε_{ab}` on two `su(2)` fundamental indices: the
  Levi-Civita symbol of `Fin 2`, normalized by `ε 0 1 = 1`
- `sum_su2Epsilon_mul` : every element of `SU(2)` fixes the antisymmetric symbol: contracted against
  two rows of `U` it gives `det U` times itself (`sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod`), and `det U = 1`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The antisymmetric symbol
- B. The entries of an `SU(2)` matrix under conjugation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The antisymmetric symbol

## B. The entries of an `SU(2)` matrix under conjugation

The determinant being one, the adjugate of `U` is its inverse, and `U` being unitary, so is
its conjugate transpose. Reading the adjugate of a `2 × 2` matrix entry by entry gives the four
identities.

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Epsilon
declarations.doc:
The antisymmetric symbol `ε_{ab}` on two `su(2)` fundamental indices: the Levi-Civita
symbol of `Fin 2`, normalized by `ε 0 1 = 1`.
declarations.statement: def su2Epsilon (a b : Fin 2) : ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Epsilon_zero_zero
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol vanishes when both indices are zero.
declarations.statement: lemma su2Epsilon_zero_zero : su2Epsilon 0 0 = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Epsilon_zero_one
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol on the increasing pair.
declarations.statement: lemma su2Epsilon_zero_one : su2Epsilon 0 1 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Epsilon_one_zero
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol on the decreasing pair.
declarations.statement: lemma su2Epsilon_one_zero : su2Epsilon 1 0 = -1

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Epsilon_one_one
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol vanishes when both indices are one.
declarations.statement: lemma su2Epsilon_one_one : su2Epsilon 1 1 = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_su2Epsilon_mul
declarations.doc:
Every element of `SU(2)` fixes the antisymmetric symbol: contracted against two rows of
`U` it gives `det U` times itself (`sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod`), and `det U = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_su2Epsilon_mul (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (b c : Fin 2) :
    ∑ x : Fin 2, ∑ y : Fin 2, su2Epsilon x y * (U.1 b x * U.1 c y) = su2Epsilon b c

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2_star_eq_adjugate
declarations.doc: The conjugate transpose of an `SU(2)` matrix is its adjugate.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2_star_eq_adjugate (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    star U.1 = Matrix.adjugate U.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2_conj_apply
declarations.doc:
The conjugate of an entry of an `SU(2)` matrix is the transposed entry of its
adjugate.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2_conj_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (i j : Fin 2) :
    conj (U.1 i j) = Matrix.adjugate U.1 j i

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2_conj_apply_zero_zero
declarations.doc: Conjugating the upper left entry of an `SU(2)` matrix gives the lower right one.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2_conj_apply_zero_zero (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    conj (U.1 0 0) = U.1 1 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2_conj_apply_one_one
declarations.doc: Conjugating the lower right entry of an `SU(2)` matrix gives the upper left one.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2_conj_apply_one_one (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    conj (U.1 1 1) = U.1 0 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2_conj_apply_zero_one
declarations.doc:
Conjugating the upper right entry of an `SU(2)` matrix gives minus the lower left
one.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2_conj_apply_zero_one (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    conj (U.1 0 1) = -U.1 1 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2_conj_apply_one_zero
declarations.doc:
Conjugating the lower left entry of an `SU(2)` matrix gives minus the upper right
one.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2_conj_apply_one_zero (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    conj (U.1 1 0) = -U.1 0 1

modules.title: The infinitesimal gauge action on the Higgs doublet
modules.doc:
The explicit `(1, 2)_{3}` action of the gauge algebra on the Higgs doublet, and its agreement
with the matter field.

## i. Overview

The infinitesimal `(1, 2)_{3}` action of the gauge algebra on the Higgs doublet is written out
here in the form used by physicists. The weak part of the algebra element acts on the weak index
and the hypercharge part scales, both through the physicists' factor of `i`, matching the group
action `u ^ 3 • U₂` infinitesimally. Section B checks that this is the action of the Lie algebra
on the matter field `HiggsVec.matterField`, which is defined abstractly as the derivative of the
group action, transported along the Lie algebra isomorphism `gaugeAlgebraEquiv`.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.HiggsVec.weakEnd` : the endomorphism of the Higgs doublet defined by a
  `2 × 2` matrix on the weak index.
- `StandardModel.HiggsVec.gaugeAlgebraAction` : the infinitesimal `(1, 2)_{3}` action of the
  gauge algebra.
- `StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_repAlgebra_gaugeAlgebraEquiv` : the action of the Lie
  algebra on the matter field of the Higgs, at the image of `c` under `gaugeAlgebraEquiv`, is
  `gaugeAlgebraAction c`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of the gauge algebra
- B. The action of the gauge algebra of the matter field

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The action of the gauge algebra
## B. The action of the gauge algebra of the matter field

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.weakEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the Higgs doublet defined by a `2 × 2` complex matrix acting on
the weak index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def weakEnd (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    HiggsVec →ₗ[ℂ] HiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.weakEnd_apply
declarations.doc: The weak endomorphism applies the matrix to the doublet.
declarations.statement:
lemma weakEnd_apply (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) (v : HiggsVec) :
    weakEnd A v = Matrix.toLpLinAlgEquiv 2 A v

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.weakEnd_add
declarations.doc: The weak endomorphism is additive in the matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma weakEnd_add (A B : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    weakEnd (A + B) = weakEnd A + weakEnd B

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.weakEnd_smul
declarations.doc: The weak endomorphism is complex-linear in the matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma weakEnd_smul (z : ℂ) (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    weakEnd (z • A) = z • weakEnd A

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.actionMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the infinitesimal `(1, 2)_{3}` action of a gauge algebra element on
the weak index, `i` times the weak part shifted by `i` times `3` the hypercharge.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def actionMatrix (c : GaugeAlgebra) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.gaugeAlgebraAction
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal action of the gauge algebra on the Higgs doublet, the derivative of the
`(1, 2)_{3}` action of the gauge group. It is real-linear in the algebra slot and
complex-linear in the value slot.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeAlgebraAction :
    GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] HiggsVec →ₗ[ℂ] HiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.valEnd_eq_weakEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the Higgs doublet induced by a matrix on the internal index, through
the identification `tensorEquiv`, is the weak endomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_eq_weakEnd (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    MatrixRep.valEnd tensorEquiv A = weakEnd A

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.derivMat_gaugeRep_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the action of the gauge algebra on the gauge representation of the Higgs,
at the image of `c` under `gaugeAlgebraEquiv`, is `actionMatrix c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_gaugeRep_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    derivMat gaugeRep (gaugeAlgebraEquiv c) = actionMatrix c

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_repAlgebra_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The action of the gauge algebra of the matter field of the Higgs, at the image of
`c` under `gaugeAlgebraEquiv`, is `gaugeAlgebraAction c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma matterField_repAlgebra_gaugeAlgebraEquiv (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    matterField.repAlgebra (gaugeAlgebraEquiv c) = gaugeAlgebraAction c

modules.title: The Higgs field as a matter field
modules.doc:
The Higgs doublet `(1, 2)_{3}` as a matter field of the Standard Model global gauge group.

## i. Overview

The target space `HiggsVec` is the Euclidean space `ℂ²`, already normed. The Higgs is a Lorentz
scalar, so its Lorentz representation is the trivial one on `ℂ`. The global gauge group acts on
it by the fundamental representation of the `SU(2)` block, twisted by the power `3` of the
hypercharge phase. This is the charge `3` twist of the fundamental representation of `SU(2)`,
which gives a bosonic matter field of mass weight two. Its action of the global gauge group, on
the image of `StandardModel.gaugeGroupEquiv`, is the existing action
`StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI`.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField` : the Higgs as a matter field of
  `StandardModel.globalGaugeGroup`.
- `StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_repAlgebra` : its action of the gauge algebra.
- `StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_rep_gaugeGroupEquiv` : its action of the gauge
  group is `StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI`.
- `StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_lorentzContinuous`,
  `StandardModel.HiggsVec.matterField_gaugeLorentzCommute` : its Lorentz action is continuous and
  commutes with its gauge action.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gauge representation
- B. The matter field

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The mixed gauge-fermion sector
modules.doc:
The gauge-fermion sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra, as a join of products.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

The field-strength towers are bosonic, so they commute with every fermion tower
(`LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_d`, `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_bard`, ...,
`LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_bare`). Consequently the gauge algebra
and the fermion algebra commute (`commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_fermionAlgebra`),
and so do their mass-weight submodules in either order
(`fermionMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le`). Feeding this into the abstract two-class
sector bound `sectorMassWeight_pair_le` gives the mixed `{gauge, fermion}` sector's
weight-`w` piece as (the join over splittings of `w` into non-zero parts of) products
of the gauge and fermion sectors' own mass-weight submodules
(`sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_le`).

Since a non-zero gauge weight is at least `4` and a non-zero fermion weight is at
least `3`, the mixed sector vanishes below weight `7`
(`sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_seven`) and at weight `8`
(`sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eight`), and at weight `7` is exactly the product of
the underived field-strength submodule with the underived fermion submodule
(`sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven`).

## ii. Key results

- `commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_fermionAlgebra` : the gauge algebra and the fermion algebra
  commute element-wise.
- `sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_le` : the mixed gauge-fermion sector as a join of products.
- `sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_seven`, `sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eight` :
  the mixed sector vanishes below weight `7` and at weight `8`.
- `sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven` : the mixed sector at weight `7` is exactly the product
  of the underived field strength with the underived fermion towers.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gauge and fermion algebras commute
- B. The mixed gauge-fermion sector

## iv. References

* None.
