## B. The mixed gauge-fermion sector

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_fermionAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The gauge algebra and the fermion algebra commute element-wise. Every generator of
the gauge algebra commutes with every generator of the fermion algebra by the
commutation rules `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_d`, ..., `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_bare`,
and commutation extends from generators to the algebras they generate.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.fermionMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le
declarations.doc:
The fermion sector's mass-weight submodules and the gauge sector's mass-weight
submodules commute past each other, in the order needed by
`sectorMassWeight_pair_le`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le (a b : ℕ) :
    FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule a * GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule b
      ≤ GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule b * FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule a

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_le
declarations.doc:
The mixed gauge-fermion sector decomposition. The weight-`w` piece of the
`{gauge, fermion}` sector lies in the join, over the splittings of `w` into two
non-zero parts, of the products of the gauge and fermion sectors' own mass-weight
submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_le (w : ℕ) :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} w
      ≤ ⨆ (p : ℕ × ℕ) (_ : p.1 + p.2 = w) (_ : p.1 ≠ 0) (_ : p.2 ≠ 0),
        GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule p.1 * FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule p.2

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_seven
declarations.doc:
The mixed gauge-fermion sector vanishes below weight `7`. A non-zero gauge
weight is at least `4` and a non-zero fermion weight is at least `3`, so no
splitting of a weight below `7` into two non-zero parts can supply both.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_seven {w : ℕ} (hw : w < 7) :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eight
declarations.doc:
The mixed gauge-fermion sector vanishes at weight `8`. The only splittings of
`8` into two non-zero parts with a non-zero gauge weight and a non-zero fermion
weight would need the gauge part to be `4` or `6` (with fermion part `4` or `2`), but
the fermion sector vanishes at both `4` and `2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eight :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} 8 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven
declarations.doc:
The mixed gauge-fermion sector at weight `7` is exactly the product of the
underived field-strength submodule with the underived fermion submodule, the only
splitting of `7` into a non-zero gauge weight and a non-zero fermion weight that
survives is `4 + 3`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} 7
      = GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0

modules.title: The gauge-fermion invariants below mass weight nine
modules.doc:
The gauge-fermion sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra carries no invariant.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

The mixed `{gauge, fermion}` sector is almost empty below weight nine, and what little
there is cannot be invariant. A field-strength tower weighs at least four and a fermion
tower at least three, so the sector vanishes below weight seven. At weight eight the two
splittings that arithmetic allows are `4 + 4` and `6 + 2`, and the fermion sector is
trivial at both four and two, so weight eight vanishes too. That leaves weight seven, the
single product `F ψ` of the underived field strength against the underived fermion towers.

Weight seven is barred from carrying an invariant by the same parity count on spin that
empties the Yukawa sector at weights five and seven. The field strength is of integer spin,
its two covector indices and its derivative slots all mixing by the Lorentz matrix and its
adjoint index not seeing the Lorentz group at all, while a fermion carries one Weyl-spinor
index. The one product at weight seven has exactly one fermion factor, so it is of
half-integer spin, and a half-integer spin carries no Lorentz invariant.

The machinery is the Yukawa sector's: `mul_le_centreEigenspace` multiplies the signs the
two factors carry at the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`, and
`mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one` turns the sign `-1` into the absence
of invariants modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule. Only the left-hand factor changes. The
Higgs sign `+1` is replaced by the gauge one, which is `+1` for the same reason.

The bound is `w < 9` rather than `w < 8`, since weight eight is as empty as the weights below
seven, so nothing is gained by stopping short of the first weight the sector can occupy.

## ii. Key results

- `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven_sup` : mass weight seven carries
  no Lorentz invariant, being of half-integer spin.
- `mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup` : below mass weight nine the
  sector carries no Lorentz invariant.
- `mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the
  classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence. An element of
  `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` is fixed by both groups exactly
  when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Integer field strength against half-integer fermion
- B. Mass weight seven
- C. The classification below mass weight nine

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Integer field strength against half-integer fermion

The signs the two factors carry at the centre are already proved: the field-strength
derivative submodules carry `+1`, every one of their indices being inert there, and the
fermion ones carry `-1`, the Weyl-spinor value index doing the work. The Lorentz action on
the covariant field algebra is by algebra maps, so the product carries `+1` times `-1`.

## B. Mass weight seven

Weight seven is the single product `F ψ`, the underived field strength against the
underived fermion towers. It has exactly one fermion factor, so section A gives it the sign
`-1`, and a subspace of sign `-1` carries no invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule.

## C. The classification below mass weight nine

The nine weights below nine are now settled. The sector vanishes below weight seven and
again at weight eight, and weight seven is section B. So below weight nine the
gauge-fermion sector supplies no invariant beyond what `S` already carries, and the
equivalences record it in the shape the other sectors carry, so that all of them can be
combined.

No lower bound on the weight is needed. The sector is the two-class sector of the gauge
and fermion generators, so both classes must be present with a non-zero weight and the
sector is already trivial at weight zero. The scalars, which force `0 < w` in the
gauge-sector statement, never appear.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight seven carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule. A
Lorentz invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} 7 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. The
weight is the underived field strength against the underived fermion towers, of half-integer
spin.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven_sup
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} 7
      ⊔ S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup
declarations.doc:
Below mass weight nine the gauge-fermion sector carries no Lorentz invariant. A
Lorentz invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` lies in `S`.
Weights below seven and weight eight are trivial submodules, and weight seven is section
B.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9)
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y
      ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} w
      ⊔ S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence, in the shape of the gauge-
and Yukawa-sector statements. An element of
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` is fixed by both groups
exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups. Gauge stability of `S` is
not needed, and neither is gauge invariance of `x`, since the forward direction is the sign at
the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`, which uses the Lorentz group alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. Below mass weight nine an element of
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of
`S` fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)

modules.title: The fermion sector
modules.doc:
The ten fermion towers of the Standard Model, their laws, and the submodules they span.

## i. Overview

The fermion sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`
consists of the three families of each of the ten fermion species, the five species and their
conjugates, indexed by ordered tuples of covariant-derivative directions. This file names the ten
towers (`d`, `bard`, `u`, `baru`, `Q`, `barQ`, `L`, `barL`, `e`, `bare`) and the gauge, Lorentz and
mass-weight actions on `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` (`repGauge`, `repLorentz`,
`massWeightPoly`), and records the laws they obey. Each family transforms under the global gauge
group through the dual of the species' gauge representation (the conjugate representation for the
barred fields), under the Lorentz group as the covariant derivatives of the species' Lorentz
representation, and each tower is a `massWeightPoly`-eigenvector of weight `3 + 2 * n` (mass
dimension `3/2 + n`). Any two fermionic towers anticommute, by
`GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covFermion_anticomm_covFermion` and its companions.

Each law is the corresponding law of the covariant towers of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`, so
nothing new is proved here beyond the assembly.

## ii. Key results

- `repGauge_d`, ..., `repGauge_bare` : gauge transformation of the towers through the dual of the
  species representations (conjugate for the barred fields).
- `repLorentz_d`, ..., `repLorentz_bare` : the Lorentz transformation of the towers.
- `massWeight_d`, ..., `massWeight_bare` : the mass weights `3 + 2 * n`.
- `fermionAlgebra` : the algebra generated by the ten fermion families and all their covariant
  derivatives.
- `derivSubmodule` : the submodule of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` generated by the fermion
  symbols carrying exactly `n` covariant derivatives.
- `anticomm_of_mem_derivSubmodule` : any two elements of the derivative submodules anticommute.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The towers and actions on the covariant field algebra
- B. The laws of the towers
- C. The fermion-derivative submodules

## iv. References

* None.

The algebra generated by the ten fermion families and all their covariant
derivatives.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fermionAlgebra : Subalgebra ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The submodule of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` generated by the fermion symbols carrying
exactly `n` covariant derivatives, the join, over the families and derivative slots, of the
ranges of the ten species' symbol maps.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivSubmodule (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.derivSubmodule_eq_span
declarations.doc: The derivative submodule as the span of the fermion symbol values.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_eq_span (n : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n = Submodule.span ℂ
      (⋃ (i : Fin 3) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        Set.range (d i l) ∪ Set.range (bard i l) ∪
        Set.range (u i l) ∪ Set.range (baru i l) ∪
        Set.range (Q i l) ∪ Set.range (barQ i l) ∪
        Set.range (L i l) ∪ Set.range (barL i l) ∪
        Set.range (e i l) ∪ Set.range (bare i l))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.derivSubmodule_le_span_kindGenerators
declarations.doc:
Every fermion derivative submodule lies in the span of the fermionic covariant generators,
each of its symbols being one.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_span_kindGenerators (n : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n ≤ Submodule.span ℂ (fieldData.kindGenerators .fermion)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.anticomm_of_mem_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Any two elements of the fermion derivative submodules anticommute. They are combinations of
fermionic covariant generators, which anticommute by
`GaugeFieldData.anticomm_of_mem_span_kindGenerators_fermion`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.derivSubmodule_mul_comm
declarations.doc:
The fermion derivative submodules commute with one another as submodules, the
sign from anticommutation is absorbed by the span.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_mul_comm (n m : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n * derivSubmodule m = derivSubmodule m * derivSubmodule n

modules.title: The components of the fermion symbols
modules.doc:
The components of the ten fermion symbols on a basis of their value spaces, and their gauge and
Lorentz transformation laws.

## i. Overview

The fermion sector of the covariant field algebra gives the ten species as linear maps out of
the dual of a value space. Fixing a basis of that value space turns each map into a finite
family of elements of the covariant field algebra, the components. This file records those
components and the transformation laws they carry.

Both laws are dictated by the variance. A symbol eats a covector, so it carries the
contragredient of its value space. Its gauge charges are the negatives of the value
space's, entering through the matrix entries of the inverse group element, transposed. The
barred species carry the conjugate on top of that, which stars every coefficient. On the
Lorentz side a right-handed value space contributes the entrywise conjugate of the inverse
matrix and a left-handed one the inverse matrix itself, with the conjugates swapping the
two.

## ii. Key results

- `dComponent` ... `bareComponent` : the components of the ten fermion symbols.
- `rep_dComponent` ... `rep_bareComponent` : the gauge transformation of a component,
  expanded over components.
- `repLorentz_dComponent` ... `repLorentz_bareComponent` : the Lorentz transformation of a
  component carrying no derivatives, expanded over components.
- `repGauge_gaugeTorusGen_dComponent` ... `repGauge_gaugeTorusGen_bareComponent` : the
  specialisation of the gauge law to the four torus generators, reproducing the weights
  already recorded for the fermion derivative submodules.
- `repGauge_su3_d`, `repGauge_su2_d`, `repGauge_u1_d` and their companions for the other nine
  species : the gauge law of each component read at the colour, isospin and hypercharge
  factors.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The components of the ten fermion symbols
- B. The gauge transformation of a component
- C. The Lorentz transformation of a component
- D. The torus specialisation and the recorded gauge weights
- E. The gauge laws of the components at each factor
  - E.1. The down singlet
  - E.2. The conjugate down singlet
  - E.3. The up singlet
  - E.4. The conjugate up singlet
  - E.5. The quark doublet
  - E.6. The conjugate quark doublet
  - E.7. The lepton doublet
  - E.8. The conjugate lepton doublet
  - E.9. The lepton singlet
  - E.10. The conjugate lepton singlet

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The components of the ten fermion symbols

Each species is evaluated on the dual basis of its value space. The generation index and
the derivative slots ride along untouched; the new index is the basis index of the value
space, which for the barred species is that of the conjugate basis.

## B. The gauge transformation of a component

A symbol eats a covector, so it carries the contragredient of its value space. The gauge
charges are the negatives of the value space's, and the coefficients are the matrix entries
of the inverse group element with its indices transposed. The barred species carry the
conjugate on top of that, which stars every coefficient. Colour mixes only the colour
index, weak isospin only the isospin index, and hypercharge is an overall scalar.

## C. The Lorentz transformation of a component

A tower with `n` covariant derivatives mixes into every assignment of `n` derivative
directions, so its Lorentz law is a sum over such assignments. At `n = 0` there is exactly
one assignment and the product of Lorentz factors is empty, leaving only the action on the
value index. That is the case recorded here. A right-handed value space contributes the
entrywise conjugate of the inverse matrix and a left-handed one the inverse matrix itself,
with the conjugate species swapping the two.

## D. The torus specialisation and the recorded gauge weights

Restricting the gauge law of section B to the four torus generators must return the gauge
weights already recorded for the fermion derivative submodules, the negative of the value
space's weight for an unbarred species, and the value space's own weight for a barred one.
The lemmas below derive exactly those weights from the full-group laws, so the variance of
section B and the weight bookkeeping of the derivative submodules agree.

## E. The gauge laws of the components at each factor

A gauge transformation is a triple, and each of the three index laws that classify a block
constrains one factor of it. So each of the ten symbols is read at each factor in turn:
colour moves only a colour index, isospin only an isospin index, and hypercharge is an
overall scalar whose power is the `6Y` of the species. A symbol eats a covector, so it
carries the contragredient of its value space. The unbarred species come out
anti-fundamental in colour and isospin and the barred ones fundamental, which is what makes
every conjugate pair a fundamental against an anti-fundamental.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.rep_dComponent
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformation of a down-singlet component. The colour index mixes by the
transposed `SU(3)` matrix of `g⁻¹`, scaled by the conjugate hypercharge factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_dComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGauge g (dComponent i l j) =
      ∑ c, (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 2 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2 c) • dComponent i l (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.rep_bardComponent
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformation of a conjugate down-singlet component has the coefficients of
the down-singlet law, conjugated.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_bardComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGauge g (bardComponent i l j) =
      ∑ c, star (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 2 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2 c) •
        bardComponent i l (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.rep_QComponent
declarations.doc:

transposed `SU(3)` matrix of `g⁻¹` and the isospin index by the transposed `SU(2)`

        QComponent i l (j.1, c, w)

lemma rep_barLComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 2) :
    repGauge g (barLComponent i l j) =
      ∑ w, star (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 3 * (g⁻¹).toSU2.1 j.2 w) •

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.rep_eComponent
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformation of a lepton-singlet component. Colour and isospin act
trivially, so the sum over components collapses to the conjugate hypercharge scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_eComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : Fin 2) :
    repGauge g (eComponent i l j) =
      (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 6 : ℂ) • eComponent i l j

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.rep_bareComponent
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformation of a conjugate lepton-singlet component has the scalar of the
lepton-singlet law, conjugated.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_bareComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : Fin 2) :
    repGauge g (bareComponent i l j) =
      star (star (g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 6 : ℂ) • bareComponent i l j

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.univ_derivIndex_zero
declarations.doc:
At zero covariant derivatives the assignments of derivative directions form a
one-element type, so the Lorentz law of a tower has a single term.
declarations.statement:
lemma univ_derivIndex_zero (l : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = {l}

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.repGauge_su3_d
declarations.doc:
A colour transformation moves the colour index of a down-singlet symbol by the
conjugate matrix, the index being anti-fundamental.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_d (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (f : Fin 3) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Fin 2) (c : Fin 3) :
    repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (dComponent f l (s, c))
      = ∑ a, conj (U.1 a c) • dComponent f l (s, a)

modules.title: The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` on the fermion sector
modules.doc:
The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `-1` on the fermion derivative submodules.

## i. Overview

The fermion symbols are the only Standard Model generators of half-integer spin, and this
file records what that costs them. The element `-1` of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on every fermion
derivative submodule by `-1`, where it acts on the Higgs and gauge ones by `+1`.

The mechanism is uniform across the ten species. A fermion symbol `d i l φ` carries `n`
covariant-derivative slots, each a four-vector index, and one value index in the dual of a
Weyl-based representation. The derivative slots see `-1` through the Lorentz matrix, which is
the identity there (`SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one`), so they do not move at all; the value
index sees it through `rep.dual`, and `repLorentzGroup_neg_one` says that the Weyl factor
turns it into a sign. `Invariants.range_le_centreEigenspace_neg_one` does this once for an
arbitrary symbol family; section A applies it to the ten species and section B joins them.

This is the half-integer-spin obstruction of `Invariants/CentreEigenspace.lean` in the form the
Yukawa and gauge-fermion classifications need. A product with an odd number of fermion factors
inherits the sign, and a subspace of sign `-1` carries no Lorentz invariant.

## ii. Key results

- `range_d_le_centreEigenspace`, ..., `range_bare_le_centreEigenspace` : the symbols of each of
  the ten species carry the sign `-1`.
- `derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace` : the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the fermion derivative
  submodules by `-1`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The ten species
- B. The fermion derivative submodules

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The ten species

Each species feeds `range_le_centreEigenspace_neg_one` with its own Lorentz law and the sign
of its value space. The five unbarred species are Weyl-valued and the five barred ones are
conjugate Weyl-valued; conjugation does not move a real sign, so all ten carry `-1`.

## B. The fermion derivative submodules

The derivative submodule is the join over the three families, the derivative slots and the ten
species of the ranges of section A, and an eigenspace is closed under joins.

modules.title: The gauge weight decomposition of the fermion sector
modules.doc:
The fermion derivative submodules decompose by gauge weight, with the weights of the ten species.

## i. Overview

The gauge torus acts diagonally on the basis of each fermion value space, with
weights given by the colour and isospin weights of the fundamental representations
and the species' hypercharge. Through the dual (and, for the barred species, the
conjugate-dual) this makes every symbol component a simultaneous eigenvector, and the
derivative submodules of the fermion sector decompose by gauge weight
(`derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight`), for every number of covariant derivatives.

## ii. Key results

- `derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight` : the gauge weight decomposition of the fermion derivative submodules,
  for any number of covariant derivatives.
- `derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_supp` : its support, the gauge weights of the ten species.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gauge weight decomposition of the derivative submodules
- B. The support of the decomposition

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The support of the decomposition

modules.title: The mass-weight grading of the fermion sector
modules.doc:
The mass-weight submodules of the fermion algebra, and their description up to weight eight.

## i. Overview

The elements of the fermion algebra of a given mass weight form a submodule. Mass weight is
twice the mass dimension, so that it is a natural number. A fermion tower `∇ⁿψ` with `n`
covariant derivatives has mass dimension `3/2 + n` and mass weight `3 + 2 * n`, and a term
of mass dimension four, as in the Lagrangian, has mass weight eight.

The fermion towers generate the fermion algebra, and `massWeightPoly` is a monomial on
each of them. The results of `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.HomogeneousGenerators` then describe
every mass-weight submodule. The submodules of weight at most eight are found by removing
the leftmost tower of each product, and weight eight collapses, by the commutation of the
derivative submodules, to the kinetic sector `derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 1`.

## ii. Key results

- `massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul` : removing the leftmost fermion tower.
- `massWeightSubmodule_eq` : the binary weight recursion.
- `massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot` : the weights `1`, `2` and `4` are empty.
- `massWeightSubmodule_three_eq` to `massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq` : the mass weights up to eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight submodules
- B. The fermion towers generate and have weight `3 + 2 * n`
- C. The weight decompositions
- D. Mass weights up to eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mass-weight submodules
## B. The fermion towers generate and have weight `3 + 2 * n`

## C. The weight decompositions

Every result here is a spanning statement. A submodule is a join of products of fermion
towers, in the order written. It says nothing about the products being nonzero or
independent.

## D. Mass weights up to eight

Each case removes the leftmost tower. The towers `ψ`, `∇ψ` and `∇∇ψ` have weights `3`, `5`
and `7`; the remaining weight is then read off from a smaller weight.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
All elements of the fermion algebra of mass weight exactly `w`, the intersection
of the algebra generated by the fermion towers with the part on which
`massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ w`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule (w : ℕ) :
    Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightPoly_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: An element of the weight-`w` submodule is a mass-weight eigenvector of weight `w`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.mem_fermionAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The weight-`w` submodule lies in the fermion algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_fermionAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule {w : ℕ} {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w) : x ∈ fermionAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc: The scalars have mass weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero : (1 : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ≤
    massWeightSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_mul_le
declarations.doc: Mass weights add under multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_mul_le (m n : ℕ) :
    massWeightSubmodule m * massWeightSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (m + n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.fermionAlgebra_eq_adjoin_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc: The fermion algebra is generated by the fermion towers of every derivative order.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionAlgebra_eq_adjoin_derivSubmodule :
    fermionAlgebra = Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      (⋃ n, (derivSubmodule n : Set fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightPoly_of_mem_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
`massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ (3 + 2 * n)` on the fermion towers with `n`
covariant derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_of_mem_derivSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ x ∈ derivSubmodule n, massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial (3 + 2 * n) x

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.derivSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: A fermion tower with `n` covariant derivatives has mass weight `3 + 2 * n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (3 + 2 * n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq
declarations.doc: Weight zero is the scalars, as every fermion tower has positive weight.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq : massWeightSubmodule 0 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq
declarations.doc:
The weight recursion. An element of positive mass weight `i` is a sum of single
fermion towers of weight `i` and of products of two elements of lower positive weights
summing to `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    massWeightSubmodule i
      = (⨆ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin i => 3 + 2 * (k : ℕ) = i),
          derivSubmodule (k : ℕ))
        ⊔ (⨆ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin i × Fin i => (p.1 : ℕ) + (p.2 : ℕ) = i),
            massWeightSubmodule (p.1 : ℕ) * massWeightSubmodule (p.2 : ℕ))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul
declarations.doc:
Removing the leftmost fermion tower. An element of positive weight `w` is a sum of
products of a tower `∇ⁿψ` of weight `3 + 2 * n ≤ w` with an element of the remaining
weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul (w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) :
    massWeightSubmodule w
      = ⨆ n ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun n => 3 + 2 * n ≤ w),
          derivSubmodule n * massWeightSubmodule (w - (3 + 2 * n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
The weights `1`, `2` and `4` are empty, since the tower weights `3, 5, 7, …` and their sums
only reach `0`, `3` and every weight from `5` on.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot {w : ℕ} (hw : ¬ (w = 0 ∨ w = 3 ∨ 5 ≤ w)) :
    massWeightSubmodule w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_one_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight one.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_one_eq : massWeightSubmodule 1 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_two_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight two.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_two_eq : massWeightSubmodule 2 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_three_eq
declarations.doc: Weight three is the underived fermion towers, as `ψ` leaves weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_three_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 3 = derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_four_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight four.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_four_eq : massWeightSubmodule 4 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_five_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight five is the once-derived fermion towers. `ψ` would leave weight two, which is
empty, and `∇ψ` leaves weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_five_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 5 = derivSubmodule 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_six_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight six is the products of two underived fermion towers. `ψ` leaves weight three,
which is `ψ`, and `∇ψ` would leave weight one, which is empty.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_six_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 6 = derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_seven_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight seven is the twice-derived fermion towers. `ψ` and `∇ψ` would leave weights
four and two, which are empty, and `∇∇ψ` leaves weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_seven_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 7 = derivSubmodule 2

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight eight is the products of an underived and a once-derived fermion tower, the
kinetic-term sector. `ψ` leaves `∇ψ`, `∇ψ` leaves `ψ`, and `∇∇ψ` would leave weight one,
which is empty. The two orders agree by `derivSubmodule_mul_comm`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 8 = derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 1

modules.title: The gauge weight decomposition of the fermion mass-weight submodules
modules.doc:
The gauge-singlet content of the fermion sector up to mass weight eight, the mass and kinetic
pairings of each species with its conjugate.

## i. Overview

Each mass-weight submodule of the fermion sector up to weight eight has an explicit
description in terms of the derivative submodules, and the derivative submodules carry
a gauge weight decomposition. Weights one, two and four are trivial, weights three, five and
seven are the towers with zero, one and two covariant derivatives, weight six is the product
of two underived towers, and weight eight is the kinetic sector.

No single fermion symbol is a gauge singlet, every species carrying a nonzero hypercharge, so
the towers of weights three, five and seven carry no gauge invariant modulo a gauge-stable
submodule (section C). Weights six and eight are products of two towers, and their weight-zero
pieces are the pairings of each species with its own conjugate (section B).

## ii. Key results

- `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix`, `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight` : the gauge weight
  decompositions of mass weights six and eight.
- `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero`, `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight_piece_zero` :
  their weight-zero pieces, the pairings of each species with its own conjugate.
- `mem_of_invariant_of_mem_derivSubmodule_sup` : a gauge invariant of a derivative submodule
  joined with a gauge-stable `S` lies in `S`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The decompositions at mass weights six and eight
- B. The weight-zero pieces
  - B.1. Infrastructure for the product weights six and eight
- C. Invariants modulo a gauge-stable submodule

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The decompositions at mass weights six and eight

The fermion mass-weight submodules that are products of two towers carry the product of the
gauge weight decompositions of their factors.
## B. The weight-zero pieces

### B.1. Infrastructure for the product weights six and eight

Mass weights six and eight are products of two fermion towers, and their weight-zero
piece is genuinely nontrivial: it is spanned by pairing each species with its own
conjugate (a mass term). Splitting the product decomposition down to the ten species
and discarding the non-conjugate pairings, whose hypercharges never cancel, takes the
infrastructure developed here.

## C. Invariants modulo a gauge-stable submodule

A submodule `S` closed under the gauge action can be discarded from a gauge-invariant
element: if `x` is gauge invariant and lies in a fermionic submodule joined with `S`, then
its fermionic part has to vanish and `x` already lies in `S`. The reason is the one behind
`derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero`: every one of the ten species carries a fixed nonzero
hypercharge, so no nonzero fermionic element is a gauge singlet.

The argument is the torus sieve `GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant`:
each piece of nonzero weight is scaled by a torus generator by a scalar other than one, so
modulo `S` an invariant lies in the weight-zero piece, and the weight-zero piece of a single
tower is trivial (`derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero`).

    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge (massWeightSubmodule 6)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.zero_not_mem_fermionGaugeWeights
declarations.doc:
Every gauge weight carried by a fermion symbol has nonzero hypercharge, since each of the
ten species has a fixed nonzero hypercharge, independent of colour, isospin and
family, and the barred species carry the negative of the unbarred one. So the zero
weight never occurs.
declarations.statement: lemma zero_not_mem_fermionGaugeWeights : (0 : GaugeWeight) ∉ fermionGaugeWeights

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece of the fermion derivative submodules is trivial. Unlike
the gauge sector, no single fermion symbol is a gauge singlet, since every one of the
ten species carries a fixed nonzero hypercharge. A gauge-invariant combination needs
at least two fermion insertions, which is why it is the mass weights six and eight,
the products of two towers, that carry the interesting weight-zero content.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero (n : ℕ) :
    (derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece 0 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.piece_sup_mul
declarations.doc:
If the left factor of a product decomposition is a join `VA ⊔ VB`, its weight-`w`
piece splits along the join.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_sup_mul {VA VB VC : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (dA : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VA) (dB : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VB)
    (dC : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VC) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup (d := dA) (d' := dB))
        (d' := dC)).piece w
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA) (d' := dC)).piece w
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dB) (d' := dC)).piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.piece_mul_sup
declarations.doc:
If the right factor of a product decomposition is a join `VA ⊔ VB`, its weight-`w`
piece splits along the join.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_mul_sup {VA VB VC : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (dC : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VC) (dA : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VA)
    (dB : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGauge VB) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dC)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup (d := dA) (d' := dB))).piece w
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dC) (d' := dA)).piece w
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dC) (d' := dB)).piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.mul_piece_zero_eq_bot_of_hypercharge
declarations.doc:
Two decompositions with constant, non-cancelling hypercharge across their whole
supports have a trivial product at weight zero, since a weight from one can never cancel
a weight from the other.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:
lemma rangeGaugeWeightE_mul_speciesGaugeWeight_piece_zero {n m : ℕ} (f f' : Fin 3)
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightE f l)
        (d' := speciesGaugeWeight f' l')).piece 0
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightE f l)
        (d' := rangeGaugeWeightBarE f' l')).piece 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarE_mul_speciesGaugeWeight_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
Against the full symbol set of a family, the `bare` symbols reach gauge weight zero only

declarations.statement:
lemma rangeGaugeWeightBarE_mul_speciesGaugeWeight_piece_zero {n m : ℕ} (f f' : Fin 3)
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightBarE f l)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece of the product of two families' full symbol sets collapses
to the ten conjugate pairings, since every other combination of species has hypercharges
that cannot cancel.
declarations.statement:
lemma speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero {n m : ℕ} (f f' : Fin 3) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := speciesGaugeWeight f l)
        (d' := speciesGaugeWeight f' l')).piece 0
      =
      (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightD f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightBarD f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightBarD f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightD f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightU f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightBarU f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightBarU f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightU f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightQ f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightQ f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightL f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightBarL f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightBarL f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightL f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightE f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightBarE f' l')).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := rangeGaugeWeightBarE f l)
            (d' := rangeGaugeWeightE f' l')).piece 0

modules.title: The kinetic terms of the fermion sector
modules.doc:
The package that turns a kinetic block of the fermion sector into its kinetic term and the
reduction of the block to it.

## i. Overview

The invariants of the fermion sector at mass weight eight are the kinetic terms, and this
file builds them. A kinetic term pairs a species with its own conjugate, one of the two
carrying a covariant derivative, and joins their indices in the only ways available. The
colour indices by the Kronecker delta, the isospin indices by the Kronecker delta, and the
four-vector index against the two opposite-chirality spinor indices by the conjugate Pauli
matrices. That last contraction is `ψ̄ σ̄^μ ∂_μ ψ`.

Ten blocks arise, the five conjugate pairs each with the derivative on one factor or the
other, and they differ only in which indices their symbols carry. So the work is done once,
generically, in terms of `InvariantReductionToSpan`: a `KineticBlock` packages a
block together with its three classification steps — colour, isospin, Lorentz — and from
that package alone come the contraction, its invariance under both groups, and the reduction
of the block down to the line through it. The ten blocks are then ten instantiations.

The three stages are the same three the Yukawa sector runs, in the same order, and for the
same reason: each contraction is a spectator of the ones after it. Where a block's symbols
carry no colour index — the two lepton-doublet blocks and the two lepton-singlet ones — the
colour stage is `InvariantReductionToSpan.ofFixedFamily` rather than a classification, and
likewise for isospin where the symbols carry none. That keeps all ten blocks in one shape.

The ten blocks themselves are built in `KineticTerms`, which instantiates the package.

## ii. Key results

- `KineticBlock` : one kinetic block of the fermion sector, together with the three classifications
  its indices admit.
- `KineticBlock.reducesInvariantsTo` : the block span reduces to the span of its kinetic term.
- `KineticBlock.repGauge_kineticTerm`, `KineticBlock.repLorentz_kineticTerm` : the kinetic term
  is gauge and Lorentz invariant.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The once-derived chiral component families
- B. Products of two components
- C. The kinetic block package

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The once-derived chiral component families

A tower with one covariant derivative mixes into every assignment of one derivative
direction, so its Lorentz law is a sum over such assignments, with one column of the
Lorentz matrix per slot. The value index is untouched by that sum. It still moves by the
contragredient action, exactly as at zero derivatives. Composing the two gives the laws
`repLorentz_leftComp_deriv_one` and `repLorentz_rightComp_deriv_one`, the derivative slot
fundamental and the spinor slot dual.

## B. Products of two components

A block is a product of two components, and each of its index laws comes from the laws of
the two factors. The representation respects multiplication, so the two transform
independently and their coefficients multiply. Which slot of the classifier a factor
occupies is decided by its variance, the fundamental one going first, so each law comes in
two arrangements according to which factor is the barred one.

## C. The kinetic block package

A kinetic block is classified in three stages, and every block runs the same three: colour,
then isospin, then Lorentz, each contraction a spectator of the ones after it. `KineticBlock`
packages a block together with the three steps, and from the package alone come the kinetic
term, its invariance under both groups, and the reduction of the block to the line
through it.

The colour and isospin indices of the block are listed in the order the classifiers read
them, fundamental first; a block whose symbols carry no colour, or no isospin, simply
ignores the corresponding pair and supplies `InvariantReductionToSpan.ofFixedFamily` for that
stage. Each step comes with the fact that its contraction lies in the submodule it classifies, which
is what carries the invariance of one stage through the stages after it.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.repLorentz_symbol_deriv_one
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz transformation of a symbol with one covariant derivative. The derivative
slot moves by the columns of the Lorentz matrix and the value index by the
contragredient action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_symbol_deriv_one {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    {X : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hX : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz rep X) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repLorentz Λ (X ![μ] φ)
      = ∑ ν, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • X ![ν] (rep.dual Λ φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.repLorentz_component_deriv_one
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz transformation of a component of a once-derived symbol, when the
coordinate functionals `c` are permuted by the contragredient action with coefficients
`m`. This is the once-derived form of the laws of `Components`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.repLorentz_leftComp_deriv_one
declarations.doc:
Every undotted component family carries a four-vector index and a dual undotted
spinor index, at one covariant derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_leftComp_deriv_one (i : LeftIdx) :
    ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (leftComp ![μ] i a)
      = ∑ ν, ∑ β, ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) * (Λ⁻¹).1 a β) •
        leftComp ![ν] i β

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.repLorentz_rightComp_deriv_one
declarations.doc:
Every dotted component family carries a four-vector index and a dual dotted spinor
index, at one covariant derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_rightComp_deriv_one (i : RightIdx) :
    ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (rightComp ![μ] i a)
      = ∑ ν, ∑ β, ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) * star ((Λ⁻¹).1 a β)) •
        rightComp ![ν] i β

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_mul
declarations.doc:
A product of a component with a fundamental colour index and one with an
anti-fundamental colour index carries one colour index of each kind.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_mul
    {A C : Fin 3 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hA : ∀ (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c : Fin 3),
      repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (A c) = ∑ a, U.1 a c • A a)
    (hC : ∀ (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c : Fin 3),
      repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (C c) = ∑ a, conj (U.1 a c) • C a) :
    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGauge.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => A (l 0) * C (l 1)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_mul_swap
declarations.doc: The same with the two factors exchanged, the anti-fundamental one first.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_mul_swap
    {A C : Fin 3 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hA : ∀ (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c : Fin 3),
      repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (A c) = ∑ a, conj (U.1 a c) • A a)
    (hC : ∀ (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c : Fin 3),
      repGauge ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (C c) = ∑ a, U.1 a c • C a) :
    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGauge.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => A (l 1) * C (l 0)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_mul
declarations.doc:
A product of a component with a fundamental isospin index and one with an
anti-fundamental isospin index carries one isospin index of each kind.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_mul
    {A C : Fin 2 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hA : ∀ (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (w : Fin 2),
      repGauge ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (A w) = ∑ a, V.1 a w • A a)
    (hC : ∀ (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (w : Fin 2),
      repGauge ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (C w) = ∑ a, conj (V.1 a w) • C a) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGauge.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => A (l 0) * C (l 1)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_mul_swap
declarations.doc: The same with the two factors exchanged, the anti-fundamental one first.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_mul_swap
    {A C : Fin 2 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hA : ∀ (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (w : Fin 2),
      repGauge ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (A w) = ∑ a, conj (V.1 a w) • A a)
    (hC : ∀ (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (w : Fin 2),
      repGauge ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (C w) = ∑ a, V.1 a w • C a) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGauge.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => A (l 1) * C (l 0)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.repGauge_mul_fixed
declarations.doc:
A product of two components that a gauge transformation fixes is fixed by it. This is the form
in which a block whose symbols carry no colour, or no isospin, supplies the corresponding
stage.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_mul_fixed
    {g : GaugeGroupI} {a c : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (ha : repGauge g a = a)
    (hc : repGauge g c = c) :
    repGauge g (a * c) = a * c

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.repGauge_mul_smul_fixed
declarations.doc:
A product of two components that a gauge transformation scales by reciprocal scalars
is fixed by it. This is the form in which the hypercharges of a species and its conjugate
cancel.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_mul_smul_fixed
    {g : GaugeGroupI} {z z' : ℂ} {a c : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hz : z * z' = 1)
    (ha : repGauge g a = z • a) (hc : repGauge g c = z' • c) :
    repGauge g (a * c) = a * c

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isEquivariant_upDownRDownL_sum
declarations.doc:
A finite sum of families carrying one four-vector index and a pair of dual
opposite-chirality Weyl indices is such a family again, the colour and isospin
contractions are Lorentz spectators.

    {T : ι → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hT : ∀ i, complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.up, .downR, .downL] repLorentz
      (liftComponents (T i ∘ dualIndexEquiv))) :

      (liftComponents ((fun p => ∑ i, T i p) ∘ dualIndexEquiv))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.KineticBlock
declarations.doc:
One kinetic block of the fermion sector, together with the three classifications its
indices admit. The block is indexed by the derivative direction, the pair of spinor
indices in the order `(undotted, dotted)`, the pair of colour indices and the pair of
isospin indices, each pair in the order `(fundamental, anti-fundamental)`.
declarations.statement:
structure KineticBlock where
  /-- The components of the block. -/
  blk : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → B
  /-- The colour stage. At fixed derivative, spinor and isospin indices the colour pair is
    classified, by the delta contraction if the block carries colour and trivially if it
    does not. -/
  colourStep : ∀ (q : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2) (w w' : Fin 2),
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ => repGauge (U, 1, 1))
      (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => blk q l (n 0) (n 1) w w'))
  /-- The colour contraction lies in the span of the components it contracts. -/
  colourStep_mem : ∀ q l w w', (colourStep q l w w').spanningVector
    ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => blk q l (n 0) (n 1) w w')
  /-- The isospin stage, applied to the colour contraction. -/
  isospinStep : ∀ (q : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ => repGauge (1, V, 1))
      (Submodule.span ℂ
        (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => (colourStep q l (n 0) (n 1)).spanningVector))
  /-- The isospin contraction lies in the span of the colour contractions. -/
  isospinStep_mem : ∀ q l, (isospinStep q l).spanningVector
    ∈ Submodule.span ℂ
      (Set.range fun n : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => (colourStep q l (n 0) (n 1)).spanningVector)
  /-- The Lorentz stage, applied to the doubly contracted block, one four-vector index
    against a dual dotted and a dual undotted spinor index. -/
  lorentzStep : InvariantReductionToSpan (fun Λ : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz Λ)
    (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun p : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      (isospinStep p.1 p.2).spanningVector))
  /-- The Lorentz contraction lies in the span of the isospin contractions. -/
  lorentzStep_mem : lorentzStep.spanningVector
    ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun p : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      (isospinStep p.1 p.2).spanningVector)
  /-- A hypercharge transformation fixes every component of the block, the hypercharges of
    a species and its conjugate cancelling. -/
  hyper : ∀ (t : unitary ℂ) q l c c' w w',
    repGauge ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI) (blk q l c c' w w') = blk q l c c' w w'

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.KineticBlock.kineticTerm
declarations.doc:
The kinetic term of a block, the conjugate Pauli contraction of its doubly contracted
form, which is `ψ̄ σ̄^μ ∂_μ ψ` with the colour and isospin indices already joined.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def kineticTerm : B

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.KineticBlock.blockSpan

The join, over the derivative, spinor and isospin indices, of the colour spans of the
block, the span the block submodule is reduced from.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def blockSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.KineticBlock.reducesInvariantsTo

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.KineticBlock.kineticTerm_mem

contraction lies in the span of the objects of the stage before it.

The kinetic term is fixed by the colour factor, since the colour contractions are, and every
later stage stays inside their span.

The kinetic term is fixed by the hypercharge factor, the hypercharges of a species and
its conjugate cancelling on every component of the block.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.KineticBlock.repGauge_kineticTerm
declarations.doc:
The kinetic term is gauge invariant. A gauge transformation is the product of its
colour, isospin and hypercharge parts, and each fixes it.
declarations.statement: lemma repGauge_kineticTerm (g : GaugeGroupI) : repGauge g K.kineticTerm = K.kineticTerm

declarations.doc:
The kinetic term is Lorentz invariant, being the conjugate Pauli contraction of a
vector dual left-right Weyl family.
declarations.statement:

    repLorentz Λ K.kineticTerm = K.kineticTerm

modules.title: The ten kinetic blocks
modules.doc:
The ten kinetic blocks of the fermion sector, each a conjugate pair with one covariant
derivative, as instances of `KineticBlock`.

## i. Overview

The five conjugate pairs of the fermion sector, each with the covariant derivative on one
factor or the other, give ten blocks at mass weight eight, and each is packaged here as a
`KineticBlock` of `KineticFamilies`. The package does the work; what a block has to supply
is its components, the three index laws they obey, and the cancellation of the two
hypercharges.

The blocks differ only in which indices their symbols carry. The four quark-singlet
pairings `d ∂ bard`, `bard ∂ d`, `u ∂ baru` and `baru ∂ u` run a genuine colour stage and a
trivial isospin one; the two quark-doublet pairings `Q ∂ barQ` and `barQ ∂ Q` run both; the
two lepton-doublet pairings run a trivial colour stage and a genuine isospin one; and the
two lepton-singlet pairings run neither, their two symbols carrying only hypercharge and a
spinor index between them. In every case the unbarred symbol is anti-fundamental and the
barred one fundamental, since a symbol eats a covector and so carries the contragredient of
its value space; that is what makes each conjugate pair a fundamental against an
anti-fundamental, and it is the same fact that makes the two spinor indices of a pair
opposite in chirality.

What comes out of each block is one kinetic term per pair of generations. The join of the
ten over the nine generation pairs is the kinetic span of the sector, assembled in
`MassDimEight`.

## ii. Key results

- `dbardKineticBlock`, `barddKineticBlock`, `ubaruKineticBlock`, `baruuKineticBlock`,
  `QbarQKineticBlock`, `barQQKineticBlock`, `LbarLKineticBlock`, `barLLKineticBlock`,
  `ebareKineticBlock`, `bareeKineticBlock` : the ten kinetic blocks.
- `dbardBlk` and its nine companions : the components of each block, an underived symbol against
  a once-derived symbol of the conjugate species.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The four quark-singlet pairings
- B. The two quark-doublet pairings
- C. The two lepton-doublet pairings
- D. The two lepton-singlet pairings

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The four quark-singlet pairings

The down and up singlets carry colour and hypercharge and nothing else, so their four
pairings run a genuine colour stage and a trivial isospin one.

## B. The two quark-doublet pairings

The quark doublet carries colour, isospin and hypercharge, so its two pairings are the only
blocks that run both a colour and an isospin stage.

## C. The two lepton-doublet pairings

The lepton doublet carries isospin and hypercharge but no colour, so its colour stage is
the trivial one.

## D. The two lepton-singlet pairings

The lepton singlet carries only hypercharge and a spinor index, so both gauge stages are
trivial and the whole classification is the Lorentz one.

modules.title: The kinetic terms at mass weight eight
modules.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of the fermion sector at mass weight eight, the kinetic terms.

## i. Overview

Mass weight eight is the first weight at which the fermion sector carries an invariant,
and what it carries is the kinetic terms. The submodule is
`derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 1`, one underived tower against one once-derived one,
and the single derivative is exactly what mass weight six was missing. It supplies a
four-vector index, and a four-vector index together with a dotted and an undotted spinor
index has one invariant contraction, against the conjugate Pauli matrices. That
contraction is `ψ̄ σ̄^μ ∂_μ ψ`.

The classification runs the four stages every sector runs. Hypercharge first, through the
gauge weight decomposition, where `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight_piece_zero` cuts the
hundred pairings of two fermion symbols down to the ten conjugate ones, every other
pairing having hypercharges that cannot cancel. Then colour, then isospin, then Lorentz,
one classification each, chained by the `ReducesInvariantsTo` relation of
`PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.InvariantReduction` and supplied by the `KineticBlock` packages of
`KineticTerms`. What is left is the kinetic span: one term for each of the ten pairings and each of
the nine pairs of generations.

## ii. Key results

- `dbardPairSubmodule` and its nine companions : the submodule of each block of a generation pair.
- `kineticSpan` : the join of the kinetic terms over the ten conjugate pairings and the nine
  pairs of generations.
- `reducesInvariantsTo_kineticSpan` : the fermion sector at mass weight eight reduces to the
  kinetic span.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the classification at mass
  weight eight as an equivalence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Symbol ranges and their stability
- B. The block submodules
- C. The symbol ranges inside the derivative submodules, and the mass weight
- D. The kinetic span
- E. The blocks reduce to the kinetic terms
- F. The classification as an equivalence

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Symbol ranges and their stability

The reduction asks two things of the submodule a block is read from: that the two groups
carry it into itself, and that it lies in the span of the block's components. Both come
from the symbol maps. A gauge transformation moves only the covector a symbol is evaluated
at, so a symbol range is gauge stable at any number of derivative slots. The Lorentz group
moves the covector too, but it also mixes the derivative slots, so an underived range is
Lorentz stable on its own while a once-derived one is stable only after joining over the
derivative direction — which is why a block submodule carries that join.

## B. The block submodules

Each of the ten conjugate pairings gives one submodule per pair of generations: the
underived range of one species against the once-derived ranges of its conjugate, joined
over the derivative direction so that the Lorentz group has somewhere to move it. Each is
carried into itself by both groups and lies in the span of the components of the matching
kinetic block, which is all the reduction asks.

## C. The symbol ranges inside the derivative submodules, and the mass weight

An underived symbol range lies in `derivSubmodule 0` and a once-derived one in
`derivSubmodule 1`, so every component of a kinetic block is a product of the two, which
is `massWeightSubmodule 8`. Each stage of a block's classification stays inside the span
of the stage before it, so the kinetic term is there too.

## D. The kinetic span

The kinetic span of the fermion sector at mass weight eight is the join, over the ten
conjugate pairings and the nine pairs of generations, of the lines through the kinetic
terms. Each generator is a gauge and Lorentz invariant of mass weight eight, which is the
easy direction of the classification and what makes it an equivalence rather than an
inclusion.

## E. The blocks reduce to the kinetic terms

The weight-zero piece of the gauge weight decomposition lies in the join of the ten block
submodules, hypercharge having already cut the hundred pairings down to ten; and each
block reduces to its kinetic term, by the three stages its `KineticBlock` package supplies.
Joining the ten and then the nine generation pairs is `ReducesInvariantsTo.sup` and
`ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup`, which is where the stability of the blocks and of the kinetic span is
spent.

## F. The classification as an equivalence

The two directions meet. Forwards, hypercharge puts a gauge invariant in the weight-zero
piece (`GaugeWeightDecomposition.reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero`), and section E reduces
that to the kinetic span. Backwards, the kinetic span is a space of gauge and Lorentz
invariants of mass weight eight (section D), which turns the reduction into an equivalence.

So the fermion sector at mass weight eight carries exactly the kinetic terms — one for
each species, each pair of generations and each placement of the derivative — and nothing
else. Compare mass weight six, where the same argument leaves nothing at all. Without a
derivative there is no four-vector index for the conjugate Pauli matrices to carry, and
the Dirac mass term does not exist.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isStableUnder_iSup_range_deriv_one
declarations.doc:
The join, over the derivative direction, of the ranges of a once-derived symbol map is
carried into itself by the Lorentz group. A Lorentz transformation mixes the derivative
slot into the other directions and moves the covector, and both stay inside the join.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isStableUnder_range_underived
declarations.doc: The range of an underived symbol map is carried into itself by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_range_underived {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℂ M]
    {ρG : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI M} {ρL : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) M}
    {F : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ M →ₗ[ℂ] fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hG : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ M),
      repGauge g (F (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) φ)
        = F (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ρG.dual g φ))
    (hL : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz ρL F) :
    IsStableUnder (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz)
      (LinearMap.range (F (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.isStableUnder_iSup_range_derived
declarations.doc:
The join, over the derivative direction, of the ranges of a once-derived symbol map is
carried into itself by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_iSup_range_derived {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℂ M]
    {ρG : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI M} {ρL : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) M}
    {F : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ M →ₗ[ℂ] fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hG : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ M),
      repGauge g (F ![μ] φ) = F ![μ] (ρG.dual g φ))
    (hL : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz ρL F) :
    IsStableUnder (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz)
      (⨆ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, LinearMap.range (F ![μ]))

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification of mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of the
sibling sectors. An element of `massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S` is fixed by both groups
exactly when it is a combination of the kinetic terms up to a remainder in `S` fixed by
both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ kineticSpan

modules.title: The invariants below mass weight eight
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The fermion sector carries nothing invariant below mass weight eight. Weights one, two
and four are trivial submodules and weights three, five and seven are single fermion
towers, which carry a nonzero hypercharge and so no gauge singlet. That leaves mass
weight six, the products of two underived towers, and it is the interesting one: it is
where a Dirac mass term `ψ̄ ψ` would sit, and the statement proved here is that no such
term exists.

The two symmetries cooperate. Gauge invariance cuts the hundred pairings of two fermion
symbols down to the ten conjugate ones, `d bard`, `bard d`, `u baru`, ..., `bare e`,
every other pairing having hypercharges that cannot cancel. This is
`massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero` of the gauge weight decomposition. Each
surviving pairing is then a product of two symbols of opposite chirality, one dotted and
one undotted, since a species and its conjugate always sit in opposite Weyl
representations. A pair of opposite-chirality spinor indices with nothing else to
contract against admits no invariant at all — `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_upR_eq_bot`
— so each pairing contributes nothing and mass weight six is left empty.

That is the absence of a Dirac mass term in the Standard Model, and it is why the fermion
masses have to come from the Yukawa sector instead. The Higgs doublet supplies the missing
index, and its own mass weight makes the Yukawa terms weight eight.

The products of opposite-chirality one-index families, `Lorentz.isEquivariant_downLDownR_mul`
and its swap, live in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Metric`; they take
the chirality law of each factor, contragredient to the left-handed Weyl representation or to
its conjugate. The chirality bookkeeping
of the species is done once here and reused at mass weight eight, in `MassDimEight`, which
imports this file. The five undotted species are indexed by
`LeftIdx` and the five dotted ones by `RightIdx`, and `leftComp` and `rightComp` list
their components with the spinor index singled out.

The final statement `mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`
needs `0 < w` as well as `w < 8`. At `w = 0` the mass-weight submodule contains the
scalars, so `1` is an invariant of weight zero lying in no `S`.

## ii. Key results

- `leftComp`, `rightComp` : the components of the five undotted and the five dotted species,
  presented as two-element families in the spinor index.
- `mem_of_invariant_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleSix_sup` : mass weight six carries no invariant,
  there being no Dirac mass term.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the classification below
  mass weight eight as an equivalence. An element of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8`
  is fixed by both groups exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The five undotted and the five dotted species
- B. The ranges of the symbol maps inside the chirality spans
- C. Mass weight six with no Dirac mass term
- D. The classification below mass weight eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The five undotted and the five dotted species

Each of the ten fermion species sits in one of the two Weyl representations, and a
species and its conjugate always sit in opposite ones. The five undotted species are
`bard`, `baru`, `Q`, `L` and `bare`, the five dotted ones `d`, `u`, `barQ`, `barL` and
`e`. Indexing each list by the generation and the remaining internal indices, `leftComp`
and `rightComp` present every fermion component as a two-element family in its spinor
index, which is the shape the chirality laws `repLorentz_leftComp` and `repLorentz_rightComp`
are stated in.

## B. The ranges of the symbol maps inside the chirality spans

A symbol map is determined by its values on a basis of the dual of its value space, so
its range is the join of the lines through its components
(`LinearMap.range_eq_iSup_span_coord`).
Collecting the ten ranges into the two chirality spans is then a matter of naming the
right index.

## C. Mass weight six with no Dirac mass term

Gauge invariance is what selects the conjugate pairings. A gauge-invariant element lies
in the weight-zero piece of the gauge weight decomposition, and modulo a gauge-stable
submodule the same holds with the submodule joined on. The torus generators scale every
other weight, and `GaugeWeightDecomposition.reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero` deletes them
one piece at a time. Unlike the single-tower case, the generator has to be chosen weight by
weight, since a product like `Q barQ` at two different colours has vanishing hypercharge and
nonzero colour, so no one generator sees every weight.

Mass weight six is the product of two underived fermion towers. Gauge invariance puts
such an invariant in the weight-zero piece, which `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero`
writes as the ten conjugate pairings, and every one of those is an undotted
component times a dotted one. `Lorentz.isEquivariant_downLDownR_mul` turns each into a dual
left-right Weyl family and `Lorentz.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span`
peels the lot off, leaving nothing.

The physics is that the Standard Model has no Dirac mass term. A mass term pairs a
left-handed field with a right-handed one, and while such a pair is exactly what survives
the gauge cut, its two spinor indices have nothing to contract against. A dotted index
and an undotted one carry no invariant pairing, and only the symplectic form pairs two indices
of the same chirality. The fermion masses have to come from somewhere else, and they do,
from the Yukawa sector, where the Higgs doublet supplies the missing index.

## D. The classification below mass weight eight

The seven weights between zero and eight are now settled. Weights one, two and four are
trivial submodules, weights three, five and seven are single fermion towers and carry a
nonzero hypercharge, and weight six is section F. So between weight zero and weight eight
the fermion sector has no invariant beyond what `S` already supplies, and the equivalence
records it.

The lower bound `0 < w` cannot be dropped. Weight zero contains the scalars by
`one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero`, and `1` is fixed by both groups, the two
representations being multiplicative, without lying in any given `S`.
