declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleSix_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight six carries no invariant modulo a stable submodule, there being no Dirac
mass term. A gauge- and Lorentz-invariant element of `massWeightSubmodule 6 ⊔ S` lies
in `S`, gauge invariance cutting the hundred pairings of two fermion symbols down to
the ten conjugate ones and Lorentz invariance killing each of those, its two spinor
indices being of opposite chirality.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleSix_sup
    {S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hS : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra), y ∈ S → repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule 6 ⊔ S)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.mem_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup
declarations.doc:
Between mass weight zero and mass weight eight the fermion sector carries no
invariant. An element of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` fixed by both
groups lies in `S`. Weights one, two and four are trivial, weights three, five and
seven carry no gauge singlet, and weight six is the missing Dirac mass term.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup (w : ℕ) (hw0 : 0 < w)
    (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of
`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`. An element of
`massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is
itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups. The span of invariants that the weight
eight statement leaves over is here the trivial one, so `x - y` lies in it exactly when
`x = y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. Below mass weight eight an element
of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of `S` fixed by both
groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)

modules.title: The mixed gauge-Higgs sector
modules.doc:
The gauge-Higgs sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra, as a join of products.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

The field-strength towers are bosonic, so they commute with every Higgs tower
(`LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_H`, `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_barH`). Consequently the gauge
algebra and the Higgs algebra commute (`commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_higgsAlgebra`), and so do
their mass-weight submodules in either order (`higgsMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le`). Feeding
this into the abstract two-class bound `sectorMassWeight_pair_le` gives the mixed `{gauge, scalar}`
sector's weight-`w` piece as a join, over the splittings of `w` into two non-zero parts, of products
of the two sectors' own mass-weight submodules (`sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_le`).

Both a non-zero gauge weight and a non-zero Higgs weight are even, and they are at
least `4` and `2` respectively. So the mixed sector vanishes below weight `6` and at
every odd weight. At weight `6` it is exactly the underived field strength against the
underived Higgs, and at weight `8` it is bounded by the field strength against the
weight-four Higgs terms together with the once-derived field strength against the
underived Higgs.

## ii. Key results

- `commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_higgsAlgebra` : the gauge algebra and the Higgs algebra
  commute element-wise.
- `sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_le` : the mixed gauge-Higgs sector as a join of products.
- `sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six`, `sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight` : the mixed sector at
  weights six and eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mixed gauge-Higgs sector

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mixed gauge-Higgs sector

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc: The gauge algebra and the Higgs algebra commute element-wise.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.higgsMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le
declarations.doc: The Higgs and gauge mass-weight submodules commute past each other.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le (a b : ℕ) :
    ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule a * GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule b
      ≤ GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule b * ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule a

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_le
declarations.doc: The mixed gauge-Higgs sector decomposition.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_le (w : ℕ) :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} w
      ≤ ⨆ (p : ℕ × ℕ) (_ : p.1 + p.2 = w) (_ : p.1 ≠ 0) (_ : p.2 ≠ 0),
        GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule p.1 * ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule p.2

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eq_bot_of_lt_six
declarations.doc: The mixed gauge-Higgs sector vanishes below weight `6`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eq_bot_of_lt_six {w : ℕ} (hw : w < 6) :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_seven
declarations.doc:
The mixed gauge-Higgs sector vanishes at weight `7`, since both a gauge weight and a
Higgs weight are even, so they cannot sum to an odd number.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_seven :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} 7 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six
declarations.doc:
The mixed gauge-Higgs sector at weight `6` is exactly the product of the
underived field strength with the underived Higgs, the only surviving splitting being
`4 + 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} 6
      = GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_le_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs
declarations.doc:
A product of a gauge-weight piece and a Higgs-weight piece lands in the mixed
sector of the total weight.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight
declarations.doc:
The mixed gauge-Higgs sector at weight `8`. The surviving splittings are
`4 + 4` and `6 + 2`, giving the field strength against the weight-four Higgs terms
and the once-derived field strength against the underived Higgs.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} 8
      = GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 1
        ⊔ GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0
          * ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0
        ⊔ GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 1 * ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0

modules.title: The gauge-Higgs invariants below mass weight nine
modules.doc:
The gauge-Higgs sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra carries no invariant.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

The mixed `{gauge, scalar}` sector is small, and none of it is invariant. A field-strength
tower weighs at least four and a Higgs tower at least two, and both weights are even, so
the sector vanishes below weight six and at every odd weight, weight seven included. What
is left is weight six, the underived field strength against the underived Higgs, and
weight eight, that same field strength against the weight-four Higgs terms, together with
the once-derived field strength against the underived Higgs.

None of it can carry an invariant, and the reason is an index count. The Higgs is a Lorentz
scalar, so an underived Higgs symbol has no covector index at all and is fixed by the whole
Lorentz group, while a once-derived one carries a single index, its derivative slot. The
covector indices of these products are therefore those of the field strength — two when it
is underived and three when it is once derived — plus at most one from the Higgs.

Two indices admit exactly one invariant contraction, the metric trace, and it vanishes, since the
metric is symmetric in the pair of indices in which `GaugeSector.F_antisymm` says the
field strength is antisymmetric. Three indices admit no invariant contraction at all, the
metric tying two and the Levi-Civita symbol four. Weight six and the two-Higgs term of
weight eight are of the first kind and the other two terms of weight eight of the second,
so at no weight below nine does the sector add an invariant to what is already there.

Neither count needs the gauge group, and neither needs a basis of the Higgs. The families
being peeled are indexed by a covector of the gauge algebra together with a piece of Higgs
material, and neither index is finite; section A peels a join over an arbitrary index type
by passing to a finite subset of it, which is all an element of a join ever needs.

The bound is `w < 9` rather than the gauge sector's `w < 8`, weight eight being as empty of
invariants as the weights below it. No lower bound on `w` is needed either. The sector is
the two-class sector of the gauge and Higgs generators, so both classes must be present
with a non-zero weight and the scalars, which force `0 < w` in the gauge-sector statement,
never appear.

## ii. Key results

- `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_rankTwo_span` : a Lorentz invariant of a join, over an arbitrary
  index type, of the spans of bi-Lorentz families with vanishing metric traces lies in the stable
  submodule it is taken modulo.
- `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six_sup`,
  `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight_sup` : mass weights six and eight
  carry no Lorentz invariant.
- `mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the
  classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Peeling a join over an arbitrary index
- B. The underived Higgs is Lorentz inert
- C. Field strengths against Higgs material
- D. Mass weights six and eight
- E. The classification below mass weight nine

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Peeling a join over an arbitrary index

The gauge sector combines the reductions of a join of spans indexed by a finite set, which
is what its twelve directions of the gauge algebra need. Here the families are indexed by a
covector of the gauge algebra together with a piece of Higgs material, and neither index is
finite. Nothing is lost: an element of a join lies in the join over finitely many of the
summands, so `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup` combines the reductions over the whole join, by
way of `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup_of_biSup`. The rest of the section collects the
stability and the inertness of products and joins that section D consumes.

## B. The underived Higgs is Lorentz inert

The Higgs is a Lorentz scalar, and an underived symbol has no derivative slot for the
Lorentz matrix to act on, so it is fixed outright — and with it every element of the
submodule the underived symbols span.

## C. Field strengths against Higgs material

Three products have to be classified. An underived field strength against inert material is
a bi-Lorentz family whose metric trace vanishes with the antisymmetry of the field strength;
a once-derived one against inert material is a triple Lorentz family; and an underived one
against a once-derived Higgs is a triple Lorentz family as well, the Higgs supplying the
third index. The last is the only one in which a Higgs index moves at all.

## D. Mass weights six and eight

Weight six is a single product and section C settles it outright. Weight eight is a join of
three, and they are peeled one at a time, the two not yet peeled joining the error term —
which asks that they be Lorentz stable. The gauge and Higgs derivative submodules are, and
so are their products and joins.

## E. The classification below mass weight nine

The nine weights below nine are now settled: the sector vanishes below weight six and at
weight seven, and weights six and eight are section D. So below weight nine the gauge-Higgs
sector supplies no invariant beyond what `S` already carries, and the equivalences record it
in the shape the other sectors carry, so that all of them can be combined.

declarations.name: StandardModel.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_rankTwo_span
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz invariant of a join, over an arbitrary index type, of the spans of
bi-Lorentz families with vanishing metric traces lies in the stable submodule it is taken
modulo. Each span reduces to the line through its metric contraction, which is zero; the
reductions combine over every finite set of indices, and so over the whole join.

declarations.name: StandardModel.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_rankThree_span
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz invariant of a join, over an arbitrary index type, of the spans of triple Lorentz
families lies in the stable submodule it is taken modulo, since three covector indices admit no
invariant contraction at all, so each span reduces to `⊥`, and the reductions combine over every
finite set of indices, and so over the whole join.

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_eq_self_of_mem_mul
declarations.doc: A product of two pointwise Lorentz-inert submodules is pointwise Lorentz inert.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_eq_self_of_mem_mul
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {V W : Submodule ℂ B} (hV : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz g y = y)
    (hW : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ W, repLorentz g y = y) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ∀ y ∈ V * W, repLorentz g y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_mem_mul_of_stable
declarations.doc: A product of two Lorentz-stable submodules is Lorentz stable.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mem_mul_of_stable
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {V W : Submodule ℂ B} (hV : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz g y ∈ V)
    (hW : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ W, repLorentz g y ∈ W) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ∀ y ∈ V * W, repLorentz g y ∈ V * W

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_mem_of_fixed
declarations.doc: A pointwise Lorentz-inert submodule is Lorentz stable.

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_mem_sup_of_stable
declarations.doc: A join of two Lorentz-stable submodules is Lorentz stable.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mem_sup_of_stable {V W : Submodule ℂ B}
    (hV : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz g y ∈ V)
    (hW : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ W, repLorentz g y ∈ W) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ∀ y ∈ V ⊔ W, repLorentz g y ∈ V ⊔ W

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentz_eq_self_of_mem_higgs_derivSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc:
The underived Higgs and conjugate-Higgs symbols are Lorentz scalars with no derivative
slot to rotate, so every element of the weight-two Higgs submodule is fixed by the whole
Lorentz group.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_fixed_sup
declarations.doc:
An underived field strength against Lorentz-inert material carries no Lorentz
invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_fixed_sup
    (C : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hC : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ C, repLorentzGroup g y = y)
      (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * C ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_one_mul_fixed_sup
declarations.doc:
A once-derived field strength against Lorentz-inert material carries no Lorentz
invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_one_mul_fixed_sup
    (C : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hC : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ C, repLorentzGroup g y = y)
      (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 1 * C ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_higgsOrConj_deriv_one
declarations.doc:
The once-derived Higgs and conjugate-Higgs symbols, read as one family indexed by the
derivative direction, transform as a Lorentz vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_higgsOrConj_deriv_one
    (j : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec ⊕ Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec))
    (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup g (Sum.elim (fun φ => higgsField ![μ] φ)
      (fun ψ => conjHiggsField ![μ] ψ) j)
      = ∑ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          Sum.elim (fun φ => higgsField ![ν] φ)
            (fun ψ => conjHiggsField ![ν] ψ) j

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.fieldStrengthHiggsDerivFamily
declarations.doc:
The underived field strength against a once-derived Higgs or conjugate-Higgs symbol, as a
family of three covector indices, the two of the field strength and the derivative direction
of the Higgs.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fieldStrengthHiggsDerivFamily
    (i : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra ×
      (Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec ⊕ Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)))
    (l : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_up_fieldStrengthHiggsDerivFamily
declarations.doc: The underived field strength against a once-derived Higgs is a triple Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_up_fieldStrengthHiggsDerivFamily
    (i : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra ×
      (Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec ⊕ Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec))) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 3 => .up) repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents (fieldStrengthHiggsDerivFamily i))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_derivSubmodule_one_le_iSup_span
declarations.doc:
An underived field-strength symbol times the once-derived Higgs submodule lies in the join
of the spans of the families `fieldStrengthHiggsDerivFamily`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_derivSubmodule_one_le_iSup_span (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 1
      ≤ Submodule.comap (LinearMap.mulLeft ℂ (gaugeFieldStrength ![] μ ν φ))
        (⨆ i, Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (fieldStrengthHiggsDerivFamily i)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_higgs_one_sup
declarations.doc:
An underived field strength against a once-derived Higgs carries no Lorentz invariant
modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule, since three covector indices admit no contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_higgs_one_sup
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ GaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 1 ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight six carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule. A
Lorentz invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar} 6 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. The weight is
the underived field strength against the underived Higgs, whose two covector indices are
contracted only by the metric, and that trace vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six_sup
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} 6 ⊔
      S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight eight carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule. A
Lorentz invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar} 8 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. The three
products making up the weight are peeled off one at a time, the two carrying three
covector indices by the absence of any contraction and the one carrying two by the
vanishing of the metric trace.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight_sup
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} 8 ⊔
      S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup
declarations.doc:
Below mass weight nine the gauge-Higgs sector carries no Lorentz invariant. A Lorentz
invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` lies in `S`. Weights
below six and weight seven are trivial submodules, and weights six and eight are the two
index counts.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9)
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y
      ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} w ⊔
      S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence, in the shape of the gauge-
and Yukawa-sector statements. An element of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar} w ⊔ S` for
`w < 9` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both
groups. Gauge stability of `S` is not needed, and neither is gauge invariance of `x`, since the
forward direction is the index count, which uses the Lorentz group alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. Below mass weight nine an element of
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar} w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of `S`
fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)

modules.title: The gauge sector
modules.doc:
The field-strength towers of the Standard Model, their laws, and the submodules they span.

## i. Overview

The gauge sector of the covariant field algebra of the Standard Model is generated by the
field-strength towers `gaugeFieldStrength`, indexed by ordered tuples of
covariant-derivative directions, two covector indices and a functional on the gauge algebra.
They transform under the global gauge group through the adjoint action on the dual value index,
under the Lorentz group as the covariant derivatives of a two-index Lorentz tensor, they
commute with one another, are antisymmetric in the two covector indices, and each tower is a
`massWeightPoly`-eigenvector of weight `2 * (2 + n)` (mass dimension `2 + n`).
In prose the tower `gaugeFieldStrength` is written `F`.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.gaugeFieldStrength` : the field strength and its covariant derivatives.
- `GaugeSector.repGauge_F`, `GaugeSector.repLorentz_F`, `GaugeSector.massWeight_F`,
  `GaugeSector.F_comm_F`, `GaugeSector.F_antisymm` : the laws of the field-strength towers.
- `GaugeSector.gaugeAlgebra` : the algebra generated by the field strength and all its
  covariant derivatives.
- `GaugeSector.gluonField`, `GaugeSector.wField`, `GaugeSector.hyperchargeField` : the gluon,
  `W`-boson and hypercharge contributions to the field strength and its covariant derivatives.
- `GaugeSector.derivSubmodule` : the span of the field-strength symbols with `n` covariant
  derivatives.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The field-strength towers and their laws
- B. The individual gauge-group contributions to the field strength
- C. The field-strength derivative submodules
  - C.1. Commutativity of the derivative submodules
  - C.2. Closure of the derivative submodules under the gauge and Lorentz groups

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The field-strength towers and their laws

## B. The individual gauge-group contributions to the field strength

The field-strength symbol family `gaugeFieldStrength` packages together the contributions of
the three factors of the gauge group. Evaluating it on the coordinate of `GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis`
dual to a Gell-Mann direction, a Pauli direction, or the `u(1)` direction isolates the
gluon, `W`-boson, and hypercharge contributions individually.
## C. The field-strength derivative submodules
### C.1. Commutativity of the derivative submodules
### C.2. Closure of the derivative submodules under the gauge and Lorentz groups

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.gaugeFieldStrength
declarations.doc:
The field-strength towers of the covariant field algebra of the Standard Model, indexed by
functionals on the gauge algebra `GaugeAlgebra`, transported along `gaugeAlgebraEquiv` from those
on the Lie algebra of the global gauge group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeFieldStrength {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_F
declarations.doc:
The field strength transforms under the global gauge group through the adjoint action on its
dual value index.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_F (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ) =
      gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν ((GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repLorentz_F
declarations.doc:
The field-strength towers transform under the Lorentz group as the covariant derivatives of a
two-index Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_F (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    repLorentzGroup Λ (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ) =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        (∏ i, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 (p i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
      ∑ a, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
      ∑ b, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 b ν : ℝ) : ℂ) • gaugeFieldStrength p a b φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeight_F
declarations.doc: Each field-strength tower with `n` covariant derivatives has mass weight `2 * (2 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeight_F {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    massWeightPoly (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ) =
      Polynomial.monomial (2 * (2 + n)) (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.F_comm_F
declarations.doc: The gauge sector is bosonic, any two field-strength towers commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma F_comm_F {n m : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ' ν' : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ψ' : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    Commute (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν ψ) (gaugeFieldStrength l' μ' ν' ψ')

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.F_antisymm
declarations.doc: The field strength is antisymmetric in its two covector indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma F_antisymm {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    gaugeFieldStrength l ν μ φ = - gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gaugeAlgebra
declarations.doc: The algebra generated by the field strength and all its covariant derivatives.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeAlgebra : Subalgebra ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gluonField
declarations.doc:
The gluon contribution to the field strength (and its covariant derivatives), the
field-strength symbol evaluated on the coordinate dual to the `a`-th Gell-Mann
direction of the standard basis of the gauge algebra, i.e. the `su(3)` factor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gluonField {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (a : Fin 8) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.wField
declarations.doc:
The `W`-boson contribution to the field strength (and its covariant derivatives),
the field-strength symbol evaluated on the coordinate dual to the `i`-th Pauli
direction of the standard basis of the gauge algebra, i.e. the `su(2)` factor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def wField {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (i : Fin 3) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeField
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge contribution to the field strength (and its covariant derivatives),
i.e. the `B`-boson contribution, the field-strength symbol evaluated on the coordinate
dual to the single basis direction of the `u(1)` factor of the standard basis of the
gauge algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def hyperchargeField {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The submodule of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` generated by the field-strength symbols
carrying exactly `n` covariant derivatives, the join, over the derivative slots and the two
covector indices, of the ranges of the symbol maps.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivSubmodule (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.commute_of_mem_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The gauge sector is bosonic, so any element of a derivative-`n` submodule commutes with any
element of a derivative-`m` submodule. This extends `F_comm_F` from generators to the
submodules that they span.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_mem_derivSubmodule {n m : ℕ} {x y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ derivSubmodule n) (hy : y ∈ derivSubmodule m) : Commute x y

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.derivSubmodule_mul_comm
declarations.doc:
The derivative-`n` and derivative-`m` submodules commute with one another as submodules
of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`, since every pair of their elements commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_mul_comm (n m : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n * derivSubmodule m = derivSubmodule m * derivSubmodule n

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.derivSubmodule_map_repGauge_le
declarations.doc:
The image of a derivative-`n` submodule under a gauge transformation lies inside the
same submodule. Each generator `gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ` is sent by `repGauge_F` to another
generator `gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ'` with the same derivative slots and covector
indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_map_repGauge_le (n : ℕ) (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    (derivSubmodule n).map (repGaugeGroupI g) ≤ derivSubmodule n

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.derivSubmodule_map_repLorentz_le
declarations.doc:
The image of a derivative-`n` submodule under a Lorentz transformation lies inside the
same submodule, since `repLorentz_F` expands each generator into a finite linear combination of
generators with the same number `n` of derivative slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_map_repLorentz_le (n : ℕ) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    (derivSubmodule n).map (repLorentzGroup Λ) ≤ derivSubmodule n

modules.title: The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` on the gauge sector
modules.doc:
The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `+1` on the field-strength derivative submodules.

## i. Overview

The field strength is of integer spin, so the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on its derivative
submodules by `+1`. Every index a field-strength symbol carries — the two covector indices and
the covariant-derivative slots — mixes by the Lorentz matrix, and the adjoint value index does
not see the Lorentz group at all; since `-1` covers the identity Lorentz transformation
(`SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one`), nothing moves.

This is the integer-spin half of the parity count the gauge-fermion classification runs.
Paired with `FermionSector.derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace`, which gives the fermions
`-1`, it makes the product `F ψ` carry `-1`, and a subspace of sign `-1` carries no Lorentz
invariant.

Unlike the Higgs and fermion towers, the field-strength symbols are not of the shape
`IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms` describes — they carry two covector indices beside their
derivative slots — so the collapse at the centre is run directly on `repLorentz_F`.

## ii. Key results

- `repLorentz_neg_one_F` : a field-strength symbol is fixed by the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`.
- `span_range_F_le_centreEigenspace` : the span of a field-strength symbol family carries the sign
  `+1`.
- `derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace` : the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the field-strength
  derivative submodules by `+1`, for any number of covariant derivatives.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The field-strength symbols
- B. The field-strength derivative submodules

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The field-strength symbols

At the centre each of the three sums of `repLorentz_F` is a sum against a row of the identity
matrix, so each collapses to its diagonal term and the symbol is returned unchanged.

## B. The field-strength derivative submodules

The derivative submodule is the join of the symbol spans over the derivative slots and the two
covector indices, and an eigenspace is closed under joins.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repLorentz_neg_one_F
declarations.doc:
A field-strength symbol is fixed by the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`, since all of its indices mix by
the Lorentz matrix, which is the identity there.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_neg_one_F {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) : repLorentzGroup (-1) (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ) =
      gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.span_range_F_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: The span of a field-strength symbol family carries the sign `+1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_range_F_le_centreEigenspace {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν))
      ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentzGroup 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the field-strength derivative submodules by `+1`, for
any number of covariant derivatives. The field strength is of integer spin and every one of
its indices is inert at the centre.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace (n : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentzGroup 1

modules.title: The mass-weight grading of the gauge sector
modules.doc:
The mass-weight submodules of the gauge algebra, and their description up to weight eight.

## i. Overview

The elements of the algebra generated by the field strength, the gauge sector of the covariant
field algebra of the Standard Model, of a given mass weight form a submodule. Mass weight is
twice the mass dimension. A field-strength tower `∇ⁿF` with `n` covariant derivatives has
mass dimension `2 + n` and mass weight `2 * (2 + n)`, and a term of mass dimension four, as
in the Lagrangian, has mass weight eight.

The field-strength towers generate the gauge algebra, and `massWeightPoly` is a monomial on
each of them. The results of `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.HomogeneousGenerators` then describe
every mass-weight submodule. The submodules of weight at most eight are found by removing
the leftmost tower of each product; weight eight is the `∇∇F` and `F · F` sectors.

## ii. Key results

- `massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul` : removing the leftmost field-strength tower.
- `massWeightSubmodule_eq` : the binary weight recursion.
- `massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot` : the odd weights and the weight two are empty.
- `massWeightSubmodule_four_eq` to `massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq` : the mass weights up to eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight submodules
- B. The field-strength towers generate and have weight `2 * (2 + n)`
- C. The weight decompositions
- D. Mass weights up to eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mass-weight submodules
## B. The field-strength towers generate and have weight `2 * (2 + n)`

## C. The weight decompositions

Every result here is a spanning statement. A submodule is a join of products of
field-strength towers, in the order written.

## D. Mass weights up to eight

Each case removes the leftmost tower. The towers `F`, `∇F` and `∇∇F` have weights `4`, `6`
and `8`; the remaining weight is then read off from a smaller weight.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
All elements of the gauge algebra of mass weight exactly `w`, the intersection of
the algebra generated by the field-strength towers with the part on which
`massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ w`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule
  (w : ℕ) :
    Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightPoly_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: An element of the weight-`w` submodule is a mass-weight eigenvector of weight `w`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The weight-`w` submodule lies in the gauge algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule {w : ℕ} {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w) : x ∈ gaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc: The scalars have mass weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero : (1 : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ≤
    massWeightSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_mul_le
declarations.doc: Mass weights add under multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_mul_le (m n : ℕ) :
    massWeightSubmodule m * massWeightSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (m + n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gaugeAlgebra_eq_adjoin_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The gauge algebra is generated by the field-strength towers of every derivative
order.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAlgebra_eq_adjoin_derivSubmodule :
    gaugeAlgebra = Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      (⋃ n, (derivSubmodule n : Set fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightPoly_of_mem_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
`massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ (2 * (2 + n))` on the field-strength towers with
`n` covariant derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_of_mem_derivSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ x ∈ derivSubmodule n, massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial (2 * (2 + n)) x

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.derivSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
A field-strength tower with `n` covariant derivatives has mass weight
`2 * (2 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (2 * (2 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq
declarations.doc: Weight zero is the scalars, as every field-strength tower has positive weight.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq : massWeightSubmodule 0 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq
declarations.doc:
The weight recursion. An element of positive mass weight `i` is a sum of single
field-strength towers of weight `i` and of products of two elements of lower positive
weights summing to `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    massWeightSubmodule i
      = (⨆ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin i => 2 * (2 + (k : ℕ)) = i),
          derivSubmodule (k : ℕ))
        ⊔ (⨆ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin i × Fin i => (p.1 : ℕ) + (p.2 : ℕ) = i),
            massWeightSubmodule (p.1 : ℕ) * massWeightSubmodule (p.2 : ℕ))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul
declarations.doc:
Removing the leftmost field-strength tower. An element of positive weight `w` is a sum
of products of a tower `∇ⁿF` of weight `2 * (2 + n) ≤ w` with an element of the
remaining weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul (w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) :
    massWeightSubmodule w
      = ⨆ n ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun n => 2 * (2 + n) ≤ w),
          derivSubmodule n * massWeightSubmodule (w - 2 * (2 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
The weights `1`, `2`, `3`, `5` and `7` are empty, since the tower weights `4, 6, 8, …` and
their sums only reach `0` and the even weights from `4` on.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_bot {w : ℕ} (hw : ¬ (w = 0 ∨ (4 ≤ w ∧ w % 2 = 0))) :
    massWeightSubmodule w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_one_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight one.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_one_eq : massWeightSubmodule 1 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_two_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight two.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_two_eq : massWeightSubmodule 2 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_three_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight three.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_three_eq : massWeightSubmodule 3 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_four_eq
declarations.doc: Weight four is the underived field-strength towers, as `F` leaves weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_four_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 4 = derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_five_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight five.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_five_eq : massWeightSubmodule 5 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_six_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight six is the once-derived field-strength towers, as `F` would leave weight two,
which is empty, and `∇F` leaves weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_six_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 6 = derivSubmodule 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_seven_eq
declarations.doc: There is nothing of weight seven.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_seven_eq : massWeightSubmodule 7 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight eight is the twice-derived field-strength towers together with the products
of two underived ones, the `∇∇F` and `F · F` sectors. `F` leaves weight four, which is
`F`, `∇F` would leave weight two, which is empty, and `∇∇F` leaves weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 8 = derivSubmodule 2 ⊔ derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0

modules.title: Products of two field strengths as bi-adjoint gauge tensors
modules.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of the gauge sector at mass weight eight, the kinetic and theta
terms of the three gauge groups.

## i. Overview

A single field-strength symbol of the gauge sector carries one adjoint index of the gauge
algebra, so a product of two of them carries two. Restricting the value index to one
factor of the gauge group turns such a product into a family indexed by two adjoint
indices of that factor, and the gauge transformation law `repGauge_F` says exactly that
the maps of these families out of the tensors with two adjoint indices are equivariant
(`ColourAdjAdj.of_law`, `IsospinAdjAdj.of_law`), and for hypercharge the family is fixed
outright. The gauge invariant these laws supply is the trace contraction,
the Kronecker contraction of the two adjoint indices, the familiar kinetic pairing of two
field strengths; it has mass weight eight and is fixed by the whole gauge group.

Conversely every twice-derived field strength and every product of two underived ones,
sorted by gauge factor, is a component of a gluon or `W`-boson pair family, a hypercharge
invariant, or a family carrying an unpaired adjoint index of a non-abelian factor, which
contributes nothing by `ColourAdj.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` and
`IsospinAdj.reducesInvariantsTo_bot`. Putting the two
directions together classifies the gauge invariants of mass weight eight modulo any
gauge-stable submodule. Such an invariant is a combination of the three underived trace
contractions and the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths. Both shapes carry four
covector indices and no others, so both are quadruple Lorentz tensors, and the Lorentz
classification cuts the combinations down further, to the four Lorentz contractions of
each of the four families. All four families are antisymmetric in their last two slots, by
`F_antisymm`, and that leaves two contractions of each, eight spanning generators in all
(`lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`).

Both classifications are reductions in the sense of `ReducesInvariantsTo`, stated modulo
any stable submodule. The converse is that each span consists of invariants of mass weight
eight already, the gauge one because its generators are fixed by the gauge group and carry
the right mass weight, and the Lorentz one because it sits inside the gauge span and is
spanned by contractions that `RankFour` shows to be Lorentz invariant. Section J composes
the two reductions and puts the two directions together as the equivalences
`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff` and
`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`, the second also with the
eight generators, `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_reduced`.

## ii. Key results

- `lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq` : the Lorentz contraction span is spanned by eight of its
  sixteen generators, for each family the `(0,2)(1,3)` metric contraction and the Levi-Civita
  contraction.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff` : the gauge classification of mass weight
  eight as an equivalence.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the gauge and Lorentz
  classification of mass weight eight as an equivalence, with the four Lorentz contractions of
  the four families of section H.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_reduced` : the same
  equivalence with the eight generators of `lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Spans and stability
- B. The gauge transformation of the gauge-factor field strengths
- C. Products of two underived field strengths as bi-adjoint families
- D. The families of mass weight eight
- E. Mass weight eight inside the family spans
- F. The unpaired non-abelian adjoint indices
- G. The gauge invariants of mass weight eight
- H. The Lorentz classification of the mass-weight eight invariants
- I. The Lorentz contraction span as invariants of mass weight eight
- J. The classifications as equivalences

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Spans and stability

Every subspace in this file is spanned by a finite family. Where a classifier supplies or
consumes it, it is written `Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)`; where a family of lines is
collected, it is the join `⨆ i, ℂ ∙ T i`, and `Submodule.span_range_eq_iSup` passes between
the two. A join of lines lies in a submodule as soon as its generators do, and a linear map
fixing each generator fixes it pointwise; a linear map moving each generator to a
combination of the generators carries the span into itself.

The classification runs through `ReducesInvariantsTo`. Each bi-adjoint family's span
reduces, for its factor of the gauge group, to the line through its trace contraction, and
each adjoint family's span to `⊥`; `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup` joins the families of one
kind, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.sup` joins the kinds.

## B. The gauge transformation of the gauge-factor field strengths

The gauge law `repGauge_F` moves the field-strength symbol by the coadjoint action of
the gauge group on its argument, which on the standard basis coordinates is the adjoint
matrix. That matrix is block diagonal, so the gluon field strengths transform among
themselves by the `su(3)` adjoint matrix of the colour factor, the `W`-boson field
strengths by the `su(2)` adjoint matrix of the isospin factor, and the hypercharge field
strength is fixed. The colour factor alone fixes the `W`-boson field strengths as well.

## C. Products of two underived field strengths as bi-adjoint families

A product of two underived field strengths of one gauge factor, at the four covector
indices `p`, is a family indexed by the two adjoint indices of that factor, and by section
B and the multiplicativity of the gauge action it obeys the transformation law of a tensor
with two adjoint indices (`repGaugeGroupI_gluonPair_eq_sum`, `repGaugeGroupI_wPair_eq_sum`,
`repGaugeGroupI_hyperchargePair`), at every gauge element and not only at those of its own
factor. Its trace contraction, the Kronecker contraction of the two adjoint indices, is fixed by the
whole
gauge group and has mass weight eight, the sum of the mass weights of its two factors; so
is the twice-derived hypercharge field strength, the other shape of mass weight eight.

## D. The families of mass weight eight

Mass weight eight is the twice-derived field strengths together with the products of two
underived ones (`massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq`), and each field-strength symbol is a
combination of its values on the twelve coordinates of the standard basis of the gauge
algebra: eight gluon, three `W`-boson and one hypercharge direction. Sorting the symbols and
their products by gauge factor gives five kinds of family.

- Two gluon symbols form a component of a gluon pair family, and two `W`-boson symbols one of
  a `W`-boson pair family, the bi-adjoint families of section C.
- Two hypercharge symbols form a hypercharge trace contraction, and a twice-derived
  hypercharge symbol is a twice-derived hypercharge field strength; both are fixed by the
  whole gauge group.
- A gluon symbol, alone or against a symbol of another factor, carries an unpaired `su(3)`
  adjoint index. These are the colour families, whose maps out of `SuT[3, .adj]` are
  equivariant: the colour factor moves the gluon index and fixes the other factor.
- A `W`-boson symbol, alone or against a hypercharge symbol, carries an unpaired `su(2)`
  adjoint index. These are the isospin families, with maps out of `SuT[2, .adj]`.

## E. Mass weight eight inside the family spans

A derivative submodule lies in a submodule as soon as the symbols on the twelve standard
coordinates do, by `F_mem_iSup_span_coord`. Sorting the twice-derived symbols and the
products of two underived ones by gauge factor, as in section D, bounds mass weight eight by
the joins of the unpaired families together with the pair spans, the hypercharge trace
contractions and the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths.

## F. The unpaired non-abelian adjoint indices

A family carrying one unpaired adjoint index of a non-abelian factor has no gauge invariant
in its span at all, the adjoint representations of `su(3)` and `su(2)` having no invariant
vector: `ColourAdj.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` and its `su(2)` twin reduce such a span to
`⊥` for that factor. The colour families are reduced first, with the isospin join carried
in the target, since the colour factor fixes every isospin family; the isospin families
are reduced after that.

## G. The gauge invariants of mass weight eight

Section E bounds mass weight eight by the unpaired joins, the two non-abelian pair spans and
the two hypercharge spans. Section F reduces the unpaired joins to `⊥`. Each pair span
reduces to its trace contractions by `ColourAdjAdj.reducesInvariantsTo_span_traceContraction` and
its `su(2)` twin, and the
two hypercharge spans are fixed pointwise by the gauge group and reduce to themselves.
`ReducesInvariantsTo.sup` joins the parts, asking stability of every part but the first and
of the target; no independence of the parts is needed.

The section closes with the converse, that the gauge span is made of gauge invariants of mass
weight eight already.

## H. The Lorentz classification of the mass-weight eight invariants

A product of two underived field-strength symbols carries four covector indices and
nothing else, so as a family indexed by those four it is a quadruple Lorentz tensor in the
sense that its map out of `ℂT(fun _ : Fin 4 => .up)` is equivariant: `repLorentz_F` at no covariant
derivatives moves each covector index by the Lorentz matrix of the `SL(2,ℂ)` element, and
`repLorentzGroup_mul` carries that
through the product. The three trace contractions are sums of such products over a gauge
index, and a finite sum of quadruple Lorentz tensors is one again. So is the twice-derived
hypercharge field strength, whose two derivative slots and two covector indices are four
four-vector indices as well. The four spans of section G are exactly the spans of these
four families, and `ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor` reduces each, for the
Lorentz group, to the span of its four contractions.

What is left is spanned by the four Lorentz contractions of each family,
`liftComponents T (RankFour.contractionTensor i)`: the metric contractions of the slot pairs
`(0,1)(2,3)`, `(0,2)(1,3)` and `(0,3)(1,2)` and the Levi-Civita contraction. These are
sixteen spanning vectors, `lorentzContractionEightSpan`, which is the output of the
classification.

Half of them are redundant. In each of the four families the last two slots are the two
covector indices of one field strength: of the second factor for the three trace families,
and of the only factor, after the two derivative slots, for the twice-derived hypercharge
field strength. So `F_antisymm` makes each family antisymmetric under exchanging slots `2` and
`3` (`gluonTrace_comp_swap_two_three` and its three companions), and
`RankFour.span_range_contractionTensor_of_antisymm` then removes two contractions of each.
The `(0,1)(2,3)` contraction vanishes, and the `(0,3)(1,2)` one is minus the `(0,2)(1,3)`
one (`quadContractionSpan_eq_of_antisymm`). Eight spanning vectors remain
(`lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`).

* six underived ones, quadratic in the field strengths. For each of the gluon, `W`-boson and
  hypercharge trace families these are the `(0,2)(1,3)` metric contraction, of the kinetic
  shape `η^{μρ} η^{νσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}`, and the Levi-Civita contraction, of the theta shape
  `ε^{μνρσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}`, the gauge index summed in both;
* two linear in the twice-derived hypercharge field strength, `η^{μρ} η^{νσ} ∇_μ ∇_ν B_{ρσ}`
  and `ε^{μνρσ} ∇_μ ∇_ν B_{ρσ}`.

Each is the plain component sum of `RankFour.liftComponents_contractionTensor`, repeated
indices summed, against the integer metric `diag(1,-1,-1,-1)` or the symbol taking the value
`1` at `(t, x, y, z)`, with no further normalisation; the shapes are not claimed to carry the
conventional factors of an action. The last two are kept because nothing in the laws of the gauge
sector relates the two derivative slots, no symmetry of the derivatives, no Bianchi identity, no
equation of motion and no quotient by total derivatives. In the covariant field algebra of the
Standard Model the hypercharge derivatives do commute and the last two vanish
(`LocalCovFieldAlgebra.gaugeSector_lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq_traceFamilies`). The eight
form a spanning family, not a basis. None is shown to be nonzero, and no independence among them
is claimed.

## I. The Lorentz contraction span as invariants of mass weight eight

The converse of the Lorentz classification is that the Lorentz contraction span is made of gauge
and Lorentz invariants of mass weight eight. Its gauge invariance and its mass weight pass
to it from the gauge span, which contains it; Lorentz invariance comes from `RankFour`
directly, each block being spanned by the four contractions of a quadruple Lorentz family.

## J. The classifications as equivalences

The gauge reduction of section G and the Lorentz reduction of section H compose, and the
composite needs no stability or fixedness of the gauge span under the Lorentz group. The
converse, sections G and I, turns each reduction into an equivalence through
`ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff`.

products of the family with that vector by the same matrix.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.map_fixed_mul_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The mirror of `map_mul_fixed_eq_sum` with the fixed vector on the left.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_F_coord
declarations.doc:
The field-strength symbol evaluated on a standard-basis coordinate transforms under
the gauge group through the column of `adjointMatrix` indexed by that coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_F_coord (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (c : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν (GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis.coord c))
      = ∑ b, ((GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g b c : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν (GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis.coord b)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_gluonField
declarations.doc:
The gluon field strength transforms in the adjoint representation of the `su(3)`
factor of the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_gluonField (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (c : Fin 8) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (gluonField l μ ν c)
      = ∑ a : Fin 8, ((su3AdjointMatrix (GaugeGroupI.toSU3 g) a c : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          gluonField l μ ν a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_wField
declarations.doc:
The `W`-boson field strength transforms in the adjoint representation of the `su(2)`
factor of the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_wField (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (c : Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (wField l μ ν c)
      = ∑ i : Fin 3, ((su2AdjointMatrix (GaugeGroupI.toSU2 g) i c : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          wField l μ ν i

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_hyperchargeField
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge field strength is gauge invariant, the adjoint action of the gauge
group on the `u(1)` factor of the gauge algebra is trivial.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_hyperchargeField (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (hyperchargeField l μ ν) = hyperchargeField l μ ν

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_su3_wField
declarations.doc:
The `W`-boson field strengths are fixed by the colour factor of the gauge group, since the
`su(2)` block of the adjoint matrix reads the isospin factor alone.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isEquivariant_colourAdj_gluonField
declarations.doc:
The gluon field strengths at fixed derivative slots and covector indices form a family
of one `su(3)` adjoint index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourAdj_gluonField {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.adj] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((gluonField l μ ν) ∘ relabelAdjIdx su3Label))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isEquivariant_isospinAdj_wField
declarations.doc:
The `W`-boson field strengths at fixed derivative slots and covector indices form a
family of one `su(2)` adjoint index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinAdj_wField {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.adj] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((wField l μ ν) ∘ relabelAdjIdx su2Label))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.EightIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a product of two underived field strengths, the two covector indices of
the first factor followed by the two of the second, read as one family of four
four-vector indices so that the Lorentz classification applies to it.
declarations.statement: abbrev EightIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gluonPair
declarations.doc:
The product of two underived gluon field strengths at the covector indices `p`, indexed
by the two `su(3)` adjoint indices it carries.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gluonPair (p : EightIdx) (a : Fin 2 → Fin 8) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.wPair
declarations.doc:
The product of two underived `W`-boson field strengths at the covector indices `p`,
indexed by the two `su(2)` adjoint indices it carries.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def wPair (p : EightIdx) (a : Fin 2 → Fin 3) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargePair
declarations.doc:
The product of two underived hypercharge field strengths at the covector indices `p`,
indexed by the two `u(1)` adjoint indices it carries.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def hyperchargePair (p : EightIdx)
    (_ : Fin 2 → Fin 1) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv
declarations.doc:
The twice-derived hypercharge field strength at the derivative slots `d 0`, `d 1` and
the covector indices `d 2`, `d 3`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hyperchargeDeriv (d : EightIdx) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGaugeGroupI_gluonPair_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
A gauge transformation moves a gluon pair as the `SU(3)` factor of that gauge group
element moves a tensor with two `su(3)` adjoint indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_gluonPair_eq_sum (p : EightIdx) (g : GaugeGroupI) (l : Fin 2 → Fin 8) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (gluonPair p l) = ∑ a : Fin 2 → Fin 8,
      (∏ i : Fin 2, ((su3AdjointMatrix (GaugeGroupI.toSU3 g) (a i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
        gluonPair p a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isEquivariant_colourAdjAdj_gluonPair
declarations.doc: A gluon pair is a bi-adjoint `su(3)` tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourAdjAdj_gluonPair (p : EightIdx) :
    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.adj, .adj] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((gluonPair p) ∘ relabelAdjPairIdx su3Label))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGaugeGroupI_wPair_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
A gauge transformation moves a `W`-boson pair as the `SU(2)` factor of that gauge group
element moves a tensor with two `su(2)` adjoint indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_wPair_eq_sum (p : EightIdx) (g : GaugeGroupI) (l : Fin 2 → Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (wPair p l) = ∑ a : Fin 2 → Fin 3,
      (∏ i : Fin 2, ((su2AdjointMatrix (GaugeGroupI.toSU2 g) (a i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
        wPair p a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isEquivariant_isospinAdjAdj_wPair
declarations.doc: A `W`-boson pair is a bi-adjoint `su(2)` tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinAdjAdj_wPair (p : EightIdx) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.adj, .adj] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((wPair p) ∘ relabelAdjPairIdx su2Label))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGaugeGroupI_hyperchargePair
declarations.doc: A gauge transformation fixes a hypercharge pair, which is the `u(1)` bi-adjoint law.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_hyperchargePair (p : EightIdx) (g : GaugeGroupI) (l : Fin 2 → Fin 1) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (hyperchargePair p l) = hyperchargePair p l

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gluonTrace
declarations.doc:
The gluon trace contraction at the covector indices `p`, the Kronecker contraction of
the two colour indices of the gluon pair.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gluonTrace (p : EightIdx) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.wTrace
declarations.doc: The `W`-boson trace contraction at the covector indices `p`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def wTrace (p : EightIdx) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace
declarations.doc: The hypercharge trace contraction at the covector indices `p`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hyperchargeTrace (p : EightIdx) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gluonTrace_eq
declarations.doc: The gluon trace contraction is the kinetic pairing of two gluon field strengths.
declarations.statement:
lemma gluonTrace_eq (p : EightIdx) :
    gluonTrace p
      = ∑ a : Fin 8, gluonField ![] (p 0) (p 1) a * gluonField ![] (p 2) (p 3) a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.wTrace_eq
declarations.doc:
The `W`-boson trace contraction is the kinetic pairing of two `W`-boson field
strengths.
declarations.statement:
lemma wTrace_eq (p : EightIdx) :
    wTrace p = ∑ i : Fin 3, wField ![] (p 0) (p 1) i * wField ![] (p 2) (p 3) i

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace_eq
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge trace contraction is the product of the two hypercharge field
strengths, the `u(1)` factor being one dimensional.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeTrace_eq (p : EightIdx) :
    hyperchargeTrace p
      = hyperchargeField ![] (p 0) (p 1) * hyperchargeField ![] (p 2) (p 3)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_gluonTrace
declarations.doc: The gluon trace contraction is fixed by the whole gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_gluonTrace (g : GaugeGroupI) (p : EightIdx) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (gluonTrace p) = gluonTrace p

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_wTrace
declarations.doc: The `W`-boson trace contraction is fixed by the whole gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_wTrace (g : GaugeGroupI) (p : EightIdx) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (wTrace p) = wTrace p

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_hyperchargeTrace
declarations.doc: The hypercharge trace contraction is fixed by the whole gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_hyperchargeTrace (g : GaugeGroupI) (p : EightIdx) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (hyperchargeTrace p) = hyperchargeTrace p

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_hyperchargeDeriv
declarations.doc: The twice-derived hypercharge field strength is fixed by the whole gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_hyperchargeDeriv (g : GaugeGroupI) (d : EightIdx) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (hyperchargeDeriv d) = hyperchargeDeriv d

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.F_mem_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Every field-strength symbol lies in the derivative submodule of its own number of
covariant derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma F_mem_derivSubmodule {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) : gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ ∈ derivSubmodule n

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.F_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: A field-strength symbol with `n` covariant derivatives has mass weight `2 * (2 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma F_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) : gaugeFieldStrength l μ ν φ ∈ massWeightSubmodule (2 * (2 +
      n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.F_mul_F_mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight
declarations.doc: A product of two underived field-strength symbols has mass weight eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma F_mul_F_mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight (μ ν μ' ν' : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ φ' : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    gaugeFieldStrength ![] μ ν φ * gaugeFieldStrength ![] μ' ν' φ' ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gluonTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The gluon trace contraction has mass weight eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma gluonTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule (p : EightIdx) :
    gluonTrace p ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.wTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The `W`-boson trace contraction has mass weight eight.
declarations.statement: lemma wTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule (p : EightIdx) : wTrace p ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The hypercharge trace contraction has mass weight eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule (p : EightIdx) :
    hyperchargeTrace p ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The twice-derived hypercharge field strength has mass weight `2 * (2 + 2)`, eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeDeriv_mem_massWeightSubmodule (d : EightIdx) :
    hyperchargeDeriv d ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.gluonPairSpan
declarations.doc: The join, over all covector indices, of the spans of the gluon pair families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gluonPairSpan : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.wPairSpan
declarations.doc: The join, over all covector indices, of the spans of the `W`-boson pair families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def wPairSpan : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeTraceSpan
declarations.doc: The span of the hypercharge trace contractions.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hyperchargeTraceSpan : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.hyperchargeDerivSpan
declarations.doc: The span of the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hyperchargeDerivSpan : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.neutralVec
declarations.doc:
The underived symbols of the factors other than colour, on the `W`-boson and hypercharge
coordinates of the standard basis.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def neutralVec (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_su3_neutralVec
declarations.doc:
The symbols of the factors other than colour are fixed by the colour factor of the gauge
group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_neutralVec (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∀ j, repGaugeGroupI (U, 1, 1) (neutralVec μ ν j) = neutralVec μ ν j

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.DerivIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a twice-derived symbol, the two derivative slots and the two covector
indices.
declarations.statement: abbrev DerivIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.MixIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a mixed product with a gluon symbol, the two covector indices of the gluon
factor, the two of the other factor, and the coordinate of the other factor.
declarations.statement: abbrev MixIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.ColourIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a family carrying one unpaired `su(3)` adjoint index at mass weight
eight, a twice-derived gluon tower, or an underived gluon field strength against an
underived symbol of another factor on either side.
declarations.statement: abbrev ColourIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.colourFamily
declarations.doc: The families carrying one unpaired `su(3)` adjoint index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def colourFamily : ColourIdx → Fin 8 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isEquivariant_colourAdj_colourFamily
declarations.doc:
Each colour family is an `su(3)` adjoint family, the colour factor moves the gluon
index and fixes the other factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourAdj_colourFamily :
    ∀ i : ColourIdx, (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.adj] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((colourFamily i) ∘ relabelAdjIdx su3Label))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.IsospinIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a family carrying one unpaired `su(2)` adjoint index at mass weight
eight, a twice-derived `W`-boson tower, or an underived `W`-boson field strength against
an underived hypercharge field strength on either side.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsospinIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isospinFamily
declarations.doc: The families carrying one unpaired `su(2)` adjoint index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def isospinFamily : IsospinIdx → Fin 3 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isEquivariant_isospinAdj_isospinFamily
declarations.doc:
Each isospin family is an `su(2)` adjoint family, the isospin factor moves the
`W`-boson index and fixes hypercharge.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinAdj_isospinFamily :
    ∀ i : IsospinIdx, (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.adj] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((isospinFamily i) ∘ relabelAdjIdx su2Label))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_su3_isospinFamily
declarations.doc:
The isospin families are fixed by the colour factor, every one of their factors
being.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_isospinFamily (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    ∀ (i : IsospinIdx) (a : Fin 3),
      repGaugeGroupI (U, 1, 1) (isospinFamily i a) = isospinFamily i a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.unpairedColourSpan
declarations.doc: The join of the spans of the colour families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def unpairedColourSpan : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.unpairedIsospinSpan
declarations.doc: The join of the spans of the isospin families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def unpairedIsospinSpan : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.colourFamily_mem
declarations.doc: A component of a colour family lies in the join of the colour spans.
declarations.statement: lemma colourFamily_mem (i : ColourIdx) (a : Fin 8) : colourFamily i a ∈ unpairedColourSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.isospinFamily_mem
declarations.doc: A component of an isospin family lies in the join of the isospin spans.
declarations.statement:
lemma isospinFamily_mem (i : IsospinIdx) (a : Fin 3) :
    isospinFamily i a ∈ unpairedIsospinSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.repGauge_su3_of_mem_unpairedIsospinSpan
declarations.doc: The join of the isospin families is fixed pointwise by the colour factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_of_mem_unpairedIsospinSpan (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    ∀ y ∈ unpairedIsospinSpan, repGaugeGroupI (U, 1, 1) y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeSector.derivSubmodule_le_of_coord_mem
declarations.doc:
A derivative submodule lies in a submodule as soon as the symbols on the standard
coordinates do.
declarations.statement:
