declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isFixedBy_massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc:
The scalars are fixed by both groups, since each acts by an algebra map, so each fixes the
unit. This is what makes the constant term an invariant, and it is what the backward
direction of the classification needs of the weight-zero part of the span.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_massWeightSubmodule_zero :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (massWeightSubmodule 0)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc:
The gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content of the Standard Model up to mass weight `w`. It is
the weight-zero part of the field algebra, which is the constant term, joined with the
Standard-Model span of every weight up to `w`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule_zero_le_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: The constant term lies in the span of the filtration, at every bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero_le_standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) :
    massWeightSubmodule 0 ≤ standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpan_le_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: The graded span of a weight at most `w` lies in the span of the filtration at `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpan_le_standardModelSpanLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) :
    standardModelSpan k ≤ standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpanLE_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The span of the filtration at `w` has mass weight at most `w`. The constant term has
weight zero and each graded span has its own weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpanLE_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) :
    standardModelSpanLE w ≤ massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isFixedBy_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc:
The span of the filtration is fixed pointwise by the gauge and Lorentz groups
together. At positive weight this is the fixedness of the graded spans; at weight zero
it is the fixedness of the unit, and that is the only new content of the filtration.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (standardModelSpanLE w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_of_mem_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: Every element of the span of the filtration is a gauge invariant.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentz_of_mem_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: Every element of the span of the filtration is a Lorentz invariant.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpanLE_eight
declarations.doc:
The span of the filtration at bound eight in reduced form. Of the nine graded spans
only two are non-trivial, the Higgs mass term at weight four and the dimension-four
Lagrangian at weight eight, so what survives up to mass dimension four is the constant
term, the Higgs mass term, and the Lagrangian.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpanLE_eight :
    standardModelSpanLE 8 = (1 : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ⊔
    (ScalarSector.dotSpan 0 0
      ⊔ (GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
            ⊔ ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
          ⊔ (FermionSector.kineticSpan ⊔ yukawaSpan)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The filtration reduces to its span, at every bound up to eight. The filtration is a
join of the graded pieces, each of them stable under both groups, and `ReducesInvariantsTo` is
closed under joins in its source, so the weights are taken one at a time, each in turn joining the
error term of the others. At positive weight the graded reduction of `Invariants.lean` is
used; at weight zero a submodule reduces to itself, the constant term being carried in the
span.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmoduleLE {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (massWeightSubmoduleLE w)
      (standardModelSpanLE w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_standardModelSpanLE_eight_of_mem_sector
declarations.doc:
An element of a sector of mass weight at most eight fixed by both groups lies in the span
of the filtration at bound eight. Its weight components lie in the weight pieces of the
sector and are fixed by both groups. The weight-zero component is a constant, and every other
component lies in the Standard-Model span of its weight by the sector's reduction.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_standardModelSpanLE_eight_of_mem_sector {A : Finset GaugeFieldData.FieldKind}
    {y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hyA : y ∈ fieldData.sector A)
    (hyLE : y ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE 8)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y) (hL : ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup Λ y = y) :
    y ∈ standardModelSpanLE 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification of the Standard Model up to mass weight `w ≤ 8` as an equivalence,
in the shape every sector uses. An element of `massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S`, with `S`
stable under both groups, is fixed by both groups exactly when it is a combination of
the constant term and the Standard-Model terms of weight at most `w`, up to a remainder
in `S` fixed by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ) (hw : w ≤ 8)
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.exists_mem_standardModelSpanLE_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of mass weight at most `w`, for `w ≤ 8`, modulo a
submodule `S` stable under both groups. Such an invariant is a combination of the
constant term and the Standard-Model terms of weight at most `w`, plus a remainder in
`S`, and the remainder is fixed by both groups as well, being the difference of two
invariants.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_mem_standardModelSpanLE_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant (w : ℕ) (hw : w ≤ 8)
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) :
    ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
      ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
      ∧ x - y ∈ standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. At every bound up to eight an element
of `massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of the span of the
filtration joined with `S` fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw : w ≤ 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ standardModelSpanLE w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification at bound eight, that is at mass dimension at most four, as an
equivalence. An element of `massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S`, with `S` stable under both
groups, is fixed by both groups exactly when it lies in the span of the filtration up to
a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ standardModelSpanLE 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc: The same at bound eight without the existential.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ standardModelSpanLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
The invariant content of the Standard Model up to mass dimension four. An element of
`massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S`, for `S` a submodule stable under both groups, is fixed by
the gauge group and the Lorentz group exactly when it is a combination of
the constant term, of mass dimension zero,
the Higgs mass term `H† H`, of mass dimension two (`ScalarSector.dotSpan`),
and the dimension-four span — the four Lorentz contractions of the three `F·F` trace
families and of the twice-derived hypercharge field strength, among them the gauge
kinetic and theta terms (`GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), the Higgs
kinetic term, its quartic potential and its two box terms
(`ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), the kinetic terms of the ten fermion
species over the nine family pairs (`FermionSector.kineticSpan`), and the six Yukawa
couplings over the nine family pairs (`yukawaSpan`) —
up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups, and nothing else. The generators span;
they are not shown to be independent, and no quotient by total derivatives is taken.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ (1 : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ⊔ (ScalarSector.dotSpan 0 0
              ⊔ (GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                    ⊔ ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                  ⊔ (FermionSector.kineticSpan ⊔ yukawaSpan)))

modules.title: The invariant content of the Standard Model
modules.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of the Standard Model at each mass weight from one to eight,
obtained by joining the classifications of the eight sectors.

## i. Overview

This is where the classification of the Standard Model closes. A product of covariant
generators realises a set of kinds (gauge, scalar, fermion), and the eight sets of kinds cut the
field algebra into eight sectors `fieldData.sectorMassWeight A w`, each of which has been classified
separately at every mass weight up to eight, that is at every mass dimension up to four.
This file joins the eight.

At mass dimension four the gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content is spanned by the four
Lorentz contractions of each of the three `F·F` trace families and of the twice-derived
hypercharge field strength. The antisymmetry of the field strength cuts these to two of each
(`GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`), and the two of the twice-derived hypercharge
field strength vanish, its covariant derivatives being ordinary ones (A.1). What is left is the
kinetic-shape and theta-shape contractions of the three gauge groups. Beside them stand the
Higgs kinetic term with its quartic potential and its two box terms; the kinetic terms of the
ten fermion species over the nine family pairs; and the six Yukawa couplings over the nine
family pairs. Below mass dimension four there is a single term, the Higgs mass term `H† H` at
mass weight four; below that, nothing.

The statement is about formal expressions, the elements of the field algebra with complex
coefficients. It is a spanning statement, and the listed generators are not shown to be
independent or nonzero. No reality condition is imposed, and nothing is identified modulo
total derivatives or the equations of motion, so both box terms, both placements of each
fermion derivative and the theta terms all appear.

The join is the delicate step. `massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_sectorMassWeight` writes the
weight-`w` submodule as the join of the eight sectors' weight-`w` parts, but reading off
from an invariant of the whole that its eight pieces are separately invariant would need
the pieces to be determined by their sum — the independence of the sectors, which does
not follow from the structure of the covariant field algebra of the Standard Model used here.

Nothing here uses it. Each sector's classification is a reduction `ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W`
of `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.InvariantReduction` — every `σ`-invariant of `V ⊔ S` lies in
`W ⊔ S`, for every `σ`-stable `S` — and that relation is closed under joins in its source.
Joining the sectors therefore asks only that each of them be carried into itself by the two
groups, which they are (`repGauge_mem_sectorMassWeight`, `repLorentz_mem_sectorMassWeight`).
The eight are taken one at a time, each in turn joining the error term of the others, and
independence never enters.

Section A collects the surviving spans of the eight sectors into `standardModelSpan`, and
section B checks that it is made of invariants of the right mass weight, which is both the
easy direction of the classification and the stability the reduction asks of its target.
Section C restricts each sector's reduction to its weight part, section D joins them, and
sections E and F read off the equivalence, through
`ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`, and its consequence at mass
dimension four.

The weight is bounded below as well as above. At weight zero the field algebra contains
the scalars, which are fixed by both groups and lie in no given `S`; every one of the
sector classifications combined here excludes that weight for the same reason.

## ii. Key results

In the namespace `StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`:

- `standardModelSpan` : the gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content of the Standard Model at mass
  weight `w`, the join of the surviving spans of the eight sectors.
- `reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule` : the weight-`w` submodule reduces to the span, for
  `w` from one to eight.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the classification at each
  mass weight from one to eight.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian` : the invariant
  content at mass dimension four, written out term by term.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The span of the Standard Model Lagrangian
  - A.1. The twice-derived hypercharge contractions vanish
- B. The span is made of invariants of the right weight
- C. Each sector reduces to the span
- D. Joining the eight sectors
- E. The classification at mass dimension at most four
- F. The Standard Model Lagrangian

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The span of the Standard Model Lagrangian

### A.1. The twice-derived hypercharge contractions vanish

The hypercharge coordinate kills brackets, so the covariant derivatives of the hypercharge
field strength are ordinary derivatives, which commute (`covF_comp_perm_of_map_lie` with
`GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis_coord_inr_inr_lie`). The twice-derived hypercharge family is therefore
symmetric in its two derivative slots as well as antisymmetric in its two field-strength slots,
and `RankFour` sends both of its remaining contractions to zero. So six generators span the
gauge contribution: for each of the gluon, `W` and hypercharge trace families, the `(0,2)(1,3)`
metric contraction `η^{μρ} η^{νσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}` and the Levi-Civita contraction
`ε^{μνρσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}`, gauge index summed, as the plain component sums of `RankFour` with no
further normalisation. These are identities of local expressions; no integration by parts,
total-derivative quotient or equation of motion is involved.

The derivative symmetry is not a law of `GaugeSector`, which relates no derivative slots. It
holds here because the covariant derivatives of the field strength in the covariant field algebra of
the Standard Model are ordinary ones. Nothing is said about the
gluon and `W` components, whose covariant derivatives do not commute.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpan
declarations.doc:
The gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content of the Standard Model at mass weight `w`, the join of
the surviving spans of the eight sectors. At weight eight it is the gauge sector's four Lorentz
contractions of each of its four families, two of which already span for each family
(`GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`), and the two of the twice-derived hypercharge field
strength vanish, leaving the two contractions of each of the three trace families
(`gaugeSector_lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq_traceFamilies`). These are the kinetic-shape and
theta-shape contractions of the three gauge groups. Together with these come the Higgs sector's
two box terms, kinetic term and quartic potential, the fermion sector's ten kinetic terms over the
nine family pairs, and the six Yukawa couplings over the nine family pairs. Below weight eight
only the Higgs sector survives, and only at weight four, where it contributes the Higgs mass
term.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def standardModelSpan (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpan_eight
declarations.doc:
At mass weight eight the span is the gauge, Higgs, fermion and Yukawa spans
together.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpan_eight :
    standardModelSpan 8 = GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
        ⊔ ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
      ⊔ (FermionSector.kineticSpan ⊔ yukawaSpan)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpan_four
declarations.doc:
At mass weight four the span is the line through the Higgs mass term `H† H`, the one
invariant of the Standard Model below mass dimension four.
declarations.statement: lemma standardModelSpan_four : standardModelSpan 4 = ScalarSector.dotSpan 0 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpan_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
At every mass weight other than four and eight the span is trivial. Apart from the
Higgs mass term there is no Standard-Model term below mass dimension four.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpan_eq_bot {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≠ 8) (hw4 : w ≠ 4) :
    standardModelSpan w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.hyperchargeDeriv_comp_swap_zero_one
declarations.doc:
The twice-derived hypercharge field strengths are symmetric in their two derivative
slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeDeriv_comp_swap_zero_one (d : GaugeSector.EightIdx) :
    GaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv (d ∘ Equiv.swap 0 1) = GaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv d

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.hyperchargeDeriv_contractionTensor_one
declarations.doc:
The metric contraction `η^{μρ} η^{νσ} ∇_μ ∇_ν B_{ρσ}` vanishes, a symmetric pair of
derivatives being contracted against the antisymmetric pair of field-strength indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeDeriv_contractionTensor_one :
    liftComponents GaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv (RankFour.contractionTensor 1) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.hyperchargeDeriv_contractionTensor_three
declarations.doc:
The Levi-Civita contraction `ε^{μνρσ} ∇_μ ∇_ν B_{ρσ}` vanishes, a symmetric pair of
derivatives being contracted against the antisymmetric symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeDeriv_contractionTensor_three :
    liftComponents GaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv (RankFour.contractionTensor 3) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.gaugeSector_lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq_traceFamilies
declarations.doc:
The gauge contribution at mass weight eight is spanned by the Lorentz contractions of the
three trace families alone. For each of `gluonTrace`, `wTrace` and `hyperchargeTrace` these are
the `(0,2)(1,3)` metric contraction `η^{μρ} η^{νσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}` and the Levi-Civita contraction
`ε^{μνρσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}`, as plain component sums. The two twice-derived hypercharge
generators of `GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq` vanish. The six span; they are
not shown to be independent or nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSector_lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq_traceFamilies :
    GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
      = Submodule.span ℂ {liftComponents GaugeSector.gluonTrace (contractionTensor 1),
          liftComponents GaugeSector.gluonTrace (contractionTensor 3)}
        ⊔ (Submodule.span ℂ {liftComponents GaugeSector.wTrace (contractionTensor 1),
            liftComponents GaugeSector.wTrace (contractionTensor 3)}
          ⊔ Submodule.span ℂ {liftComponents GaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace (contractionTensor 1),
            liftComponents GaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace (contractionTensor 3)})

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.gaugeSector_massWeightSubmodule_le
declarations.doc:
At a non-zero weight the gauge sector's mass-weight submodule sits inside that of the
covariant field algebra, being the `{gauge}` piece of the sector decomposition there.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSector_massWeightSubmodule_le {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    GaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule w ≤ massWeightSubmodule w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.scalarSector_massWeightSubmodule_le
declarations.doc:
At a non-zero weight the Higgs sector's mass-weight submodule sits inside that of the
covariant field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma scalarSector_massWeightSubmodule_le {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule w ≤ massWeightSubmodule w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.fermionSector_massWeightSubmodule_le
declarations.doc:
At a non-zero weight the fermion sector's mass-weight submodule sits inside that of the
covariant field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionSector_massWeightSubmodule_le {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule w ≤ massWeightSubmodule w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.standardModelSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The span at weight `w` has mass weight `w`, each of its contributions is a
combination of words of that weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule (w : ℕ) :
    standardModelSpan w ≤ massWeightSubmodule w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isFixedBy_standardModelSpan
declarations.doc:
The span at weight `w` is fixed pointwise by the gauge and Lorentz groups together, since
every one of its contributions is a span of invariants. This is the easy direction of
the classification, and it is also what supplies the stability the reduction asks of its
target.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_standardModelSpan (w : ℕ) :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_empty
declarations.doc:
The empty sector reduces to the span. Away from weight zero it is trivial, its only word
being the empty one.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_empty {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight ∅ w) (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_gauge
declarations.doc:
The gauge sector reduces to the span, at weight eight to the four Lorentz contractions of
its four families, two of each spanning, below it to nothing at all.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_gauge {w : ℕ} (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge} w) (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_higgs
declarations.doc:
The Higgs sector reduces to the span, at weight eight to the two box terms, the kinetic
term and the quartic potential, at weight four to the Higgs mass term, and elsewhere to
nothing.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_higgs {w : ℕ} (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar} w) (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_fermion
declarations.doc:
The fermion sector reduces to the span, at weight eight to the ten kinetic terms over the
nine family pairs and below it to nothing. There is no Dirac mass term.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_fermion {w : ℕ} (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.fermion} w) (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion
declarations.doc:
The Yukawa sector reduces to the span, at weight eight to the six Yukawa couplings over the
nine family pairs, below it to nothing.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w)
      (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs
declarations.doc:
The gauge-Higgs sector reduces to nothing, as it carries no Lorentz invariant below weight
nine.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar} w)
      (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion
declarations.doc:
The gauge-fermion sector reduces to nothing, as it carries no Lorentz invariant below weight
nine.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.fermion} w)
      (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_mixed
declarations.doc: The mixed sector reduces to nothing, as it is trivial below weight nine.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_mixed {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight
        {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w)
      (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isStableUnder_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
Every weight part of every sector is carried into itself by both groups. This is the
stability the join of the reductions asks of its summands.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_sectorMassWeight (T : Finset FieldKind) (w : ℕ) :
    IsStableUnder (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight T w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
Every sector reduces to the span, at every weight from one to eight. The three
constructors of `GaugeFieldData.FieldKind` give eight sets of kinds, and section C treats
each.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight {w : ℕ} (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w ≤ 8)
    (T : Finset FieldKind) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup)
      (fieldData.sectorMassWeight T w) (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The whole weight-`w` submodule reduces to the span, for `w` from one to eight. The
mass-weight submodule is the join of the eight sectors' weight-`w` parts, each of them
stable under both groups, and `ReducesInvariantsTo` is closed under joins in its source. The
sectors are taken one at a time, each in turn joining the error term of the others. No
independence of the sectors is used, and none is available.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule {w : ℕ} (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (massWeightSubmodule w)
      (standardModelSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification of the Standard Model at mass dimension at most four as an
equivalence, in the shape every sector uses. An element of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S`
for `0 < w ≤ 8`, with `S` stable under both groups, is fixed by both groups exactly when
it is a combination of the Standard-Model terms of weight `w` up to a remainder in `S`
fixed by both groups. Forwards this is the reduction of section D; backwards it uses
that the span is made of invariants of weight `w`, section B. The weight-four Higgs mass
term is what makes the span, rather than the bare equation `x = y`, the right form of
the statement.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ) (hw0 : 0 < w)
    (hw : w ≤ 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ standardModelSpan w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.exists_mem_standardModelSpan_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of mass weight `w` for `0 < w ≤ 8`, modulo a
submodule `S` stable under both groups. Such an invariant is a combination of the
Standard-Model terms of that weight plus a remainder in `S`, and the remainder is fixed
by both groups as well, being the difference of two invariants.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_mem_standardModelSpan_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w ≤ 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) :
    ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
      ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
      ∧ x - y ∈ standardModelSpan w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. At every weight from one to eight an
element of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of the
Standard-Model span joined with `S` fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w ≤ 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ standardModelSpan w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
The invariant content of the Standard Model at mass dimension four. An element of
`massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S`, for `S` a submodule stable under both groups, is fixed by
the gauge group and the Lorentz group exactly when it is a combination of
the four Lorentz contractions of the three `F·F` trace families and of the twice-derived
hypercharge field strength (`GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), two of each
spanning by `GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq` (the kinetic-shape and
theta-shape contractions of the three gauge groups and two contractions of the
twice-derived hypercharge field strength, which vanish
(`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian_traceFamilies`)),
the Higgs kinetic term, its quartic potential and its two box terms
(`ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan`),
the kinetic terms of the ten fermion species over the nine family pairs
(`FermionSector.kineticSpan`),
and the six Yukawa couplings over the nine family pairs (`yukawaSpan`),
up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups — and nothing else. The generators span;
they are not shown to be independent, and no quotient by total derivatives is taken.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ GaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                ⊔ ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
              ⊔ (FermionSector.kineticSpan ⊔ yukawaSpan)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian_traceFamilies
declarations.doc:
The invariant content of the Standard Model at mass dimension four with the gauge
contribution written through the Lorentz contractions of the three trace families alone,
the `(0,2)(1,3)` metric contraction and the Levi-Civita contraction of each of `gluonTrace`,
`wTrace` and `hyperchargeTrace` (`gaugeSector_lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq_traceFamilies`).
The Higgs, fermion and Yukawa contributions are as in
`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian`. The
generators span; they are not shown to be independent or nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian_traceFamilies
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ (Submodule.span ℂ
                {liftComponents GaugeSector.gluonTrace (contractionTensor 1),
                  liftComponents GaugeSector.gluonTrace (contractionTensor 3)}
              ⊔ (Submodule.span ℂ {liftComponents GaugeSector.wTrace (contractionTensor 1),
                  liftComponents GaugeSector.wTrace (contractionTensor 3)}
                ⊔ Submodule.span ℂ
                  {liftComponents GaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace (contractionTensor 1),
                    liftComponents GaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace (contractionTensor 3)}))
                ⊔ ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
              ⊔ (FermionSector.kineticSpan ⊔ yukawaSpan)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_sup
declarations.doc:
Below mass dimension two there is nothing at all, and at mass dimension two only the
Higgs mass term. At every weight from one to seven other than four an element of
`massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups already lies in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_sup (w : ℕ) (hw0 : 0 < w)
    (hw : w < 8) (hw4 : w ≠ 4) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_four_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_higgsMass
declarations.doc:
At mass dimension two the only invariant of the Standard Model is the Higgs mass term
`H† H`. An element of `massWeightSubmodule 4 ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is a multiple of
it up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_four_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_higgsMass
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule 4 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ ScalarSector.dotSpan 0 0

modules.title: The one-kind sectors of the Standard Model
modules.doc:
The pure gauge, Higgs and fermion sectors of the Standard Model as its three sector algebras.

## i. Overview

The sectors of the covariant field algebra of the Standard Model are the generic sectors
`fieldData.sector A` of its field datum, and their weight pieces are
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight A w`. The Higgs is the only bosonic species, so the scalar kind is
the Higgs kind.

The Standard Model sector files work with three algebras: `GaugeSector.gaugeAlgebra`, generated
by the field-strength towers, `ScalarSector.higgsAlgebra`, generated by the Higgs towers, and
`FermionSector.fermionAlgebra`, generated by the fermion towers. Each is generated by covariant
generators of one kind, and contains all of them. So at a non-zero weight `w` the weight-`w`
piece of the sector of that kind is the weight-`w` piece of the algebra. At weight zero the
algebras also contain the constants, which the generic decomposition files under the sector
of `∅`.

## ii. Key results

- `sectorMassWeight_gauge_eq`, `sectorMassWeight_higgs_eq`, `sectorMassWeight_fermion_eq` : at
  a non-zero weight the one-kind sectors are the weight pieces of the three sector algebras.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The field-strength tower at a functional on the Lie algebra
- B. The sector algebras and the generators of their kind
- C. The one-kind sectors are the sector algebras

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covF_comp_gaugeAlgebraEquiv
declarations.doc:
The tower `covF`, indexed by functionals on `GaugeAlgebra`, at the transport of a
functional on the Lie algebra of the global gauge group, is the tower `fieldStrength`,
indexed by functionals on that Lie algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma covF_comp_gaugeAlgebraEquiv {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covF l μ ν
        (φ ∘ₗ (gaugeAlgebraEquiv : GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] globalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra))
      = fieldStrength l μ ν φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.gaugeAlgebra_generators_subset

    (⋃ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),

      ⊆ fieldData.kindGenerators .gauge

modules.title: The covariant towers of the Standard Model
modules.doc:
The thirteen covariant towers of the Standard Model in the notation of the classification of
invariants, their commutation across sectors, and the algebra they generate.

## i. Overview

The covariant fields of the Standard Model, and every polynomial expression in them, live in
the covariant field algebra of the Standard Model `StandardModel.fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`,
which carries the global gauge action, the Lorentz action and the mass-weight grading. This file
names its thirteen covariant towers in the notation of the classification of invariants, records
that towers of different sectors commute, and defines the field algebra they generate.

The thirteen towers are the field strength, the Higgs field and its conjugate, and the five
fermion species in three generations with their conjugates, each with all of its covariant
derivatives. Section A names them. Section B records the symmetry of the field-strength tower
at a dual vector vanishing on brackets. Section C states the commutation of towers of
different sectors, which is what the classification of invariants is written in terms of, and
section D defines the field algebra.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covF`, `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covH` and their companions : the thirteen
  covariant towers.
- `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.F_comm_H` and its companions : the towers of different sectors
  commute.
- `LocalCovFieldAlgebra.fieldAlgebra` : the algebra generated by all the covariant towers.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The covariant fields of the Standard Model
- B. The field strength at a dual vector vanishing on brackets
- C. The cross-sector commutation rules
- D. The field algebra

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The covariant fields of the Standard Model

The thirteen covariant towers the theory is written in are the towers of the covariant field
algebra of the Standard Model. The field-strength tower is real-linear in its value index.
## B. The field strength at a dual vector vanishing on brackets

## C. The cross-sector commutation rules

A bosonic tower is central (`fieldStrength_commute`, `higgsField_commute`,
`conjHiggsField_commute`), so it commutes with every tower of another sector. The rules are
named as the classification of invariants uses them.
## D. The field algebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.covF
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivatives `∇_l F_{μν}` of the field strength inside the covariant field

    (hφ : ∀ x y : GaugeAlgebra, φ ⁅x, y⁆ = 0) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    covF (l ∘ σ) μ ν φ = covF l μ ν φ

modules.title: The mixed sector
modules.doc:
The gauge-Higgs-fermion sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra, at low weight.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

The sector `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar, fermion} w` of the generic
`GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight` is the home of any term that mixes all three kinds of
covariant field at once. A field-strength tower carries weight at least `4`, a Higgs (or
conjugate Higgs) tower weight at least `2`, and a fermion tower weight at least `3`, so a
product of generators of all three kinds has total weight at least `4 + 2 + 3 = 9`, by
`GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_eq_bot_of_lt`.

Consequently the mixed sector vanishes identically below weight nine
(`sectorMassWeight_mixed_eq_bot_of_lt_nine`), in particular at every weight up to
eight. There is no Standard-Model term of mass dimension at most four (mass
weight, twice the mass dimension, at most eight) that mixes gauge, Higgs and fermion
fields together.

Below weight nine, then, there is nothing left to classify. The sector is `⊥`, so an
element of `⊥ ⊔ S` is an element of `S` outright, whatever `S` may be. Section B records
that in the shape the other sectors carry, so that the four can later be combined; unlike
them it asks no stability of `S` and no invariance of the element, there being nothing to
peel away and no parity or index count to run.

## ii. Key results

- `minKindWeight` : the minimum mass weight of a generator of each kind.
- `sectorMassWeight_mixed_eq_bot_of_lt_nine` : the mixed sector vanishes below weight nine.
- `mem_sectorMassWeight_mixed_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the classification
  below mass weight nine as an equivalence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mixed sector vanishes below weight nine
- B. The classification below weight nine

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mixed sector vanishes below weight nine

## B. The classification below weight nine

Nine is beyond every weight a dimension-four term can reach, so the vanishing of section A settles
the whole of the mixed sector at a stroke. An element of `⊥ ⊔ S` is an element of `S`. The three
statements below are those of the gauge and Yukawa sectors, name for name, so that the four sectors
can be combined uniformly. There the forward direction is an argument — a metric trace, an index
count, the sign at the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` — and needs `S` stable and the element invariant; here it
is the emptiness of the sector, and the invariance conjuncts ride along in the equivalences only to
keep the shapes matched.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.minKindWeight
declarations.doc:
The minimum mass weight of a covariant generator of each kind in the Standard Model, four
for the field strength, two for the Higgs and three for the fermions.
declarations.statement: def minKindWeight : FieldKind → ℕ

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.minKindWeight_le
declarations.doc:
Every covariant generator of the Standard Model has at least the minimum mass weight of its
kind.
declarations.statement:
lemma minKindWeight_le {k : FieldKind} {v : ℕ} {b : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ fieldData.weightedGenerators k v) : minKindWeight k ≤ v

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_mixed_eq_bot_of_lt_nine
declarations.doc:
The mixed sector vanishes below weight nine, since a product of generators of all three kinds
carries gauge weight at least four, Higgs weight at least two and fermion weight at least
three, for a total of at least nine. So no such product exists at a lower weight, and the
sector's span there is trivial.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_mixed_eq_bot_of_lt_nine {w : ℕ} (hw : w < 9) :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight
      {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_mixed_lt_nine_sup
declarations.doc:
Below mass weight nine the mixed sector adds nothing to a submodule `S`. An element of
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` already lies in `S`. The
sector is trivial there, so no invariance is asked of `x` and no stability of `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_mixed_lt_nine_sup (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9)
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar,
      FieldKind.fermion} w ⊔ S) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_mixed_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence, in the shape of the
gauge- and Yukawa-sector statements. An element of
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` is fixed by both groups
exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups. Neither stability
hypothesis on `S` is needed, the forward direction being the vanishing of the sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_mixed_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ)
    (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar,
          FieldKind.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_mixed_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. Below mass weight nine an element of
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight {gauge, scalar, fermion} w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of
`S` fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_mixed_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.gauge, FieldKind.scalar,
          FieldKind.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)

modules.title: The scalar sector of the covariant field algebra
modules.doc:
The Higgs towers, the algebra they generate, and its mass-weight submodules up to weight eight.

## i. Overview

The scalar sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`
is the part built from the covariant towers `∇_l H` and `∇_l H̄` of the Higgs field and its
conjugate. The towers `covH` and `covBarH` are those of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`, and every
law they satisfy (the gauge law, the Lorentz law, bosonic commutation and the mass weight) is a law
of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra`, restated here for the towers. From them the file builds the
submodules `higgsSubmodule n` and `barHiggsSubmodule n` of terms linear in `∇_d H` and `∇_d H̄`, the
algebra `higgsAlgebra` they generate, and its mass-weight submodules `massWeightSubmodule n`. Each
of these carries a gauge weight decomposition. The mass-weight submodules are described by the
results of `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.HomogeneousGenerators`, and removing the leftmost Higgs tower
of each product gives them explicitly at weights `2`, `4`, `6` and `8`. These are the pieces from
which the Higgs terms of the Standard Model Lagrangian are assembled downstream.

## ii. Key results

- `covH`, `covBarH` : the Higgs and conjugate Higgs towers in the covariant field algebra.
- `H_equivariant`, `H_comm_H`, `H_massWeight`, `repLorentz_H` and their conjugates : the
  laws of the towers.
- `higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight`, `barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight` : the gauge weight
  decompositions of the Higgs submodules.
- `rep_dotGaugeHiggs_invariant`, `repLorentz_dotGaugeHiggs` : the gauge invariance and the
  Lorentz law of the inner product `H† H` with derivatives on the two factors.
- `massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul`, `massWeightSubmodule_eq` : removing the leftmost Higgs
  tower, and the binary weight recursion.
- `massWeightSubmodule_two_eq` up to `massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq` : the mass weights up to eight.
- `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeight` : the gauge weight decomposition of the mass-weight
  submodules.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Higgs towers and their laws
  - A.1. The gauge laws
  - A.2. The commutation laws and the mass weights
  - A.3. The Lorentz laws
- B. The Higgs algebra
- C. The components and the Higgs submodules
  - C.1. The gauge action on the components
  - C.2. The Higgs and conjugate Higgs submodules
- D. The gauge weight decomposition of the Higgs submodules
- E. The Higgs inner product
- F. The mass weight submodules
  - F.1. Membership and the grading
  - F.2. The weight decompositions
  - F.3. The odd mass weights vanish
  - F.4. The gauge weight decomposition
  - F.5. Mass weights up to eight
- G. Gauge invariants

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The Higgs towers and their laws

The two towers the sector is written in are the covariant derivatives of the Higgs field and
of its conjugate, as elements of the covariant field algebra of the Standard Model. Every law
they satisfy is a law of that algebra, restated here for the towers.
### A.1. The gauge laws
### A.2. The commutation laws and the mass weights
### A.3. The Lorentz laws

## B. The Higgs algebra

The subalgebra of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` generated by every `∇_d H` and `∇_d H̄`. Its
elements commute with one another, so any two of its submodules commute as submodules; and a
property closed under sums and products which holds on the symbols and on the scalars holds on all
of it.

## C. The components and the Higgs submodules

The components `∇_d H^i` and `∇_d H̄^i` are the symbols evaluated on the dual of the standard
basis of `HiggsVec`. The Higgs submodule with `n` derivatives is the span of the symbols
`∇_d H` over all multi-indices `d` of length `n`, equally the span of the components.
### C.1. The gauge action on the components
### C.2. The Higgs and conjugate Higgs submodules

## D. The gauge weight decomposition of the Higgs submodules

The four torus generators `gaugeTorusGen i` act on each component by a character: `∇_d H^j`
has isospin weight `-isoWeight j` and hypercharge weight `-3`, and `∇_d H̄^j` the opposite.
The general construction `doubletGaugeWeight` turns a family of such two-component
eigenvectors into a gauge weight decomposition of its span, and the two Higgs submodules
are instances of it.

## E. The Higgs inner product

The pairing `∇_{d1} H⁰ ∇_{d2} H̄⁰ + ∇_{d1} H¹ ∇_{d2} H̄¹` is invariant under the gauge group,
since `H̄` transforms by the conjugate of the unitary matrix acting on `H`, and its two
derivative multi-indices rotate independently under the Lorentz group.

## F. The mass weight submodules

A Higgs tower `∇ⁿH` or `∇ⁿH̄` has mass weight `2 * (1 + n)`, twice its mass dimension
`1 + n`; a term of mass dimension four, as in the Lagrangian, has weight eight.
### F.1. Membership and the grading

### F.2. The weight decompositions

The Higgs algebra is generated by the towers `∇ⁿH ⊔ ∇ⁿH̄`, on which `massWeightPoly` is the
monomial `X ^ (2 * (1 + n))`. The results of `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.HomogeneousGenerators`
then describe every mass weight submodule, as a join of products of towers in the order
written.
### F.3. The odd mass weights vanish
### F.4. The gauge weight decomposition

### F.5. Mass weights up to eight

Each case removes the leftmost tower. The towers with `0`, `1`, `2` and `3` derivatives
have weights `2`, `4`, `6` and `8`, and the remaining weight is read off from a smaller weight.
Expanding the joins gives the products of `H` and `H̄`; the Higgs algebra is commutative,
so orders differing only by the position of commuting factors are merged, and the products
are written in a fixed order.
## G. Gauge invariants

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.covH
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivatives `∇_l H` of the Higgs field inside the covariant field algebra
of the Standard Model.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def covH (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec →ₗ[ℂ] fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.covBarH
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivatives `∇_l H̄` of the conjugate Higgs field inside the covariant field
algebra of the Standard Model.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def covBarH (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec) →ₗ[ℂ] fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_mul
declarations.doc: Gauge transformations act on `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` by algebra maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_mul (g : GaugeGroupI) (b₁ b₂ : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (b₁ * b₂) = repGaugeGroupI g b₁ * repGaugeGroupI g b₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_mul
declarations.doc: Lorentz transformations act on `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` by algebra maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    repLorentzGroup Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentzGroup Λ b₁ * repLorentzGroup Λ b₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.H_equivariant
declarations.doc:
The Higgs symbol carries the dual of the gauge representation on `HiggsVec`. The
`SU(2)` index transforms contragrediently, and the hypercharge character by `u⁻³`.
declarations.statement:
lemma H_equivariant (g : GaugeGroupI) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) (n : ℕ)
    (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (covH n l φ) = covH n l (HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI.dual g φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barH_equivariant
declarations.doc:
The conjugate Higgs symbol carries the conjugate-dual of the gauge representation,
the physicists' `H^† ↦ H^† g^†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma barH_equivariant (g : GaugeGroupI) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)) (n : ℕ)
    (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (covBarH n l φ) = covBarH n l (HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.H_comm_H
declarations.doc: The Higgs is bosonic, so two Higgs symbols commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma H_comm_H (φ ψ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) (n1 n2 : ℕ)
    (l1 : Fin n1 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (l2 : Fin n2 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Commute (covH n1 l1 φ) (covH n2 l2 ψ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.H_comm_barH
declarations.doc: A Higgs symbol commutes with a conjugate Higgs symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma H_comm_barH (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) (ψ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec))
    (n1 n2 : ℕ) (l1 : Fin n1 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (l2 : Fin n2 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Commute (covH n1 l1 φ) (covBarH n2 l2 ψ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barH_comm_barH
declarations.doc: Two conjugate Higgs symbols commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma barH_comm_barH (φ ψ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)) (n1 n2 : ℕ)
    (l1 : Fin n1 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (l2 : Fin n2 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Commute (covBarH n1 l1 φ) (covBarH n2 l2 ψ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.H_massWeight
declarations.doc: The mass weight of the Higgs tower is `2 * (1 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma H_massWeight (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    massWeightPoly (covH n l φ) = Polynomial.monomial (2 * (1 + n)) (covH n l φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barH_massWeight
declarations.doc: The mass weight of the conjugate Higgs tower is `2 * (1 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma barH_massWeight (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)) (n : ℕ)
    (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    massWeightPoly (covBarH n l φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial (2 * (1 + n)) (covBarH n l φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_H
declarations.doc:
The Higgs tower transforms under the Lorentz group as the covariant derivatives of a
Lorentz scalar. Each derivative slot mixes by the Lorentz matrix, and the value index is
inert.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_H : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentzGroup
    (Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) HiggsVec) (fun {n} => covH n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_barH
declarations.doc:
The conjugate Higgs tower transforms as the covariant derivatives of a Lorentz scalar,
through the conjugate of the trivial representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_barH : IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentzGroup
    (Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) HiggsVec).conj (fun {n} => covBarH n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_H_apply
declarations.doc:
The pointwise form of `repLorentz_H`. The Lorentz action rotates the derivative indices
of a Higgs symbol, and the value index is inert.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_H_apply (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) (n : ℕ)
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup g (covH n l φ) = ∑ (a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
      (∏ (i : Fin n), (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) • covH n a φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_barH_apply
declarations.doc: The pointwise form of `repLorentz_barH`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_barH_apply (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec))
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup g (covBarH n l φ) = ∑ (a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
      (∏ (i : Fin n), (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) • covBarH n a φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The subalgebra of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` generated by the Higgs, its conjugate and all
their derivatives.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def higgsAlgebra :
    Subalgebra ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.covH_mem_higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc: A Higgs symbol lies in the Higgs algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma covH_mem_higgsAlgebra {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) : covH n d φ ∈ higgsAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.covBarH_mem_higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc: A conjugate Higgs symbol lies in the Higgs algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma covBarH_mem_higgsAlgebra {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)) : covBarH n d φ ∈ higgsAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsAlgebra_induction
declarations.doc:
Induction on the Higgs algebra. A property of elements of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` which
holds on every Higgs and conjugate Higgs symbol and on every scalar, and is closed under sums and
products of elements of the algebra, holds on the whole algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsAlgebra_induction {P : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra → Prop}
    (hH : ∀ (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec),
      P (covH n d φ))
    (hbarH : ∀ (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)),
      P (covBarH n d φ))
    (halg : ∀ r : ℂ, P (algebraMap ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra r))
    (hadd : ∀ x y, x ∈ higgsAlgebra → y ∈ higgsAlgebra → P x → P y → P (x + y))
    (hmul : ∀ x y, x ∈ higgsAlgebra → y ∈ higgsAlgebra → P x → P y → P (x * y))
    {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ higgsAlgebra) : P x

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.commute_of_mem_higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc: Any two elements of the Higgs algebra commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_mem_higgsAlgebra {x y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ higgsAlgebra)
    (hy : y ∈ higgsAlgebra) : Commute x y

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mul_comm_of_le_higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc: Two submodules of the Higgs algebra commute.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgs
declarations.doc: The component `∇_d H^i` in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def higgs
    {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggs
declarations.doc: The component `∇_d H̄^i` in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def barHiggs
    {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_higgsComponent
declarations.doc:
The gauge group mixes the components of `∇_d H` by the matrix `u⁻³ g⁻¹` of the
hypercharge and `SU(2)` parts of `g⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_higgsComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (higgs d i) =
      ∑ j, (((g⁻¹).toU1 : ℂ) ^ 3 * (g⁻¹).toSU2.1 i j) • higgs d j

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_barHiggsComponent
declarations.doc: The gauge group mixes the components of `∇_d H̄` by the conjugate matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_barHiggsComponent (g : GaugeGroupI) {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (barHiggs d i) =
      ∑ j, (starRingEnd ℂ (((g⁻¹).toU1 : ℂ) ^ 3 * (g⁻¹).toSU2.1 i j)) • barHiggs d j

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The submodule of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` generated by the Higgs symbols carrying `n`
derivatives, the join, over the Lorentz indices `d`, of the ranges of the symbol maps `H n d`. Its
elements are the terms linear in `∇_d H` — of mass dimension `1 + n`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def higgsSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The submodule of `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` generated by the conjugate Higgs symbols
carrying `n` derivatives, the join, over the Lorentz indices `d`, of the ranges of the symbol maps
`barH n d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def barHiggsSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsSubmodule_eq_iSup_span
declarations.doc: The Higgs submodule is spanned by the components `∇_d H^j`.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsSubmodule_eq_iSup_span (n : ℕ) :
    higgsSubmodule n = ⨆ (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (j : Fin 2), ℂ ∙ higgs d j

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmodule_eq_iSup_span
declarations.doc: The conjugate Higgs submodule is spanned by the components `∇_d H̄^j`.
declarations.statement:
lemma barHiggsSubmodule_eq_iSup_span (n : ℕ) :
    barHiggsSubmodule n
      = ⨆ (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (j : Fin 2), ℂ ∙ barHiggs d j

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsSubmodule_le_higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc: The Higgs submodule lies in the Higgs algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsSubmodule_le_higgsAlgebra (n : ℕ) :
    higgsSubmodule n ≤ Subalgebra.toSubmodule higgsAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmodule_le_higgsAlgebra
declarations.doc: The conjugate Higgs submodule lies in the Higgs algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma barHiggsSubmodule_le_higgsAlgebra (n : ℕ) :
    barHiggsSubmodule n ≤ Subalgebra.toSubmodule higgsAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmodule_comm_higgsSubmodule
declarations.doc: The conjugate Higgs and Higgs submodules commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma barHiggsSubmodule_comm_higgsSubmodule (n1 n2 : ℕ) :
    (barHiggsSubmodule n1) * (higgsSubmodule n2)
    =  (higgsSubmodule n2)  * (barHiggsSubmodule n1)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsSubmodule_comm_higgsSubmodule
declarations.doc: Two Higgs submodules commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsSubmodule_comm_higgsSubmodule (n1 n2 : ℕ) :
    (higgsSubmodule n1) * (higgsSubmodule n2)
    =  (higgsSubmodule n2)  * (higgsSubmodule n1)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmodule_comm_barHiggsSubmodule
declarations.doc: Two conjugate Higgs submodules commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma barHiggsSubmodule_comm_barHiggsSubmodule (n1 n2 : ℕ) :
    (barHiggsSubmodule n1) * (barHiggsSubmodule n2)
    =  (barHiggsSubmodule n2)  * (barHiggsSubmodule n1)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggs_higgs_left_comm
declarations.doc:
A conjugate Higgs submodule commutes past a Higgs submodule standing in front of a third
factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma barHiggs_higgs_left_comm (n1 n2 : ℕ) (C : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    barHiggsSubmodule n1 * (higgsSubmodule n2 * C)
      = higgsSubmodule n2 * (barHiggsSubmodule n1 * C)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_gaugeTorusGen_higgs
declarations.doc:
The torus generators act on `∇_d H^j` by the character of weight
`(0, 0, -isoWeight j, -3)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_gaugeTorusGen_higgs (i : Fin 4) {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (j : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (higgs d j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (0, 0, -isoWeight j, -3) i) • higgs d j

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_gaugeTorusGen_barHiggs
declarations.doc:
The torus generators act on `∇_d H̄^j` by the character of weight
`(0, 0, isoWeight j, 3)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_gaugeTorusGen_barHiggs (i : Fin 4) {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (j : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (barHiggs d j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (0, 0, isoWeight j, 3) i) • barHiggs d j

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.iSup_span_le_eigenspace
declarations.doc: The span of a family of eigenvectors of a torus generator lies in its eigenspace.
declarations.statement:
lemma iSup_span_le_eigenspace {ι : Type} (i : Fin 4) (y : ι → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (w : GaugeWeight)
    (hy : ∀ d, repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (y d) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i) • y d) :
    (⨆ d, ℂ ∙ y d)
      ≤ Module.End.eigenspace (repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i)) ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.doubletGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the span of a two-component family `x d j` of torus
eigenvectors, the components `x d 0` of weight `w₀` and `x d 1` of weight `w₁ ≠ w₀`. The
weight-`w₀` piece is the span of the `x d 0` and the weight-`w₁` piece that of the
`x d 1`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def doubletGaugeWeight {ι : Type} (x : ι → Fin 2 → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (w₀ w₁ : GaugeWeight) (hw : w₀ ≠ w₁)
    (hx₀ : ∀ (i : Fin 4) (d : ι),
      repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (x d 0) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w₀.coord i) • x d 0)
    (hx₁ : ∀ (i : Fin 4) (d : ι),
      repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (x d 1) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w₁.coord i) • x d 1) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (⨆ (d : ι) (j : Fin 2), ℂ ∙ x d j)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the Higgs submodule. `∇_d H⁰` spans the piece of
weight `(0, 0, -1, -3)` and `∇_d H¹` that of weight `(0, 0, 1, -3)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight (n : ℕ) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (higgsSubmodule n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the conjugate Higgs submodule. `∇_d H̄⁰` spans the
piece of weight `(0, 0, 1, 3)` and `∇_d H̄¹` that of weight `(0, 0, -1, 3)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight (n : ℕ) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (barHiggsSubmodule n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotGaugeHiggs
declarations.doc: The gauge-invariant pairing `∇_{d1} H^j ∇_{d2} H̄^j`, summed over the isospin index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dotGaugeHiggs
    {n1 n2 : ℕ} (d1 : Fin n1 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (d2 : Fin n2 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_dotGaugeHiggs_invariant
declarations.doc:
The pairing is gauge invariant, since the matrix acting on `H` is unitary, and `H̄` transforms
by its conjugate.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_dotGaugeHiggs_invariant {n1 n2 : ℕ} (g : GaugeGroupI) (d1 : Fin n1 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d2 : Fin n2 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (dotGaugeHiggs d1 d2) = dotGaugeHiggs d1 d2

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_higgs
declarations.doc: The Lorentz action rotates the derivative indices of a Higgs component.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_higgs {n : ℕ} (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (k : Fin 2) :
    repLorentzGroup g (higgs d k) = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
      (∏ j, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a j) (d j) : ℝ) : ℂ)) • higgs a k

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_barHiggs
declarations.doc: The Lorentz action rotates the derivative indices of a conjugate Higgs component.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_barHiggs {n : ℕ} (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (k : Fin 2) :
    repLorentzGroup g (barHiggs d k) = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
      (∏ j, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a j) (d j) : ℝ) : ℂ)) • barHiggs a k

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_dotGaugeHiggs
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the Higgs inner product. The two factors' derivative indices
rotate independently, and the inner product itself is a Lorentz scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_dotGaugeHiggs {m n : ℕ} (g : SL(2,ℂ))
    (d₁ : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (d₂ : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup g (dotGaugeHiggs d₁ d₂) =
      ∑ a₁ : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ a₂ : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        ((∏ j, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a₁ j) (d₁ j) : ℝ) : ℂ)) *
          (∏ j, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a₂ j) (d₂ j) : ℝ) : ℂ))) •
          dotGaugeHiggs a₁ a₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
All terms built from the Higgs symbols and their derivatives which have mass weight
exactly `n`, the intersection of the algebra generated by every `∇_d H` and `∇_d H̄` with
the part on which `massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ n`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff
declarations.doc:
An element has mass weight `n` when it lies in the Higgs algebra and `massWeightPoly`
scales it by `X ^ n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff {n : ℕ} {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ massWeightSubmodule n
      ↔ x ∈ higgsAlgebra ∧ massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial n x

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightPoly_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The mass weight of an element of the weight-`n` submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule n) : massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial n x

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_higgsAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The weight-`n` submodule lies in the Higgs algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_higgsAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule n) : x ∈ higgsAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc: The scalars have mass weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero : (1 : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ≤
    massWeightSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_mul_le
declarations.doc: Mass weights add under multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_mul_le (m n : ℕ) :
    massWeightSubmodule m * massWeightSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (m + n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_higgsSubmodule_le
declarations.doc: The Higgs symbols with `n` derivatives have mass weight `2 * (1 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_higgsSubmodule_le (n : ℕ) :
    higgsSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (2 * (1 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_barHiggsSubmodule_le
declarations.doc: The conjugate Higgs symbols with `n` derivatives have mass weight `2 * (1 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_barHiggsSubmodule_le (n : ℕ) :
    barHiggsSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (2 * (1 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsAlgebra_eq_adjoin
declarations.doc:
The Higgs algebra is generated by the Higgs and conjugate Higgs towers of every
derivative order.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsAlgebra_eq_adjoin :
    higgsAlgebra = Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      (⋃ n, ((higgsSubmodule n ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule n : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
        Set fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightPoly_of_mem_higgsSubmodule_sup
declarations.doc:
`massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ (2 * (1 + n))` on the Higgs and conjugate Higgs
towers with `n` derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_of_mem_higgsSubmodule_sup (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ x ∈ higgsSubmodule n ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule n,
      massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial (2 * (1 + n)) x

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq
declarations.doc: Weight zero is the scalars, as every Higgs tower has positive weight.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero_eq : massWeightSubmodule 0 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq
declarations.doc:
