The weight recursion. A term of positive mass weight `i` is a sum of symbols of weight
`i` and of products of two terms of lower positive weight adding up to `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    massWeightSubmodule i
      = (⨆ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin i => 2 * (1 + (k : ℕ)) = i),
          higgsSubmodule (k : ℕ) ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule (k : ℕ))
        ⊔ (⨆ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin i × Fin i => (p.1 : ℕ) + (p.2 : ℕ) = i),
            massWeightSubmodule (p.1 : ℕ) * massWeightSubmodule (p.2 : ℕ))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul
declarations.doc:
Removing the leftmost Higgs tower. A term of positive weight `w` is a sum of products
of a tower `∇ⁿH` or `∇ⁿH̄`, of weight `2 * (1 + n) ≤ w`, with a term of the remaining
weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul (w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) :
    massWeightSubmodule w
      = ⨆ n ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun n => 2 * (1 + n) ≤ w),
          (higgsSubmodule n ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule n) * massWeightSubmodule (w - 2 * (1 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_odd_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
The odd mass weight submodules are trivial, since every Higgs tower has even weight, and
weights add under products.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_odd_eq_bot (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) :
    massWeightSubmodule n = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the mass weight submodules. By recursion on the
weight through `massWeightSubmodule_eq`. A term of weight `i` is either a symbol of that
weight — decomposed by `higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight` and `barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight` — or
a product of two terms of lower positive weight, decomposed by `mul` from the
decompositions supplied by the recursion.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeight :
    (i : ℕ) → 0 < i → GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (massWeightSubmodule i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightOfNeZero
declarations.doc: The `NeZero` form of `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeight`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightOfNeZero (i : ℕ) [NeZero i] :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (massWeightSubmodule i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_two_eq
declarations.doc: Weight two is the underived Higgs and conjugate Higgs.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_two_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 2 = higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_four_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight four is spanned by the once-derived symbols and the products of two underived ones. The
leftmost tower is underived, leaving weight two, or once-derived, leaving weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_four_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 4 = higgsSubmodule 1 ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule 1 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔ higgsSubmodule 0 *
    barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_six_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight six is spanned by the twice-derived symbols, a once-derived symbol against an underived
one, and the products of three underived ones. The leftmost tower leaves weight four, two or
zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_six_eq : massWeightSubmodule 6 =
    -- The derivative terms
    higgsSubmodule 2 ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule 2 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 1 * higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 1 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    barHiggsSubmodule 1 * higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    barHiggsSubmodule 1 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    -- The potential terms
    higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0  ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq
declarations.doc:
Weight eight is spanned by the derivative terms with up to three derivatives, and the products
of four underived symbols. The leftmost tower leaves weight six, four, two or zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq :
    massWeightSubmodule 8 =
      -- The derivative terms
    higgsSubmodule 3 ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule 3 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 2 * higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 2 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 2 ⊔
    barHiggsSubmodule 2 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 1 * higgsSubmodule 1 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 1 * barHiggsSubmodule 1 ⊔
    barHiggsSubmodule 1 * barHiggsSubmodule 1 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 1 * higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 1 * higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 1 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 1 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 1 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    barHiggsSubmodule 1 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    -- The potential terms
    higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    higgsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 ⊔
    barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 * barHiggsSubmodule 0 *
      barHiggsSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.gaugeInvariantOfMassDim
declarations.doc: The gauge invariants of a given mass weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeInvariantOfMassDim (M : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

modules.title: The derivative submodules of the scalar sector
modules.doc:
The span of the Higgs and conjugate Higgs symbols with a fixed number of derivatives.

## i. Overview

The scalar symbols (the Higgs and its conjugate) carrying a fixed number `n` of derivatives
span the submodule `derivSubmodule n`. The Higgs is bosonic, so these submodules commute
with one another, and since neither the gauge nor the Lorentz action changes the number
of derivatives they are closed under both.

The gauge weight decomposition of these submodules lives in `GaugeWeight.lean`,
and the sign they carry at the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` in `Centre.lean`.

## ii. Key results

- `derivSubmodule` : the submodule of the covariant field algebra generated by the Higgs symbols
  and their conjugates carrying `n` derivatives.
- `commute_of_mem_derivSubmodule` : any element of a derivative submodule commutes with any element
  of any derivative submodule, the Higgs being bosonic.
- `derivSubmodule_map_rep_le`, `derivSubmodule_map_repLorentz_le` : the derivative submodules are
  closed under the gauge and Lorentz actions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The derivative submodules of the scalar sector

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The derivative submodules of the scalar sector

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The submodule of the covariant field algebra generated by the Higgs symbols and their
conjugates carrying `n` derivatives.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivSubmodule (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_le_ker_H
declarations.doc: Every element of a derivative submodule commutes with a fixed Higgs symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_ker_H {n k : ℕ} (d : Fin k → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) :
    derivSubmodule n
      ≤ LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.mulLeft ℂ (covH k d φ)
        - LinearMap.mulRight ℂ (covH k d φ))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_le_ker_barH
declarations.doc:
Every element of a derivative submodule commutes with a fixed conjugate-Higgs
symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_ker_barH {n k : ℕ} (d : Fin k → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)) :
    derivSubmodule n
      ≤ LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.mulLeft ℂ (covBarH k d φ)
        - LinearMap.mulRight ℂ (covBarH k d φ))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.commute_of_mem_derivSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Any element of a derivative submodule commutes with any element of any derivative
submodule, the Higgs being bosonic.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_mem_derivSubmodule {n m : ℕ} {x y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ derivSubmodule n) (hy : y ∈ derivSubmodule m) : Commute x y

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_mul_comm
declarations.doc:
Derivative submodules commute with one another at the level of submodule
products.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_mul_comm (n m : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n * derivSubmodule m = derivSubmodule m * derivSubmodule n

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_map_rep_le
declarations.doc:
The derivative submodules are closed under the gauge action, each symbol being carried
to a symbol with the same number of derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_map_rep_le (n : ℕ) (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    (derivSubmodule n).map (repGaugeGroupI g) ≤ derivSubmodule n

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_map_repLorentz_le
declarations.doc:
The derivative submodules are closed under the Lorentz action, since the Lorentz group
only mixes the derivative indices within a fixed number of derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_map_repLorentz_le (n : ℕ) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    (derivSubmodule n).map (repLorentzGroup Λ) ≤ derivSubmodule n

modules.title: The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` on the scalar sector
modules.doc:
The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `+1` on the Higgs derivative submodules.

## i. Overview

The Higgs is a Lorentz scalar, so the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on its derivative submodules by
`+1`. The covariant-derivative slots mix by the Lorentz matrix, which is the identity at the
centre, and the value index is inert because the value space carries the trivial
representation. The conjugate tower is the same, conjugation of the trivial representation
being trivial again.

This is the integer-spin half of the parity count the Yukawa classification runs. Paired with
`StandardModel.FermionSector.derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace`, which gives the fermions
`-1`, it makes a product with a single fermion factor carry `-1`, and a subspace of sign `-1`
carries no Lorentz invariant.

## ii. Key results

- `range_covH_le_centreEigenspace` : the Higgs symbols carry the sign `+1`, their value space
  being a Lorentz scalar.
- `range_covBarH_le_centreEigenspace` : the conjugate Higgs symbols carry the sign `+1`, for the
  same reason.
- `derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace` : the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the Higgs derivative
  submodules by `+1`, for any number of covariant derivatives.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The two towers
- B. The Higgs derivative submodules

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The two towers

Each tower feeds `range_le_centreEigenspace` with its own Lorentz law and the sign of its
value space, which is `+1` for both. The value space of the Higgs tower carries the trivial
representation and that of the conjugate tower its conjugate.

## B. The Higgs derivative submodules

The derivative submodule is the join of the two towers over the derivative slots, and an
eigenspace is closed under joins.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.range_covH_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: The Higgs symbols carry the sign `+1`, their value space being a Lorentz scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_covH_le_centreEigenspace (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    LinearMap.range (covH n l) ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentzGroup 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.range_covBarH_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: The conjugate Higgs symbols carry the sign `+1`, for the same reason.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_covBarH_le_centreEigenspace (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    LinearMap.range (covBarH n l) ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentzGroup 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the Higgs derivative submodules by `+1`, for any
number of covariant derivatives. The Higgs is a Lorentz scalar and the derivative slots are
inert at the centre.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_centreEigenspace (n : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentzGroup 1

modules.title: The gauge weight decomposition of the scalar sector
modules.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the Higgs derivative submodules and the weights that occur.

## i. Overview

The Higgs and conjugate-Higgs submodules carrying `n` derivatives each come with a gauge
weight decomposition, and the two join to one of `derivSubmodule n`. The weights that
occur are the two Higgs weights `(0, 0, ∓1, -3)` and the two conjugate-Higgs weights
`(0, 0, ±1, 3)`; they do not depend on the number of derivatives.

## ii. Key results

- `derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight` : the gauge weight decomposition of the Higgs derivative
  submodules.
- `derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_supp` : the gauge weights occurring in the Higgs derivative
  submodules, the two Higgs weights `(0, 0, ∓1, -3)` and the two conjugate-Higgs weights
  `(0, 0, ±1, 3)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gauge weight decomposition

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The gauge weight decomposition

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the Higgs derivative submodules, the join of
the decompositions of the Higgs and conjugate-Higgs submodules, whose weights are
`(0, 0, ∓1, -3)` and `(0, 0, ±1, 3)` respectively.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight (n : ℕ) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (derivSubmodule n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_supp
declarations.doc:
The gauge weights occurring in the Higgs derivative submodules are the two Higgs
weights `(0, 0, ∓1, -3)` and the two conjugate-Higgs weights `(0, 0, ±1, 3)`.

modules.title: The mass-weight grading of the scalar sector, in derivative submodules
modules.doc:
The mass-weight submodules of the scalar sector up to weight eight, written with the derivative
submodules.

## i. Overview

The mass-weight submodules of the scalar sector are described in
`ScalarSector/Basic.lean` in terms of the Higgs and conjugate-Higgs submodules
separately. Since the two always occur together, the description is cleaner in terms
of the derivative submodules `derivSubmodule n = higgsSubmodule n ⊔ barHiggsSubmodule n`.
A Higgs tower with `n` derivatives has mass weight `2 * (1 + n)`, twice its mass dimension
`1 + n`, only even weights are non-zero, and the mass weights up to eight (mass dimension
at most four) are the partitions of the weight into such towers.

## ii. Key results

- `derivSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmodule` : the derivative submodule sits in the mass-weight
  submodule of weight `2 * (1 + n)`.
- `massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_derivSubmodule_mul` : removing the leftmost Higgs tower, a term
  of positive weight `w` is a sum of products of a tower `derivSubmodule n`, of weight
  `2 * (1 + n) ≤ w`, with a term of the remaining weight.
- `massWeightSubmodule_two_eq_deriv` up to `massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq_deriv` : the mass
  weights up to eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight grading in derivative submodules

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mass-weight grading in derivative submodules

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The derivative submodule sits in the mass-weight submodule of weight `2 * (1 + n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    derivSubmodule n ≤ massWeightSubmodule (2 * (1 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_derivSubmodule_mul
declarations.doc:
Removing the leftmost Higgs tower, written with the derivative submodules. A term of
positive weight `w` is a sum of products of a tower `derivSubmodule n`, of weight
`2 * (1 + n) ≤ w`, with a term of the remaining weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_derivSubmodule_mul (w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) :
    massWeightSubmodule w
      = ⨆ n ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun n => 2 * (1 + n) ≤ w),
          derivSubmodule n * massWeightSubmodule (w - 2 * (1 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_two_eq_deriv
declarations.doc: Weight two is the underived Higgs symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_two_eq_deriv :
    massWeightSubmodule 2 = derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_four_eq_deriv
declarations.doc:
Weight four. The leftmost tower is underived, leaving weight two, which is an underived
tower, or once-derived, leaving weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_four_eq_deriv :
    massWeightSubmodule 4
      = derivSubmodule 1 ⊔ derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_six_eq_deriv
declarations.doc:
Weight six. The leftmost tower leaves weight four, two or zero. The product of an
underived tower with a once-derived one occurs in both orders, which agree by
`derivSubmodule_mul_comm`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_six_eq_deriv :
    massWeightSubmodule 6
      = derivSubmodule 2 ⊔ derivSubmodule 1 * derivSubmodule 0
        ⊔ derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq_deriv
declarations.doc:
Weight eight. The leftmost tower leaves weight six, four, two or zero. Products that
differ only in the order of commuting towers agree by `derivSubmodule_mul_comm`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eight_eq_deriv :
    massWeightSubmodule 8
      = derivSubmodule 3 ⊔ derivSubmodule 2 * derivSubmodule 0
        ⊔ derivSubmodule 1 * derivSubmodule 1
        ⊔ derivSubmodule 1 * derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0
        ⊔ derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0
          * derivSubmodule 0

modules.title: The gauge weight decomposition of the Higgs mass-weight submodules
modules.doc:
The gauge invariants of the scalar sector up to mass weight eight, through the torus weights
and the isospin classifiers.

## i. Overview

Each mass-weight submodule of the scalar sector up to weight eight has an explicit
description in terms of the derivative submodules `derivSubmodule n`, and each derivative
submodule carries a gauge weight decomposition.  Transporting the latter along the former
decomposes every mass-weight submodule up to weight eight.

The weights carried by a derivative submodule are the four weights of the Higgs doublet
and its conjugate, `(0, 0, ∓1, -3)` and `(0, 0, ±1, 3)`.  Every one of them has
hypercharge `± 3`, so a product of `k` derivative submodules can only reach gauge weight
zero when `k` is even and the Higgs and conjugate-Higgs factors are equally many.  This
is what makes the weight-zero pieces small: at mass weight four and six they are spanned
by the isospin-diagonal pairings `∇H^i ∇H̄^i`, and at mass weight eight the quartic
monomials `∇H^i ∇H̄^i ∇H^j ∇H̄^j` join them.

The gauge weight alone cannot finish the job: it cannot separate the isospin singlet
`∇H · ∇H̄` from the neutral component of the isospin triplet, which carries the same
weight.  That separation is `SU(2)` mathematics and belongs to the isospin classifiers of
`GaugeGroup.Invariants` rather than here.  What is left for this file is to present each
surviving piece as a family those classifiers know.  A conjugate Higgs symbol against a
Higgs symbol is a family with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental isospin index — the conjugate
symbol carries the fundamental isospin index and the Higgs symbol the anti-fundamental one, so it
goes
second — and the delta contraction, which spans its invariants, is the isospin contraction
`dotGaugeHiggs`.  The quartic is a family with four fundamental indices once its two Higgs
symbols are re-indexed by the antisymmetric symbol, and of its two epsilon contractions
one is the square of the isospin contraction and the other vanishes, pairing commuting
factors antisymmetrically.

Sections F and G are reductions for the gauge group, stated modulo any gauge-stable
submodule `S`, which is what lets the other sectors be carried along; taking `S` trivial in
section H recovers the statements about the mass-weight submodules themselves.

## ii. Key results

- `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightTwo` up to `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight` : the gauge
  weight decompositions of the mass-weight submodules up to weight eight.
- `massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight_piece_zero` : the weight-zero piece at mass weight eight.
- `isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_isoFamily`, `isEquivariant_isospinQuadFund_quadFamily` : the
  Higgs symbols as isospin families.
- `reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_four` up to
  `reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_eight` : the gauge classification up to mass weight
  eight, modulo a gauge-stable submodule.
- `gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_four_eq_dotSpan` up to `gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_eight_eq_dotSpan` :
  the gauge-invariant submodules up to mass weight eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The decompositions
- B. The pieces of a derivative submodule
- C. The weight-zero pieces of the products
- D. The weight-zero pieces of the mass-weight submodules
- E. The Higgs symbols as isospin families
- F. The isospin spans reduce to the isospin contractions
- G. The gauge classification up to mass weight eight
- H. The gauge-invariant submodules up to mass weight eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The decompositions

Every term of the Higgs algebra has even mass weight, so the odd mass-weight submodules
vanish (`massWeightSubmodule_odd_eq_bot`). The even ones are built from the
derivative submodules by the descriptions of `MassWeight/Basic.lean`. Weight two is a single
derivative submodule, and the higher weights add the products which distribute the mass
weight over several towers.

## B. The pieces of a derivative submodule

A derivative submodule is the join of a Higgs and a conjugate-Higgs submodule, and each of
those is concentrated in two weights.  The four weights are distinct, so each piece of the
join is the span of one of the four families of symbols, and every other weight — the zero
weight in particular — has vanishing piece.

## C. The weight-zero pieces of the products

Two derivative submodules pair to weight zero exactly by matching a Higgs symbol against a
conjugate-Higgs symbol of the same isospin component, in either order, so the weight-zero
piece of such a product is a join of four spans of pairings `∇H^i ∇H̄^i`.  Three of them
cannot reach weight zero at all, because hypercharge is `± 3` on every generator, so an odd
number of factors leaves an odd multiple of three.  Four of them reach weight zero on the
three quartic monomials.

## D. The weight-zero pieces of the mass-weight submodules

Assembling section C along the descriptions of section A gives the weight-zero piece of
each mass-weight submodule up to weight eight.  The odd weights and weight two are trivial,
weight four is the underived pairing, weight six adds the pairings with one derivative on
either factor, and weight eight adds the pairings with two derivatives, those with one
derivative on each factor, and the three quartic monomials.

## E. The Higgs symbols as isospin families

The gauge weight has done all it can.  What it cannot see is the difference between the
isospin singlet `∇H · ∇H̄` and the neutral component of the isospin triplet: both are
neutral under the torus, so both sit in the weight-zero piece, and only the non-abelian
part of `SU(2)` tells them apart.  That is what the isospin classifiers of
`GaugeGroup.Invariants` are for, and this section presents the surviving pieces as
families they classify.

The variance has to be read off correctly, and it is opposite to what the notation
suggests.  A conjugate Higgs symbol carries a fundamental isospin index — an isospin
transformation moves it by the matrix of the `SU(2)` element, with the summed index in the
row slot — and a Higgs symbol carries an anti-fundamental one, moved by the conjugate
matrix.  So the pairing span of section C is the span of the components of
`fun l => barHiggs d' (l 0) * higgs d (l 1)`, conjugate symbol first, which is an
family with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental isospin index; and its delta contraction, which
spans its invariants, is the isospin contraction `dotGaugeHiggs`.  That identification is the whole
point of the section: `dotSpan` is the span of delta contractions, and nothing else
survives.

The quartic needs four fundamental indices, so its two Higgs symbols must be re-indexed by
the antisymmetric symbol first.  `tildeHiggs` is that re-index, `H̃⁰ = H¹` and
`H̃¹ = -H⁰`, and it is fundamental because `SU(2)` is pseudo-real.  The quartic family is
then a product of four fundamental families, and `IsospinQuadFund` classifies it.  Its
two epsilon contractions come out as the square of the isospin contraction and zero:
the second pairs the two conjugate symbols with each other and the two Higgs symbols with
each other, and an antisymmetric contraction of two commuting factors vanishes.

## F. The isospin spans reduce to the isospin contractions

The classification is wanted not for the mass-weight submodule alone but modulo a
submodule `S` gathering the other sectors, so every step is a reduction in the sense of
`ReducesInvariantsTo`: a gauge invariant of `V ⊔ S`, for `S` gauge stable, lies in `W ⊔ S`.

The weight-zero pieces of section D are joins of spans of isospin families.
`IsospinFundAntiFund.reducesInvariantsTo_span_deltaContraction` reduces each
span, for the isospin factor and hence for the gauge group, to the line through its delta
contraction, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup` joins the families. The join asks each span to
be gauge stable, which is `isoFamily_span_stable` and is why the enlargement is `isoSpan`
rather than the pairing span of section C: the pairing span keeps only the diagonal
components and a gauge transformation does not. It asks the target to be gauge stable too,
and the isospin contractions are gauge invariant.

## G. The gauge classification up to mass weight eight

Section F is now run at each weight in turn, after the torus has put a gauge invariant in
the weight-zero piece (`GaugeWeightDecomposition.reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero`). Weight
two dies outright, its weight-zero piece being trivial: a single Higgs symbol carries
hypercharge. Weights four and six are joins of isospin spans and nothing else, so what is
left are the isospin contractions of the towers occurring at that weight: the Higgs mass
term at weight four, and its once-derived companions at weight six.

Weight eight adds the quartic. `IsospinQuadFund` reduces its span to the two epsilon
contractions, the first the square of the underived isospin contraction and the second
zero. The quartic span is joined with the three isospin spans by `ReducesInvariantsTo.sup`,
which asks stability of the isospin spans only, not of the quartic span.

## H. The gauge-invariant submodules up to mass weight eight

Taking the stable submodule to be the trivial one turns section G into a statement about
the mass-weight submodules themselves, and both inclusions are then available: section G
bounds the invariants from above, and the isospin contractions are themselves gauge
invariant and of the right mass weight, which bounds them from below.  The two meet, so
the gauge-invariant part of each mass-weight submodule up to weight eight is exactly
described.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightTwo
declarations.doc: Weight two is the underived Higgs tower.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightTwo :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (massWeightSubmodule 2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightFour
declarations.doc:
Weight four is the once-derived tower together with the products of two underived
ones.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightFour :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (massWeightSubmodule 4)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix
declarations.doc:
Weight six is the twice-derived tower, the once-derived tower against an underived
one, and the products of three underived ones.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (massWeightSubmodule 6)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight
declarations.doc:
Weight eight is the thrice-derived tower, the two ways of splitting the derivatives over
two towers, the once-derived tower against two underived ones, and the products of four
underived ones.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI (massWeightSubmodule 8)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_eq
declarations.doc:
The weight-`w` piece of a derivative submodule, as the join of the Higgs and
conjugate-Higgs pieces.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_eq (n : ℕ) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece w
      = (if w = ((0, 0, -1, -3) : GaugeWeight) then
          ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ higgs d 0
        else if w = ((0, 0, 1, -3) : GaugeWeight) then
          ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ higgs d 1
        else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if w = ((0, 0, 1, 3) : GaugeWeight) then
            ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ barHiggs d 0
          else if w = ((0, 0, -1, 3) : GaugeWeight) then
            ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ barHiggs d 1
          else ⊥)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_higgs_zero
declarations.doc: The piece at the weight of the upper Higgs component.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_higgs_zero (n : ℕ) :
    (derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece (0, 0, -1, -3)
      = ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ higgs d 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_higgs_one
declarations.doc: The piece at the weight of the lower Higgs component.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_higgs_one (n : ℕ) :
    (derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece (0, 0, 1, -3)
      = ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ higgs d 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_barHiggs_zero
declarations.doc: The piece at the weight of the upper conjugate-Higgs component.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_barHiggs_zero (n : ℕ) :
    (derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece (0, 0, 1, 3)
      = ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ barHiggs d 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_barHiggs_one
declarations.doc: The piece at the weight of the lower conjugate-Higgs component.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_barHiggs_one (n : ℕ) :
    (derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece (0, 0, -1, 3)
      = ⨆ d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ℂ ∙ barHiggs d 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
A derivative submodule has no weight-zero content, since every Higgs symbol carries
hypercharge.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight_piece_zero (n : ℕ) :
    (derivSubmoduleGaugeWeight n).piece 0 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsBarHiggsSpan
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin-diagonal pairings of a Higgs symbol carrying `n` derivatives
with a conjugate-Higgs symbol carrying `m` derivatives, at isospin component `i`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def higgsBarHiggsSpan
    (n m : ℕ) (i : Fin 2) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.quarticSpan
declarations.doc:
The span of the underived quartic monomial pairing the isospin components `i` and
`j`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quarticSpan
    (i j : Fin 2) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_mul_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece of a product of two derivative submodules is spanned by the
isospin-diagonal pairings, taken in both orders of the two towers.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_mul_piece_zero (n m : ℕ) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece repGaugeGroupI (derivSubmodule n * derivSubmodule m) 0
      = higgsBarHiggsSpan n m 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan n m 1
        ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan m n 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan m n 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_mul_mul_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
A product of three derivative submodules has no weight-zero content, since the hypercharge of
three Higgs generators is an odd multiple of three.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_mul_mul_piece_zero (n m k : ℕ) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece repGaugeGroupI
      (derivSubmodule n * derivSubmodule m * derivSubmodule k) 0 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.derivSubmodule_zero_pow_four_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece of the product of four underived derivative submodules is spanned by the
three quartic monomials, the ones pairing two Higgs symbols against two conjugate ones with
matching isospin.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_zero_pow_four_piece_zero :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece repGaugeGroupI
      (derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0 * derivSubmodule 0
        * derivSubmodule 0) 0
      = quarticSpan 0 0 ⊔ quarticSpan 0 1 ⊔ quarticSpan 1 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightTwo_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece at mass weight two is trivial, since a single Higgs symbol carries
hypercharge.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightTwo_piece_zero :
    (massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightTwo).piece 0 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightFour_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece at mass weight four is spanned by the underived isospin-diagonal
pairings.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightFour_piece_zero :
    (massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightFour).piece 0
      = higgsBarHiggsSpan 0 0 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 0 0 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece at mass weight six is spanned by the isospin-diagonal pairings carrying
one derivative, on either of the two factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix_piece_zero :
    (massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightSix).piece 0
      = higgsBarHiggsSpan 1 0 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 1 0 1
        ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 0 1 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 0 1 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece at mass weight eight is spanned by the isospin-diagonal pairings carrying
two derivatives on one factor or one on each, together with the three quartic monomials.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight_piece_zero :
    (massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight).piece 0
      = higgsBarHiggsSpan 2 0 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 2 0 1
        ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 0 2 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 0 2 1
        ⊔ (higgsBarHiggsSpan 1 1 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan 1 1 1)
        ⊔ (quarticSpan 0 0 ⊔ quarticSpan 0 1 ⊔ quarticSpan 1 1)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_su2_higgs
declarations.doc:
An isospin transformation moves the isospin index of a Higgs symbol by the conjugate
matrix, the index of a Higgs symbol is anti-fundamental.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_su2_higgs (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) {n : ℕ}
    (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (higgs d i)
      = ∑ a, conj (V.1 a i) • higgs d a

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_su2_barHiggs
declarations.doc:
An isospin transformation moves the isospin index of a conjugate Higgs symbol by the
matrix itself, the index of a conjugate Higgs symbol is fundamental.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_su2_barHiggs (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) {n : ℕ}
    (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (barHiggs d i)
      = ∑ a, V.1 a i • barHiggs d a

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_mul_pair
declarations.doc:
A product of two symbols each moving by given coefficients moves by the product of
those coefficients.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgs_mul_barHiggs_comm
declarations.doc: A Higgs symbol commutes with a conjugate Higgs symbol, in the components.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgs_mul_barHiggs_comm {n m : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i j : Fin 2) :
    higgs d i * barHiggs d' j = barHiggs d' j * higgs d i

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgs_mul_higgs_comm
declarations.doc: Two Higgs symbols commute, in the components.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgs_mul_higgs_comm {n m : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i j : Fin 2) :
    higgs d i * higgs d' j = higgs d' j * higgs d i

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.barHiggs_mul_barHiggs_comm
declarations.doc: Two conjugate Higgs symbols commute, in the components.
declarations.statement:
lemma barHiggs_mul_barHiggs_comm {n m : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (i j : Fin 2) :
    barHiggs d i * barHiggs d' j = barHiggs d' j * barHiggs d i

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isoFamily
declarations.doc:
The isospin family of a Higgs tower carrying `n` derivatives against a conjugate tower
carrying `m`. The conjugate symbol supplies the fundamental index and so goes in the
first slot, the Higgs symbol the anti-fundamental one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isoFamily
    {n m : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : (Fin 2 → Fin 2) → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_isoFamily
declarations.doc: The isospin family carries one fundamental and one anti-fundamental isospin index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_isoFamily {n m : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((isoFamily d d') ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.deltaContraction_isoFamily
declarations.doc:
The delta contraction of the isospin family, which spans its isospin invariants, is the
isospin contraction, the Higgs mass term of the two towers.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaContraction_isoFamily {n m : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    IsospinFundAntiFund.deltaContraction (isoFamily d d') = dotGaugeHiggs d d'

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin contractions of a Higgs tower carrying `n` derivatives against
a conjugate tower carrying `m`, the gauge invariants the isospin classification leaves
at those two derivative orders.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dotSpan
    (n m : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isoFamily_span_stable
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin family is stable under the whole gauge group, since each factor of a
component goes to a combination of the factors of components.
declarations.statement:
lemma isoFamily_span_stable {n m : ℕ} (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (g : GaugeGroupI) {y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hy : y ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (isoFamily d d'))) :
    repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (isoFamily d d'))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsBarHiggsSpan_le_isoFamily_span
declarations.doc:
The isospin-diagonal pairing spans of section C sit inside the span of the isospin
family. A diagonal pairing is one of the four components, the two factors commuting.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsBarHiggsSpan_le_isoFamily_span (n m : ℕ) :
    higgsBarHiggsSpan n m 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan n m 1
      ≤ ⨆ (d : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (d' : Fin m → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
        Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (isoFamily d d'))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.tildeHiggs
declarations.doc:
The re-index of an underived Higgs symbol by the antisymmetric symbol, `H̃⁰ = H¹` and
`H̃¹ = -H⁰`.  `SU(2)` is pseudo-real, so this turns the anti-fundamental index of a Higgs
symbol into a fundamental one, which is what the quartic family needs.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tildeHiggs
  (i : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.tildeHiggs_zero
declarations.doc: The re-index at isospin zero is the Higgs symbol of isospin one.
declarations.statement:
lemma tildeHiggs_zero :
    tildeHiggs 0 = higgs (![] : Fin 0 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.tildeHiggs_one
declarations.doc: The re-index at isospin one is minus the Higgs symbol of isospin zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma tildeHiggs_one :
    tildeHiggs 1 = -higgs (![] : Fin 0 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_su2_tildeHiggs
declarations.doc:
The re-indexed Higgs symbol carries a fundamental isospin index, since the four entry
identities of `GaugeGroup.SU2Conjugation` remove every complex conjugate.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_su2_tildeHiggs (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (tildeHiggs i)
      = ∑ a, V.1 a i • tildeHiggs a

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.quadFamily
declarations.doc:
The quartic isospin family, two conjugate Higgs symbols against two re-indexed Higgs
symbols, each of the four carrying a fundamental isospin index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quadFamily :
    (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isEquivariant_isospinQuadFund_quadFamily
declarations.doc: The quartic family carries four fundamental isospin indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinQuadFund_quadFamily :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 4 => .fund) (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents quadFamily)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.epsilonContraction₁₂_quadFamily
declarations.doc:
The first epsilon contraction of the quartic family is the square of the isospin
contraction. Pairing the first conjugate symbol with the first Higgs symbol, and the
second with the second, is pairing each `H̄` with an `H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma epsilonContraction₁₂_quadFamily :
    IsospinQuadFund.epsilonContraction₁₂ quadFamily
      = dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![] * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![]

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.epsilonContraction₁₃_quadFamily
declarations.doc:
The second epsilon contraction of the quartic family vanishes. It pairs the two
conjugate symbols with each other and the two Higgs symbols with each other, and an
antisymmetric contraction of two commuting factors is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma epsilonContraction₁₃_quadFamily :
    IsospinQuadFund.epsilonContraction₁₃ quadFamily = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.quarticSpan_le_quadFamily_span
declarations.doc:
The three quartic monomials of section C lie in the span of the components of the
quartic family, each being one of those components up to a sign.
declarations.statement:
lemma quarticSpan_le_quadFamily_span :
    quarticSpan 0 0 ⊔ quarticSpan 0 1 ⊔ quarticSpan 1 1
      ≤ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range quadFamily)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isoSpan
declarations.doc:
The span of the components of all the isospin families of a Higgs tower carrying `n`
derivatives against a conjugate tower carrying `m`.  This is the gauge-stable
enlargement of the pairing span of section C.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isoSpan
    (n m : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isStableUnder_isoSpan
declarations.doc: The isospin span is stable under the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_isoSpan (n m : ℕ) :
    IsStableUnder (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGaugeGroupI g) (isoSpan n m)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isFixedBy_dotSpan
declarations.doc: The span of the isospin contractions is fixed pointwise by the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_dotSpan (n m : ℕ) :
    IsFixedBy (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGaugeGroupI g) (dotSpan n m)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsBarHiggsSpan_le_isoSpan'
declarations.doc: Each isospin-diagonal pairing span of section C sits inside the isospin span.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsBarHiggsSpan_le_isoSpan' (n m : ℕ) (i : Fin 2) :
    higgsBarHiggsSpan n m i ≤ isoSpan n m

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.higgsBarHiggsSpan_le_isoSpan
declarations.doc: The pairing span of section C sits inside the isospin span.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgsBarHiggsSpan_le_isoSpan (n m : ℕ) :
    higgsBarHiggsSpan n m 0 ⊔ higgsBarHiggsSpan n m 1 ≤ isoSpan n m

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_isoSpan
declarations.doc:
The isospin span reduces, for the gauge group, to the span of the isospin contractions.
Each family's span reduces to the line through its delta contraction, which is the
isospin contraction of the two towers.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_isoSpan (n m : ℕ) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGaugeGroupI g) (isoSpan n m) (dotSpan n m)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_two
declarations.doc:
Mass weight two reduces to `⊥` for the gauge group, since a single Higgs symbol carries
hypercharge, so the weight-zero piece is trivial.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_two :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGaugeGroupI g) (massWeightSubmodule 2) ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_four
declarations.doc:
Mass weight four reduces, for the gauge group, to the underived isospin contraction,
the Higgs mass term.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_four :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGaugeGroupI g) (massWeightSubmodule 4)
      (dotSpan 0 0)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_six
declarations.doc:
Mass weight six reduces, for the gauge group, to the isospin contractions carrying one
derivative, on either factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_six :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGaugeGroupI g) (massWeightSubmodule 6)
      (dotSpan 1 0 ⊔ dotSpan 0 1)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_eight
declarations.doc:
Mass weight eight reduces, for the gauge group, to the isospin contractions carrying two
derivatives and the square of the underived one, the quartic potential.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_eight :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGaugeGroupI g) (massWeightSubmodule 8)
      (dotSpan 2 0 ⊔ dotSpan 0 2 ⊔ dotSpan 1 1
        ⊔ ℂ ∙ (dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![] * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![]))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_dotSpan_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_four
declarations.doc:
A gauge-invariant term of mass weight four is a multiple of the underived isospin
contraction.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_dotSpan_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_six
declarations.doc:
A gauge-invariant term of mass weight six is a combination of the isospin contractions
carrying one derivative, on either factor.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_dotSpan_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_eight
declarations.doc:
A gauge-invariant term of mass weight eight is a combination of the isospin
contractions carrying two derivatives and of the square of the underived contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_dotSpan_of_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_eight {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8) (hg : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) :
    x ∈ dotSpan 2 0 ⊔ dotSpan 0 2 ⊔ dotSpan 1 1
      ⊔ ℂ ∙ (dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![] * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![])

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotGaugeHiggs_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: An isospin contraction has the mass weight of its two towers together.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotGaugeHiggs_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n1 n2 : ℕ} (d1 : Fin n1 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (d2 : Fin n2 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    dotGaugeHiggs d1 d2 ∈ massWeightSubmodule (2 * (1 + n1) + 2 * (1 + n2))

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_four_eq_dotSpan
declarations.doc: The gauge invariants of mass weight four are the underived isospin contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_four_eq_dotSpan :
    gaugeInvariantOfMassDim 4 = dotSpan 0 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_six_eq_dotSpan
declarations.doc:
The gauge invariants of mass weight six are the isospin contractions with one derivative
on either factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_six_eq_dotSpan :
    gaugeInvariantOfMassDim 6 = dotSpan 1 0 ⊔ dotSpan 0 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_eight_eq_dotSpan
declarations.doc:
The gauge invariants of mass weight eight are the isospin contractions with two
derivatives distributed over the two factors, together with the square of the underived
contraction — the quartic potential.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeInvariantOfMassDim_eight_eq_dotSpan :
    gaugeInvariantOfMassDim 8 = dotSpan 2 0 ⊔ dotSpan 0 2 ⊔ dotSpan 1 1
      ⊔ ℂ ∙ (dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![] * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![])

modules.title: The Higgs invariants of mass weight eight
modules.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of the scalar sector at mass weight eight, the kinetic term,
the two box terms and the quartic potential.

## i. Overview

Mass weight eight is where the scalar sector says what it is for.  The gauge classification
of `reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_eight` leaves four things: the isospin
contractions carrying two derivatives on one tower or one on each, and the square of the
underived contraction.  The Lorentz classification then contracts the derivative indices.

The Higgs is a Lorentz scalar, so the only covector indices at this weight are the two
derivative slots, and two covector indices admit exactly one invariant contraction, the
metric trace, `RankTwo.metric`.  Contracting the mixed family gives the kinetic term
`∂^μ H† ∂_μ H`; contracting the two families carrying both derivatives on one tower gives
`□H† H` and `H† □H`.  The square of the underived contraction has no index to contract and
survives as it stands as the quartic potential `(H† H)²`.

So the four surviving terms are the quartic potential, the kinetic term and the two
box terms, and `lorentzContractionEightSpan` is their span.

Everything is stated modulo a submodule `S` stable under both groups, which is what lets
the other sectors be carried along.

## ii. Key results

- `lorentzContractionEightSpan` : the gauge and Lorentz invariants of the scalar sector at mass
  weight eight, the two box terms `□H† H` and `H† □H`, the kinetic term `∂^μ H† ∂_μ H`, and the
  quartic potential `(H† H)²`.
- `reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionEightSpan` : mass weight eight reduces to that span for
  the gauge and Lorentz groups together.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the classification at
  mass weight eight as an equivalence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The isospin contractions with two derivatives as bi-Lorentz tensors
- B. The metric contraction is fixed by both groups
- C. The invariants of mass weight eight
- D. The span consists of invariants of mass weight eight
- E. The classification

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The isospin contractions with two derivatives as bi-Lorentz tensors

Two derivatives can sit both on the Higgs tower, both on the conjugate tower, or one on
each.  In each case the isospin contraction is a Lorentz scalar carrying two derivative
slots, so read as a family indexed by those two slots it is a bi-Lorentz tensor, the
Lorentz group moving each slot by the Lorentz matrix of the `SL(2,ℂ)` element.

## B. The metric contraction is fixed by both groups

Two covector indices admit one invariant contraction, the metric trace, and the metric is
carried to itself by a Lorentz matrix — that is the defining property of the Lorentz group,
recorded as `LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul` — so the trace of a bi-Lorentz family is a
Lorentz invariant, `RankTwo.metric_invariant`.  It is a gauge invariant too whenever
the components are, and the components here are isospin contractions, which the gauge group
fixes.

## C. The invariants of mass weight eight

The gauge classification reduces mass weight eight to the three spans of twice-derived
isospin contractions and the line through the square of the underived one.  Each of the
three spans is spanned by a bi-Lorentz tensor and reduces, for the Lorentz group, to the
line through its metric trace (`ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_span_metric`); the
line through the square is fixed and reduces to itself.  What is left is a combination of
the three metric traces and the square: the two box terms, the kinetic term and the quartic
potential.

## D. The span consists of invariants of mass weight eight

The reduction of section E is one-directional, and the converse is easy:
each of the four generators is built from isospin contractions of the right mass weight,
which both groups fix, so the span is made of invariants of mass weight eight already.
The metric trace inherits the mass weight of the components and both invariances from
section B, and the square of the underived contraction is a product of two invariants of
mass weight four.

## E. The classification

The gauge classification and the Lorentz classification compose: the first reduces mass
weight eight to the gauge invariants of section C, the second reduces those to the span,
and neither step needs the intermediate span to be fixed by the other group. Section D
says the span is made of invariants of mass weight eight, which turns the reduction into
an equivalence.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isEquivariant_up_rankTwo_dotGaugeHiggs_left
declarations.doc:
Both derivatives on the Higgs tower, a bi-Lorentz tensor in the two derivative
slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_up_rankTwo_dotGaugeHiggs_left :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 2 => .up) repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs d ![])

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isEquivariant_up_rankTwo_dotGaugeHiggs_right
declarations.doc: Both derivatives on the conjugate tower, a bi-Lorentz tensor in the same way.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_up_rankTwo_dotGaugeHiggs_right :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 2 => .up) repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs ![] d)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isEquivariant_up_rankTwo_dotGaugeHiggs_mixed
declarations.doc:
One derivative on each tower, the family whose metric contraction is the kinetic
term.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_up_rankTwo_dotGaugeHiggs_mixed :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 2 => .up) repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs ![d 0] ![d 1])

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan_two_zero_eq
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin contractions with both derivatives on the Higgs tower is the
span of the components of the corresponding bi-Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotSpan_two_zero_eq :
    dotSpan 2 0
      = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs d ![])

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan_zero_two_eq
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin contractions with both derivatives on the conjugate tower is
the span of the components of the corresponding bi-Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotSpan_zero_two_eq :
    dotSpan 0 2
      = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs ![] d)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan_one_one_eq
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin contractions with one derivative on each tower is the span of
the components of the mixed bi-Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotSpan_one_one_eq :
    dotSpan 1 1
      = Submodule.span ℂ
        (Set.range fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs ![d 0] ![d 1])

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_liftComponents_metric
declarations.doc: The metric trace of a family of gauge invariants is a gauge invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_liftComponents_metric {T : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hTG : ∀ (g : GaugeGroupI) (d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), repGaugeGroupI g (T d) = T d)
    (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (liftComponents T RankTwo.metric) = liftComponents T RankTwo.metric

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of the scalar sector at mass weight eight, the two box
terms `□H† H` and `H† □H`, the kinetic term `∂^μ H† ∂_μ H`, and the quartic potential
`(H† H)²`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzContractionEightSpan :
    Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.invariant_dotGaugeHiggs_sq
declarations.doc:
The square of the underived isospin contraction is fixed by both groups, being a
product of two invariants and both representations are multiplicative.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariant_dotGaugeHiggs_sq :
    (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g (dotGaugeHiggs (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ![]
        * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![])
      = dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![] * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![])
    ∧ ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g (dotGaugeHiggs (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ![]
        * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![])
      = dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![] * dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![]

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.liftComponents_metric_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The metric trace of a family of elements of mass weight eight has mass weight
eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_metric_mem_massWeightSubmodule
    {T : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hT : ∀ d, T d ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8) :
    liftComponents T RankTwo.metric ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The weight-eight span lies in the mass-weight submodule of weight eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule :
    lorentzContractionEightSpan ≤ massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_of_mem_lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc: Every element of the weight-eight span is a gauge invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_of_mem_lorentzContractionEightSpan (g : GaugeGroupI) {y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hy : y ∈ lorentzContractionEightSpan) : repGaugeGroupI g y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_of_mem_lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc: Every element of the weight-eight span is a Lorentz invariant.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isFixedBy_lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc: The weight-eight span is fixed pointwise by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_lorentzContractionEightSpan :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) lorentzContractionEightSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc:
The scalar sector at mass weight eight reduces, for the gauge and Lorentz groups
together, to the two box terms, the kinetic term and the quartic potential. The gauge group
leaves the isospin contractions with two derivatives and the square of the underived one;
the Lorentz group contracts the two derivative slots of each family with the metric, and
the square, which carries no index, is fixed.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionEightSpan :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (massWeightSubmodule 8)
      lorentzContractionEightSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz classification of mass weight eight as an equivalence. An element
of `massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is a combination of
the two box terms, the kinetic term and the quartic potential, up to a remainder in `S`
fixed by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ lorentzContractionEightSpan

modules.title: The Higgs invariants below mass weight eight
modules.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of the scalar sector below mass weight eight, the Higgs mass
term alone.

## i. Overview

The scalar sector is the one sector of the Standard Model already carrying an invariant
below mass weight eight, and it is the most familiar of all: the mass term `H† H`, of mass
weight four.  Everything else below weight eight dies, and for three different reasons.

The odd weights are trivial submodules, every Higgs tower carrying even mass weight.
Weight two dies on hypercharge. A single Higgs symbol carries `6Y = ∓3`, so nothing at that
weight is neutral, which is the gauge classification of
`reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_two`.  Weight six dies on Lorentz counting.  Its
gauge invariants are the isospin contractions with one derivative, `∂_μ H† H` and
`H† ∂_μ H`, and a single covector index admits no invariant contraction at all — the metric
ties two indices and the Levi-Civita symbol four — which is
`complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_eq_bot_of_odd` at one index.

Weight four survives because the Higgs is a Lorentz scalar.  Its gauge invariants are the
multiples of `H† H`, and with no derivative slot there is no Lorentz index to contract, so
the Lorentz group fixes the contraction outright and the whole line survives.  That is why
the conclusion here is membership in a span rather than in `S`, unlike the gauge and Yukawa
sectors. The surviving span is the Higgs mass term at weight four and trivial at every
other weight below eight.

As in the gauge sector the final statement needs `0 < w` as well as `w < 8`. At `w = 0` the
mass-weight submodule contains the scalars, so `1` is an invariant of weight zero lying in
no `S`.

## ii. Key results

- `isEquivariant_up_rankOne_dotGaugeHiggs_left` and its `_right` companion : the isospin
  contractions with one derivative are Lorentz vectors.
- `lorentzContractionLTEightSpan` : the surviving span below mass weight eight, the line through
  the Higgs mass term at weight four.
- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the classification
  below mass weight eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The isospin contractions with one derivative as Lorentz vectors
- B. The underived isospin contraction as a Lorentz scalar
- C. Mass weight six
- D. The classification below mass weight eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The isospin contractions with one derivative as Lorentz vectors

At mass weight six the gauge classification leaves the isospin contractions carrying one
derivative, on either of the two towers.  The Higgs is a Lorentz scalar, so the only
Lorentz index such a contraction has is that derivative slot, and read as a family indexed
by it the contraction is a Lorentz vector.  `invariants_up_pow_eq_bot_of_odd` says that one index
admits no invariant contraction, so the span of such a family reduces to `⊥`
(`ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_odd`); the spans are themselves stable, so
`ReducesInvariantsTo.sup` joins the two.

## B. The underived isospin contraction as a Lorentz scalar

At mass weight four the gauge classification leaves the multiples of `H† H`.  An underived
Higgs symbol carries no derivative slot, so the Lorentz group moves it by an empty product
of Lorentz matrix entries, that is not at all, and the contraction and the whole line
through it are fixed.  Nothing peels off here; the line is the answer.

## C. Mass weight six

The gauge classification leaves, at mass weight six, the two spans of once-derived isospin
contractions (`reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule_six`). Section A reduces each to `⊥`
for the Lorentz group, since a single covector index carries no invariant contraction, and
`ReducesInvariantsTo.sup` joins them: nothing is left behind.

## D. The classification below mass weight eight

The seven weights between zero and eight are now settled: weights one, three, five and
seven are trivial submodules, weight two is killed by hypercharge, weight six by section C,
and weight four leaves the line through the mass term.  `lorentzContractionLTEightSpan`
records that answer as a single submodule depending on the weight, and
`reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionLTEightSpan` reduces each weight to it, so the
statement has the shape of the weight-eight one and of the other sectors' below-eight ones,
whose spans happen to be trivial.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isEquivariant_up_rankOne_dotGaugeHiggs_left
declarations.doc:
The isospin contraction of a once-derived Higgs tower against an underived conjugate
tower, read as a family indexed by its derivative slot, is a Lorentz vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_up_rankOne_dotGaugeHiggs_left :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 1 => .up) repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents fun d : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs d ![])

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isEquivariant_up_rankOne_dotGaugeHiggs_right
declarations.doc:
The isospin contraction of an underived Higgs tower against a once-derived conjugate
tower is a Lorentz vector in the same way.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_up_rankOne_dotGaugeHiggs_right :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 1 => .up) repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents fun d : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs ![] d)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan_one_zero_eq
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin contractions with one derivative on the Higgs tower is the
span of the components of the corresponding Lorentz vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotSpan_one_zero_eq :
    dotSpan 1 0
      = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun d : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs d ![])

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan_zero_one_eq
declarations.doc:
The span of the isospin contractions with one derivative on the conjugate tower is the
span of the components of the corresponding Lorentz vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotSpan_zero_one_eq :
    dotSpan 0 1
      = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun d : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => dotGaugeHiggs ![] d)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_dotGaugeHiggs_zero
declarations.doc: The underived isospin contraction is a Lorentz scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_dotGaugeHiggs_zero (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    repLorentzGroup g (dotGaugeHiggs (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ![])
      = dotGaugeHiggs ![] ![]

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan_zero_zero_eq
declarations.doc: The span of the underived isospin contractions is the line through the mass term.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotSpan_zero_zero_eq :
    dotSpan 0 0 = ℂ ∙ dotGaugeHiggs (![] : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ![]

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_of_mem_dotSpan_zero_zero
declarations.doc:
Every element of the line through the underived isospin contraction is a Lorentz
invariant.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_of_mem_dotSpan
declarations.doc: Every element of a span of isospin contractions is a gauge invariant.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.dotSpan_zero_zero_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The line through the underived isospin contraction lies in mass weight four.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotSpan_zero_zero_le_massWeightSubmodule :
    dotSpan 0 0 ≤ massWeightSubmodule 4

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_dotSpan_one_zero_sup_zero_one
declarations.doc:
The once-derived isospin contractions reduce to `⊥` for the Lorentz group. Each span is
spanned by a Lorentz vector, and a single covector index carries no invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_dotSpan_one_zero_sup_zero_one :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentzGroup g) (dotSpan 1 0 ⊔ dotSpan 0 1) ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.lorentzContractionLTEightSpan
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of the scalar sector at mass weight `w` for
`0 < w < 8`, the line through the Higgs mass term at weight four, and nothing at any
other weight.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzContractionLTEightSpan
    (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.lorentzContractionLTEightSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The surviving span at weight `w` lies in the mass-weight submodule of weight `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzContractionLTEightSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule (w : ℕ) :
    lorentzContractionLTEightSpan w ≤ massWeightSubmodule w

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.rep_of_mem_lorentzContractionLTEightSpan
declarations.doc: Every element of the surviving span is a gauge invariant.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.repLorentz_of_mem_lorentzContractionLTEightSpan
declarations.doc: Every element of the surviving span is a Lorentz invariant.

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.isFixedBy_lorentzContractionLTEightSpan
declarations.doc: The surviving span below weight eight is fixed pointwise by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_lorentzContractionLTEightSpan (w : ℕ) :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (lorentzContractionLTEightSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionLTEightSpan
declarations.doc:
Below mass weight eight the scalar sector reduces, for the gauge and Lorentz groups
together, to the surviving span. The four odd weights are trivial submodules, weight two
dies on hypercharge, weight four leaves the Higgs mass term, which the Lorentz group fixes,
and at weight six the gauge group leaves the once-derived contractions and the Lorentz
group nothing.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionLTEightSpan {w : ℕ} (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGaugeGroupI repLorentzGroup) (massWeightSubmodule w)
      (lorentzContractionLTEightSpan w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of
`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`. An element of
`massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is an
element of the surviving span up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups.  That span
is the line through the Higgs mass term at weight four and trivial elsewhere, so at every
weight but four this says `x = y`, as in the gauge and Yukawa sectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ lorentzContractionLTEightSpan w

declarations.name: StandardModel.ScalarSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. Below mass weight eight an element of
`massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of the surviving span
joined with `S` fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ lorentzContractionLTEightSpan w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)

modules.title: The Yukawa sector's mass-weight submodules
modules.doc:
The Yukawa sector of the covariant field algebra of the Standard Model, as a join of products.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

The mixed Higgs-fermion sector — the `{scalar, fermion}` two-class sector of
`Sectors.lean` — is the home of the Yukawa couplings. Since the Higgs sector is
bosonic, its algebra commutes with the fermion algebra
(`commute_of_mem_higgsAlgebra_of_mem_fermionAlgebra`), which feeds the abstract
two-class machinery `sectorMassWeight_pair_le` to bound each weight-`w` piece of the
sector by a join of products of the two sectors' own mass-weight submodules
(`sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_le`). Combined with the explicit low-weight tables
for the Higgs sector (vanishing at odd weight) and the fermion sector (vanishing at
weight `1`, `2` and `4`), this pins the sector down explicitly up to weight eight: it
vanishes below weight five and at weight six, and at weights five, seven and eight it
sits inside the expected Yukawa-type products, the last of these being the weight of
the Yukawa term `H ψ ψ` itself.

## ii. Key results

- `commute_of_mem_higgsAlgebra_of_mem_fermionAlgebra` : the algebra generated by the Higgs towers
  commutes with the algebra generated by the fermion towers.
- `sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_le` : the Yukawa sector at weight `w` lies in the join, over the
  splittings of `w` into two non-zero parts, of the products of the Higgs-sector and
  fermion-sector mass-weight submodules.
- `sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_five`, `sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_seven`,
  `sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight` : the Yukawa sector at weights five, seven and eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Cross-algebra commutation
- B. The Yukawa sector at a fixed mass weight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Cross-algebra commutation

The Higgs sector is bosonic, so its algebra commutes with the fermion algebra
elementwise. This is the algebraic input to the whole Yukawa-sector decomposition.
## B. The Yukawa sector at a fixed mass weight

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.commute_of_mem_higgsAlgebra_of_mem_fermionAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The Higgs sector is bosonic. Every element of the algebra generated by the
Higgs towers commutes with every element of the algebra generated by the fermion
towers.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.fermionMassWeight_mul_higgsMassWeight_le
declarations.doc:
The fermion-sector and Higgs-sector mass-weight submodules commute past each
other, in the order needed by `sectorMassWeight_pair_le`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMassWeight_mul_higgsMassWeight_le (a b : ℕ) :
    FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule a * ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule b
      ≤ ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule b * FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule a

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_le
declarations.doc:
The Yukawa-sector decomposition. The weight-`w` piece of the `{scalar,
fermion}` sector is contained in the join, over the splittings of `w` into two
non-zero parts, of the products of the Higgs-sector and fermion-sector mass-weight
submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_le (w : ℕ) :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w
      ≤ ⨆ (p : ℕ × ℕ) (_ : p.1 + p.2 = w) (_ : p.1 ≠ 0) (_ : p.2 ≠ 0),
        ScalarSector.massWeightSubmodule p.1 * FermionSector.massWeightSubmodule p.2

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_five
declarations.doc:
Below weight five, the Yukawa sector vanishes. No splitting of a total weight
under five into two non-zero parts survives, since the Higgs part is either odd (hence
zero) or equal to two, forcing the fermion part to be one or two (hence also
zero).
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_five {w : ℕ} (hw : w < 5) :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w = ⊥
