declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_six
declarations.doc:
The Yukawa sector vanishes at weight six, since every splitting of six into two
non-zero parts has either an odd Higgs part or a fermion part of weight two or
four, all of which vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_six :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 6 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_le_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion
declarations.doc:
A product of a Higgs-weight piece and a fermion-weight piece lands in the Yukawa
sector of the total weight.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_five
declarations.doc:
The weight-five Yukawa sector. The only surviving splitting is the Higgs
field itself (weight two) against the underived fermion towers (weight three).
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_five :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 5
      = ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0 * FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_seven
declarations.doc:
The weight-seven Yukawa sector. The surviving splittings pair the Higgs
field (weight two) with the once-derived fermion towers (weight five), or the
once-derived Higgs field (weight four) with the underived fermion towers (weight
three).
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_seven :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 7
      = ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0 * FermionSector.derivSubmodule 1
        ⊔ ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 1 * FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0
        ⊔ ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0 * ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0
          * FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight
declarations.doc:
The weight-eight Yukawa sector. The only surviving splitting pairs the Higgs
field (weight two) with the product of two underived fermion towers (weight six), the
sector of the Yukawa term `H ψ ψ` itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight :
    fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 8
      = ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0
        * (FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0 * FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0)

modules.title: The Yukawa terms built on the conjugate Higgs symbol
modules.doc:
The conjugate-Higgs-type Yukawa terms of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

The remaining three couplings of the mass-weight-eight Yukawa sector are built on the
conjugate Higgs symbol, `barH bard Q`, `barH u barQ` and `barH L bare`.  Each is the
conjugate of one of the three couplings of `Families/Higgs.lean`, and is the same computation
with every symbol replaced by its conjugate. Fundamental and anti-fundamental indices
exchange, left- and right-handed spinors exchange, and every hypercharge changes sign.  So
the isospin structure of the conjugate up type is `2 ⊗ 2` where its partner had `2̄ ⊗ 2̄`,
and its invariant is again the antisymmetric symbol.

With these six couplings the twelve blocks are accounted for. The other six are the same
six with the two fermion factors exchanged, and by `mul_mul_swap_eq_neg` their terms are
minus these while by `mul_mul_piece_swap` their blocks are the same submodules.

## ii. Key results

- `barDownYukawa`, `barUpYukawa`, `barLeptonYukawa` : the three conjugate Yukawa terms.
- `isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_barDownBlock`, `isEquivariant_isospinFundFund_barUpBlock` and
  the rest : the index laws of the three conjugate blocks.
- `yukawaSpan` : the join of all six couplings over all nine family pairs.
- `yukawaSpan_le_inf` : the Yukawa span lies inside the gauge- and Lorentz-invariants of
  the sector at mass weight eight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The conjugate down-type Yukawa term
- B. The invariance of the conjugate down-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight
- C. The conjugate up-type Yukawa term
- D. The invariance of the conjugate up-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight
- E. The conjugate charged-lepton Yukawa term
- F. The invariance of the conjugate charged-lepton Yukawa term, and its mass weight
- G. The Yukawa span

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The conjugate down-type Yukawa term

The conjugate of the down type: the product `barH bard Q`.  Colour is `3 ⊗ 3̄` with the
conjugate down singlet supplying the fundamental index, isospin is `2 ⊗ 2̄` with the
conjugate Higgs symbol supplying the fundamental index and the quark doublet the
anti-fundamental one, and both fermions are left-handed.
## B. The invariance of the conjugate down-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight

## C. The conjugate up-type Yukawa term

The conjugate of the up type: the product `barH u barQ`.  Colour is `3 ⊗ 3̄` with the
conjugate quark doublet supplying the fundamental index, isospin is `2 ⊗ 2` — the conjugate
Higgs symbol and the conjugate quark doublet both carry the fundamental, so the invariant
is again the antisymmetric symbol — and both fermions are right-handed.
## D. The invariance of the conjugate up-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight

## E. The conjugate charged-lepton Yukawa term

The conjugate of the charged-lepton type: the product `barH L bare`.  As with its
unconjugated partner there is no colour at all, so the colour step is plain invariance;
isospin is `2 ⊗ 2̄` with the conjugate Higgs symbol supplying the fundamental index, and
both fermions are left-handed.
## F. The invariance of the conjugate charged-lepton Yukawa term, and its mass weight

## G. The Yukawa span

The six couplings, each joined over the nine family pairs, are the whole Yukawa content of
the sector at mass weight eight: six arbitrary `3 × 3` coupling matrices, and no matrix
written down anywhere.  The join lies inside the sector and inside both spaces of
invariants, which is the direction that makes the eventual classification an equivalence
rather than a one-way inclusion.  The six transposed blocks add nothing: by
`mul_mul_swap_eq_neg` their terms are minus these.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock
declarations.doc:
The components of the conjugate down-type Yukawa block `barH bard Q`, a conjugate
Higgs symbol, a conjugate down-singlet symbol and a quark-doublet symbol, none carrying
derivatives.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def barDownBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i sbd : Fin 2) (cbd : Fin 3) (sQ : Fin 2)
    (cQ : Fin 3) (wQ : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_barDownBlock
declarations.doc:
The two colour indices of the conjugate down-type block carry one fundamental and one
anti-fundamental `su(3)` index, the conjugate down singlet supplying the fundamental
one.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_barDownBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i sbd sQ wQ : Fin 2) :
    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 3 =>
        LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock f f' i sbd (l 0) sQ (l 1) wQ) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_barDownBlock
declarations.doc:
The two isospin indices of the conjugate down-type block carry one fundamental and one
anti-fundamental `su(2)` index, the conjugate Higgs symbol supplying the fundamental
one.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_barDownBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (sbd : Fin 2) (cbd : Fin 3)
    (sQ : Fin 2) (cQ : Fin 3) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 =>
        LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock f f' (l 0) sbd cbd sQ cQ (l 1)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_downLDownL_barDownBlock
declarations.doc: The two spinor indices of the conjugate down-type block are both dual left-handed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downLDownL_barDownBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i : Fin 2) (cbd cQ : Fin 3)
    (wQ : Fin 2) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downL] repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents ((fun p => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock f f' i p.1 cbd p.2 cQ wQ) ∘
          pairIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_u1_barDownBlock
declarations.doc:
A hypercharge transformation fixes every component of the conjugate down-type block,
the three hypercharges `3`, `-2` and `-1` cancelling.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_u1_barDownBlock (t : unitary ℂ) (f f' : Fin 3) (i sbd : Fin 2)
    (cbd : Fin 3) (sQ : Fin 2) (cQ : Fin 3) (wQ : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI) (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock f f' i
      sbd cbd sQ cQ wQ)
      = LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock f f' i sbd cbd sQ cQ wQ

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockColour
declarations.doc: The colour contraction of the conjugate down-type block.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def barDownBlockColour (f f' : Fin 3)
    (i sbd sQ wQ : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockColour_eq
declarations.doc: The colour contraction of the conjugate down-type block written out.
declarations.statement:
lemma barDownBlockColour_eq (f f' : Fin 3) (i sbd sQ wQ : Fin 2) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockColour f f' i sbd sQ wQ
      = ∑ a : Fin 3, LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock f f' i sbd a sQ a wQ

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_barDownBlockColour
declarations.doc:
The colour contraction of the conjugate down-type block still carries one fundamental
and one anti-fundamental isospin index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_barDownBlockColour (f f' : Fin 3) (sbd sQ : Fin 2) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 =>
        LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockColour f f' (l 0) sbd sQ (l 1)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockIsospin
declarations.doc: The isospin contraction of the colour-contracted conjugate down-type block.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def barDownBlockIsospin (f f' : Fin 3)
    (sbd sQ : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockIsospin_eq
declarations.doc: The doubly contracted conjugate down-type block written out.
declarations.statement:
lemma barDownBlockIsospin_eq (f f' : Fin 3) (sbd sQ : Fin 2) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockIsospin f f' sbd sQ
      = ∑ p : Fin 2 × Fin 3, LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlock f f' p.1 sbd p.2 sQ p.2 p.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_downLDownL_barDownBlockIsospin
declarations.doc:
The doubly contracted conjugate down-type block carries two dual left-handed Weyl
indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downLDownL_barDownBlockIsospin (f f' : Fin 3) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downL] repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents ((fun p => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownBlockIsospin f f' p.1 p.2) ∘
          pairIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.barDownYukawa
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_barUpBlock

The Yukawa span lies inside the gauge- and Lorentz-invariants of the Yukawa sector at
mass weight eight. This is the easy direction of the classification. Every Yukawa term
is an invariant of the right mass weight, so the eventual classification is an
equivalence and not merely a one-way inclusion.

modules.title: The Yukawa terms built on the Higgs symbol
modules.doc:
The Higgs-type Yukawa terms of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

Three of the twelve blocks of the mass-weight-eight Yukawa sector are built on the Higgs
symbol rather than its conjugate, the down type `H d barQ`, the up type `H baru Q` and the
charged-lepton type `H barL e`.  They are the three genuinely distinct computations of the
sector — the other nine blocks are their conjugates and the two fermion orderings of each —
and this file builds, for each of them, the block, the index laws its three symbols obey,
the iterated contraction those laws admit, and the proof that the contraction is a gauge-
and Lorentz-invariant element of the sector at mass weight eight.

The three differ in exactly two places. In isospin, the down and lepton types contract a
`2 ⊗ 2̄` by the trace, the up type a `2̄ ⊗ 2̄` by the antisymmetric symbol, since the Higgs
symbol and the quark doublet both carry the anti-fundamental. In colour, the two quark types
contract a `3 ⊗ 3̄` by the Kronecker delta, while the lepton type carries no colour at all,
so its colour step is plain invariance rather than a classification and its contraction has
two stages instead of three.

The transposed blocks — the same three triples with the two fermion factors exchanged — are
not built here. They are minus these terms and span the same submodules, by
`mul_mul_swap_eq_neg` and `mul_mul_piece_swap`.

## ii. Key results

- `downYukawa`, `upYukawa`, `leptonYukawa` : the three Yukawa terms of a family pair.
- `isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_downBlock`, `isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_downBlock`,
  `isEquivariant_downRDownR_downBlock` and their up-type and lepton-type counterparts : the index
  laws of each block.
- `repGauge_downYukawa`, `repLorentz_downYukawa` and their counterparts : the invariance of
  each Yukawa term.
- `downYukawaSpan`, `upYukawaSpan`, `leptonYukawaSpan` : the join over the nine family
  pairs, which is the coupling with an arbitrary `3 × 3` matrix.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The down-type Yukawa term
- B. The invariance of the down-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight
- C. The up-type Yukawa term
- D. The invariance of the up-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight
- E. The charged-lepton Yukawa term
- F. The invariance of the charged-lepton Yukawa term, and its mass weight
- G. The spans of the Yukawa terms

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The down-type Yukawa term

The first block, and the pattern for the other eleven.  The block is the product
`H d barQ`; the conjugate quark doublet supplies the fundamental colour index and the
fundamental isospin index, so it goes in the first slot of both mixed families, while the
down singlet supplies the anti-fundamental colour index and the Higgs symbol the
anti-fundamental isospin one.  Both fermions are right-handed.  The three contractions are
then formed in turn, each one a spectator of the next.

## B. The invariance of the down-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight

Each contraction is invariant under the factor it contracts, and inert under the other two,
so the composite is fixed by all three factors and hence gauge invariant.  Hypercharge is
already invariant component by component, the three charges `-3`, `2` and `1` summing to
zero.

## C. The up-type Yukawa term

The second computation.  Colour is again `3 ⊗ 3̄`, the conjugate up singlet supplying the
fundamental index, but isospin is `2̄ ⊗ 2̄`: the Higgs symbol and the quark doublet both
carry the anti-fundamental, whose only invariant is the antisymmetric symbol.  Both
fermions are left-handed.
## D. The invariance of the up-type Yukawa term, and its mass weight

## E. The charged-lepton Yukawa term

The lepton blocks carry no colour at all, so there is no colour family to classify and no
colour contraction to form: the three symbols are separately fixed by the colour factor,
which is `repGauge_su3_leptonBlock`.  The isospin and Lorentz steps are the same two steps
as for the quark blocks, and the contraction is the composite of those two alone.
## F. The invariance of the charged-lepton Yukawa term, and its mass weight

## G. The spans of the Yukawa terms

The nine family pairs are what the Yukawa coupling matrices are: joining the line of a
Yukawa term over `(f, f') : Fin 3 × Fin 3` gives exactly the space of terms with an
arbitrary `3 × 3` complex coupling matrix, and no matrix has to be written down.  Each such
join lies inside the sector at mass weight eight and inside both spaces of invariants,
which is the direction that will make the eventual classification an equivalence rather
than a one-way inclusion.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock
declarations.doc:
The components of the down-type Yukawa block `H d barQ`, a Higgs symbol, a
down-singlet symbol and a conjugate quark-doublet symbol, none carrying derivatives,
multiplied in the order in which the block of
`sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero` multiplies them.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def downBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i sd : Fin 2) (cd : Fin 3) (sq : Fin 2)
    (cq : Fin 3) (wq : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_downBlock
declarations.doc:
The two colour indices of the down-type block carry one fundamental and one
anti-fundamental `su(3)` index. The conjugate quark doublet supplies the fundamental
index, so it goes in the first slot, and the down singlet the anti-fundamental one.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_downBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i sd sq wq : Fin 2) :
    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 3 => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' i sd (l 1) sq
          (l 0) wq) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_downBlock
declarations.doc:
The two isospin indices of the down-type block carry one fundamental and one
anti-fundamental `su(2)` index. The conjugate quark doublet supplies the fundamental
index and the Higgs symbol the anti-fundamental one, so the Higgs index goes in the
second slot.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_downBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (sd : Fin 2) (cd : Fin 3)
    (sq : Fin 2) (cq : Fin 3) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 =>
        LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' (l 1) sd cd sq cq (l 0)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_downRDownR_downBlock
declarations.doc:
The two spinor indices of the down-type block are both dual right-handed. The down
singlet and the conjugate quark doublet are both right-handed, and the Higgs symbol
without derivatives is a Lorentz scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downRDownR_downBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i : Fin 2) (cd cq : Fin 3) (wq : Fin 2) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downR, .downR] repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents ((fun p => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' i p.1 cd p.2 cq wq) ∘
          pairIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_u1_downBlock
declarations.doc:
A hypercharge transformation fixes every component of the down-type block, the three
hypercharges `-3`, `2` and `1` cancelling.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_u1_downBlock (t : unitary ℂ) (f f' : Fin 3) (i sd : Fin 2) (cd : Fin 3)
    (sq : Fin 2) (cq : Fin 3) (wq : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI) (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' i sd
      cd sq cq wq)
      = LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' i sd cd sq cq wq

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockColour
declarations.doc:
The colour contraction of the down-type block, the Kronecker delta joining the
fundamental colour index of the conjugate quark doublet to the anti-fundamental one of
the down singlet.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def downBlockColour (f f' : Fin 3)
    (i sd sq wq : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockColour_eq
declarations.doc:
The colour contraction written out, the sum of the three components with equal colour
indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma downBlockColour_eq (f f' : Fin 3) (i sd sq wq : Fin 2) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockColour f f' i sd sq wq
      = ∑ a : Fin 3, LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' i sd a sq a wq

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_downBlockColour
declarations.doc:
The colour contraction of the down-type block still carries one fundamental and one
anti-fundamental isospin index, the colour sum being an isospin spectator.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinFundAntiFund_downBlockColour (f f' : Fin 3) (sd sq : Fin 2) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 =>
        LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockColour f f' (l 1) sd sq (l 0)) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin
declarations.doc:
The isospin contraction of the colour-contracted down-type block, the Kronecker delta
joining the fundamental isospin index of the conjugate quark doublet to the
anti-fundamental one of the Higgs.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def downBlockIsospin (f f' : Fin 3)
    (sd sq : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin_eq
declarations.doc:
The doubly contracted block written out as a single sum over the isospin and colour
indices it identifies.
declarations.statement:
lemma downBlockIsospin_eq (f f' : Fin 3) (sd sq : Fin 2) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f f' sd sq
      = ∑ p : Fin 2 × Fin 3, LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' p.1 sd p.2 sq p.2 p.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_downRDownR_downBlockIsospin
declarations.doc:
The doubly contracted block carries two dual right-handed Weyl indices, the colour and
isospin sums being Lorentz spectators.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downRDownR_downBlockIsospin (f f' : Fin 3) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downR, .downR] repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents ((fun p => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f f' p.1 p.2) ∘
        pairIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downYukawa
declarations.doc:
The down-type Yukawa term of the family pair `(f, f')`, the down-singlet symbol of family `f`
against the conjugate quark doublet of family `f'` and a Higgs symbol, with the colour indices
joined by the Kronecker delta, the isospin indices by the Kronecker delta, and the two
right-handed spinor indices by the antisymmetric symbol. It is the image of the metric `εR'` under
the map with the contracted block as its components.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def downYukawa (f f' : Fin 3) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_su3_downBlockColour
declarations.doc: The colour contraction of the down-type block is fixed by the colour factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_downBlockColour (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (f f' : Fin 3)
    (i sd sq wq : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockColour f
      f' i sd sq wq)
      = LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockColour f f' i sd sq wq

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_su3_downBlockIsospin
declarations.doc: The doubly contracted down-type block is fixed by the colour factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_downBlockIsospin (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (f f' : Fin 3)
    (sd sq : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f
      f' sd sq)
      = LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f f' sd sq

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_su2_downBlockIsospin
declarations.doc: The doubly contracted down-type block is fixed by the isospin factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su2_downBlockIsospin (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (f f' : Fin 3)
    (sd sq : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f
      f' sd sq)
      = LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f f' sd sq

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_u1_downBlockIsospin
declarations.doc:
The doubly contracted down-type block is fixed by the hypercharge factor, already
component by component.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_u1_downBlockIsospin (t : unitary ℂ) (f f' : Fin 3) (sd sq : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI) (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f
      f' sd sq)
      = LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlockIsospin f f' sd sq

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_downYukawa
declarations.doc:
The down-type Yukawa term is gauge invariant. The colour indices are joined by the
Kronecker delta, the isospin indices by the Kronecker delta, and the three hypercharges
cancel.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_downYukawa (f f' : Fin 3) (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downYukawa f f') =
      LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downYukawa f f'

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentz_downYukawa
declarations.doc:
The down-type Yukawa term is Lorentz invariant, the two right-handed spinor indices
being joined by the antisymmetric symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_downYukawa (f f' : Fin 3) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    repLorentzGroup Λ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downYukawa f f') =
      LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downYukawa f f'

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock_mem_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
Every component of the down-type block sits at mass weight eight in the Yukawa
sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma downBlock_mem_sectorMassWeight (f f' : Fin 3) (i sd : Fin 2) (cd : Fin 3)
    (sq : Fin 2) (cq : Fin 3) (wq : Fin 2) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downBlock f f' i sd cd sq cq wq
      ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downYukawa_mem_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc: The down-type Yukawa term sits at mass weight eight in the Yukawa sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma downYukawa_mem_sectorMassWeight (f f' : Fin 3) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.downYukawa f f' ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight
      {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock
declarations.doc:
The components of the up-type Yukawa block `H baru Q`, a Higgs symbol, a conjugate
up-singlet symbol and a quark-doublet symbol, none carrying derivatives.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def upBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i su : Fin 2) (cu : Fin 3) (sQ : Fin 2)
    (cQ : Fin 3) (wQ : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_upBlock
declarations.doc:
The two colour indices of the up-type block carry one fundamental and one
anti-fundamental `su(3)` index, the conjugate up singlet supplying the fundamental
one.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_colourFundAntiFund_upBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i su sQ wQ : Fin 2) :
    (suTensor 3).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU3)
      (liftComponents ((fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 3 =>
        LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f f' i su (l 0) sQ (l 1) wQ) ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_isospinAntiFundAntiFund_upBlock
declarations.doc:
The two isospin indices of the up-type block are both anti-fundamental. The Higgs
symbol and the quark doublet both carry the anti-fundamental of `su(2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinAntiFundAntiFund_upBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (su : Fin 2) (cu : Fin 3)
    (sQ : Fin 2)
    (cQ : Fin 3) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 2 => .antiFund) (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents (fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f f' (l 0) su cu sQ cQ
          (l 1)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_downLDownL_upBlock
declarations.doc: The two spinor indices of the up-type block are both dual left-handed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downLDownL_upBlock (f f' : Fin 3) (i : Fin 2) (cu cQ : Fin 3) (wQ : Fin 2) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downL] repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents ((fun p => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f f' i p.1 cu p.2 cQ wQ) ∘
        pairIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_u1_upBlock
declarations.doc:
A hypercharge transformation fixes every component of the up-type block, the three
hypercharges `-3`, `4` and `-1` cancelling.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_u1_upBlock (t : unitary ℂ) (f f' : Fin 3) (i su : Fin 2) (cu : Fin 3)
    (sQ : Fin 2) (cQ : Fin 3) (wQ : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI) (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f f' i su
      cu sQ cQ wQ)
      = LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f f' i su cu sQ cQ wQ

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockColour
declarations.doc: The colour contraction of the up-type block.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def upBlockColour (f f' : Fin 3)
    (i su sQ wQ : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockColour_eq
declarations.doc: The colour contraction of the up-type block written out.
declarations.statement:
lemma upBlockColour_eq (f f' : Fin 3) (i su sQ wQ : Fin 2) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockColour f f' i su sQ wQ = ∑ a : Fin 3, LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f
      f' i su a sQ a wQ

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_isospinAntiFundAntiFund_upBlockColour
declarations.doc:
The colour contraction of the up-type block still carries two anti-fundamental isospin
indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_isospinAntiFundAntiFund_upBlockColour (f f' : Fin 3) (su sQ : Fin 2) :
    (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 2 => .antiFund) (repGaugeGroupI.comp GaugeGroupI.ofSU2)
      (liftComponents (fun l : Fin 2 → Fin 2 => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockColour f f' (l 0) su sQ
          (l 1)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockIsospin
declarations.doc:
The isospin contraction of the colour-contracted up-type block, by the antisymmetric
symbol. Two anti-fundamental isospin indices admit no trace.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def upBlockIsospin (f f' : Fin 3) (su sQ : Fin 2) : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockIsospin_eq
declarations.doc: The doubly contracted up-type block written out.
declarations.statement:
lemma upBlockIsospin_eq (f f' : Fin 3) (su sQ : Fin 2) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockIsospin f f' su sQ = (∑ a : Fin 3, LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f f'
      0 su a sQ a 1)
      - ∑ a : Fin 3, LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlock f f' 1 su a sQ a 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isEquivariant_downLDownL_upBlockIsospin
declarations.doc: The doubly contracted up-type block carries two dual left-handed Weyl indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downLDownL_upBlockIsospin (f f' : Fin 3) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downL] repLorentzGroup
      (liftComponents ((fun p => LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upBlockIsospin f f' p.1 p.2) ∘ pairIdx))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.upYukawa
declarations.doc:

Kronecker delta, the isospin indices by the antisymmetric symbol, and the two left-handed spinor

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_upYukawa
declarations.doc: The up-type Yukawa term is gauge invariant.

modules.title: The symbols of the Yukawa blocks
modules.doc:
The symbols of the Yukawa blocks of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

At mass weight eight a Yukawa block is a product of three underived symbols, one Higgs and
two fermions, and every statement about such a block reduces to statements about its three
factors. This file is that reduction. It reads the Higgs symbols at each factor of a gauge
transformation (the fermion symbols are read in `FermionSector/Components.lean`), does the
algebra of a triple product with one inert factor once for each position the inert factor can
occupy, and records the closure of the index laws under the sums and differences a contraction
performs.

Two things here are easy to get wrong and are settled once. A gauge transformation is a
triple and the three index laws each constrain one factor of it. Colour, isospin and
Lorentz between them say nothing about hypercharge, so hypercharge is a fourth step and not
a corollary of the other three, and `forall_repGauge_eq_self`, in `GaugeGroup/Basic.lean`,
is what assembles the four into gauge invariance. And the twelve blocks come in two fermion
orderings, but the fermion
symbols anticommute, so the two orderings of a block span the same submodule and have the
same weight pieces, and `mul_mul_piece_swap` is what makes the six transposed blocks a rewrite
rather than six fresh derivations.

## ii. Key results

- `repGauge_mul_fixed_left`, `repGauge_mul_fixed_mid`, `repGauge_mul_fixed_right`,
  `repLorentz_mul_fixed_left` : the transformation of a triple product with one inert
  factor.
- `repGauge_su3_higgs`, `repGauge_su2_higgs`, `repGauge_u1_higgs` and their conjugates : the three
  gauge laws of the Higgs symbols.
- `mul_mul_piece_swap` : the two fermion orderings of a block have the same weight pieces.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Triple products with one inert factor
- B. The transformation laws of the Higgs symbols
- C. The symbols inside the derivative submodules
- D. The two fermion orderings

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Triple products with one inert factor

Every block is a product of three symbols, and every classifier moves exactly two of them.
The third is inert, being a colour singlet, an isospin singlet or a Lorentz scalar. The
three lemmas here do the algebra once for each position the inert factor can occupy, and
reduce a transformation law for a block to the laws of its factors.

## B. The transformation laws of the Higgs symbols

Each Higgs symbol is read at the three factors of a gauge transformation in turn, and at the
Lorentz group. Colour fixes it, isospin moves its isospin index, and hypercharge is an overall
scalar, the power of which is the `6Y = ∓3` of the Higgs and its conjugate. The same laws for
the ten fermion species are `FermionSector.repGauge_su3_d` and its companions, next to the
components in `FermionSector/Components.lean`.

## C. The symbols inside the derivative submodules

A block is a product of three underived symbols, and by
`sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight` the sector at mass weight eight is the product of
the Higgs derivative submodule with two copies of the fermion one.  So a block sits at mass
weight eight as soon as each of its three symbols is seen inside the matching derivative
submodule.  The ten ranges are recorded as inclusions rather than as memberships, since
section F needs the inclusion and the membership of a component follows from it.

## D. The two fermion orderings

The twelve blocks of the mass-weight-eight decomposition are six choices of a Higgs symbol
and a fermion pair, each occurring in both fermion orderings.  The two orderings are not
the same element — the fermion symbols anticommute, so one is minus the other — but they
span the same submodule, and therefore have the same weight pieces.  So a classification of
one ordering is a classification of the other, and the six transposed blocks need no
argument of their own.

coefficients moves by the product of those coefficients.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_su3_higgs
declarations.doc: A colour transformation fixes a Higgs symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_higgs (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((U, 1, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (ScalarSector.higgs l i)
      = ScalarSector.higgs l i

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_su2_higgs
declarations.doc:
An isospin transformation moves the isospin index of a Higgs symbol by the conjugate
matrix, the index being anti-fundamental.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su2_higgs (V : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, V, 1) : GaugeGroupI) (ScalarSector.higgs l i)
      = ∑ a, conj (V.1 a i) • ScalarSector.higgs l a

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGauge_u1_higgs
declarations.doc:
A hypercharge transformation scales a Higgs symbol by the cube of the conjugate
scalar, the Higgs carrying `6Y = -3`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_u1_higgs (t : unitary ℂ) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI ((1, 1, t) : GaugeGroupI) (ScalarSector.higgs l i)
      = (star (t : ℂ)) ^ 3 • ScalarSector.higgs l i

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_mul_piece_swap
declarations.doc:
Swapping the two fermion factors of a block leaves every weight piece unchanged. The
two fermion factors commute as submodules, so the two orderings of the block are the same
submodule. This is what makes the six transposed blocks of the mass-weight-eight
decomposition a rewrite rather than six fresh classifications.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mul_piece_swap {VH VX VY : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} {n m : ℕ}
    (dH : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VH)
    (dX : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VX)
    (dY : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VY)
    (hX : VX ≤ FermionSector.derivSubmodule n)
    (hY : VY ≤ FermionSector.derivSubmodule m) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dH)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dX) (d' := dY))).piece w
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dH)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dY) (d' := dX))).piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_mul_swap_eq_neg
declarations.doc: Swapping the two fermion factors of a block negates it.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mul_swap_eq_neg {n m : ℕ} (a : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    {x y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ FermionSector.derivSubmodule n)
    (hy : y ∈ FermionSector.derivSubmodule m) :
    a * (y * x) = -(a * (x * y))

modules.title: The gauge weight decomposition of the Yukawa sector at mass weight eight
modules.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the Yukawa sector of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

Mass weight eight is where the Yukawa sector first has anything to say. By
`sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight` the whole sector at that weight is one Higgs
tower against two underived fermion towers, the weight of `H ψ ψ` itself.  Transporting
the gauge weight decompositions of the two sectors along that identification decomposes
the sector, and the question of which Yukawa couplings can exist becomes the question of
which pieces survive at gauge weight zero.

Almost none of them do, and the reason is hypercharge alone.  Writing `6Y` for the
normalisation used throughout, a symbol carries the contragredient of its value space and
so the negative of its charge. The Higgs symbols carry `-3` and their conjugates `+3`,
while the ten fermion species carry
`d = 2`, `bard = -2`, `u = -4`, `baru = 4`, `Q = -1`, `barQ = 1`, `L = 3`, `barL = -3`,
`e = 6`, `bare = -6`.

A block of the decomposition is a choice of one Higgs symbol and two fermion species, and
it can reach gauge weight zero only if the three charges sum to zero.  Against the Higgs
that asks the fermion pair to sum to `+3`, which happens only for `{d, barQ}`,
`{baru, Q}` and `{barL, e}`; against the conjugate Higgs it asks for `-3`, which happens
only for `{bard, Q}`, `{u, barQ}` and `{L, bare}`.  No species pairs with itself, since
`2f = ±3` has no solution.  Each of the six pairs occurs in both orders inside the product
of the two fermion towers, so of the `2 * 10 * 10 = 200` blocks exactly twelve survive and
one hundred and eighty-eight are `⊥`.

That is the whole content of this file. The surviving twelve are the Yukawa couplings
`H d barQ`, `H baru Q`, `H barL e`, `barH bard Q`, `barH u barQ`, `barH L bare` and their
transposes. The colour and isospin structure eliminates nothing further here. It only
decides which components inside a surviving block pair up, which is a later question.

## ii. Key results

- `sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight` : the gauge weight decomposition of the Yukawa sector at mass
  weight eight.
- `mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_neg_three`,
  `mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_pos_three` : the hypercharge sieve against a Higgs and a
  conjugate-Higgs symbol.
- `sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero` : the weight-zero piece, the twelve blocks that
  hypercharge allows.
- `mem_sectorMassWeightEight_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant` : a gauge invariant lies in the
  weight-zero piece modulo a torus-stable submodule.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The sector at mass weight eight, decomposed
- B. Splitting a Higgs-fermion-fermion product along its joins
- C. Hypercharge adds across a product
- D. The two Higgs hypercharges
- E. The hypercharge sieve on two fermions against one Higgs
- F. The twelve surviving blocks
- G. Invariants modulo a gauge-stable submodule

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The sector at mass weight eight, decomposed

## B. Splitting a Higgs-fermion-fermion product along its joins

The two fermion factors are each a join over ten species, so the product has to be
distributed over both before any species-level statement can be made.  The left factor is
handled by `FermionSector.piece_sup_mul`; the two lemmas here reach the inner factors of
a triple product, which that lemma cannot see.

## C. Hypercharge adds across a product

`FermionSector.mul_piece_zero_eq_bot_of_hypercharge` kills a product of two
decompositions whose constant hypercharges do not cancel.  To use it on a triple product
the two fermion factors have to be read as a single decomposition, and the only thing
needed about them is that their hypercharges add.
## D. The two Higgs hypercharges

## E. The hypercharge sieve on two fermions against one Higgs

Everything the Standard Model gauge group has to say about which Yukawa couplings exist is
already said by hypercharge.  A block of the mass-weight-eight decomposition is a Higgs
symbol against a pair of fermion species, and the three hypercharges have to cancel.  Since
the Higgs contributes `∓3`, the fermion pair must contribute `±3`, and the ten species
charges `2, -2, -4, 4, -1, 1, 3, -3, 6, -6` admit only three unordered pairs of each sign.

The two lemmas below are stated for an arbitrary decomposition `dV` of constant hypercharge
rather than for the Higgs submodules themselves, since that is all the argument uses; the
Higgs and conjugate-Higgs cases are then two applications. No species pairs with itself,
`2f = ±3` having no integer solution.

## F. The twelve surviving blocks

The pieces now assemble.  Unfolding the Higgs derivative submodule into its Higgs and
conjugate-Higgs halves and the fermion towers into a join over families splits the product
into blocks indexed by a Higgs choice and two families, and the sieve of section E reduces
each block to six terms.  Twelve survive in all, and they are exactly the Yukawa couplings
of the Standard Model: the down-type coupling `H d barQ`, the up-type coupling `H baru Q`,
the charged-lepton coupling `H barL e`, their conjugates `barH bard Q`, `barH u barQ` and
`barH L bare`, and the transpose of each, the two fermion towers being interchangeable.

Nothing here constrains the families: all nine pairs `(f, f')` occur, which is where the
Yukawa matrices come from.

## G. Invariants modulo a gauge-stable submodule

A gauge-invariant element sits in the weight-zero piece, and the same holds modulo a
submodule `S` stable under the torus: an invariant lying in the sector joined with `S`
lies in the weight-zero piece joined with `S`.  This is what turns the twelve blocks of
section F into a statement about the invariants themselves, the remaining work being to
peel the blocks apart, which is not done here.

The statement is `GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant`, which chooses
the separating torus generator weight by weight.  That matters here: at
mass weight eight the sector carries weights of vanishing hypercharge and nonzero colour or
isospin — `H d bard` is one — so, unlike the fermion sector, no single generator sees every
weight.

declarations.doc:
The gauge weight decomposition of the Yukawa sector at mass weight eight, transported

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.piece_mul_sup_mul
declarations.doc:
If the first fermion factor of a triple product is a join `VA ⊔ VB`, its weight-`w`
piece splits along the join.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_mul_sup_mul {VX VA VB VZ : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (dX : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VX) (dA : GaugeWeightDecomposition
      repGaugeGroupI VA)
    (dB : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VB) (dZ : GaugeWeightDecomposition
      repGaugeGroupI VZ)
    (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dX)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
          (d := GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup (d := dA) (d' := dB)) (d' := dZ))).piece w
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dX)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA) (d' := dZ))).piece w
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dX)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dB) (d' := dZ))).piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.piece_mul_mul_sup
declarations.doc:
If the second fermion factor of a triple product is a join `VA ⊔ VB`, its weight-`w`
piece splits along the join.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_mul_mul_sup {VX VY VA VB : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (dX : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VX) (dY : GaugeWeightDecomposition
      repGaugeGroupI VY)
    (dA : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VA) (dB : GaugeWeightDecomposition
      repGaugeGroupI VB)
    (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dX)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dY)
          (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup (d := dA) (d' := dB)))).piece w
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dX)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dY) (d' := dA))).piece w
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dX)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dY) (d' := dB))).piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_supp_hypercharge

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_mul_speciesGaugeWeight_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece of a decomposition of constant hypercharge `h` against one of constant
hypercharge `a` and the full symbol set of a family. Only the species whose hypercharge
cancels `h + a` survive.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mul_speciesGaugeWeight_piece_zero {V VA : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    {dV : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI V}
    {dA : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI VA} {h a : ℤ}
    (hV : ∀ w ∈ dV.supp, w.2.2.2 = h) (hA : ∀ w ∈ dA.supp, w.2.2.2 = a)
    {m : ℕ} (f' : Fin 3) (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
          (d' := FermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight f' l'))).piece 0
      = (if h + (a + 2) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightD f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + -2) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + -4) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightU f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + 4) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + -1) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + 1) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + 3) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightL f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + -3) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + 6) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightE f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)
        ⊔ (if h + (a + -6) = 0 then (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dA)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarE f' l'))).piece 0 else ⊥)

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_neg_three
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge sieve against a Higgs symbol. If `dV` has constant hypercharge `-3`,
as the Higgs symbols do, then of the hundred species pairings in a product of two fermion
towers only the six whose hypercharges sum to `+3` survive at gauge weight zero, `d barQ`,
`baru Q` and `barL e`, each in both orders. The other ninety-four pairings leave a nonzero
hypercharge behind and so contribute nothing.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_neg_three
    {V : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    {dV : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI V} (hV : ∀ w ∈ dV.supp, w.2.2.2 =
      -3)
    {n m : ℕ} (f f' : Fin 3) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
          (d := FermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight f l)
          (d' := FermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight f' l'))).piece 0
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightD f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightD f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightE f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightE f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f' l'))).piece 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_pos_three
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge sieve against a conjugate-Higgs symbol. If `dV` has constant
hypercharge `3`, as the conjugate-Higgs symbols do, then of the hundred species pairings
only the six whose hypercharges sum to `-3` survive at gauge weight zero, `bard Q`,
`u barQ` and `L bare`, each in both orders.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_pos_three
    {V : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    {dV : GaugeWeightDecomposition repGaugeGroupI V} (hV : ∀ w ∈ dV.supp, w.2.2.2 = 3)
    {n m : ℕ} (f f' : Fin 3) (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (l' : Fin m → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
        (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
          (d := FermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight f l)
          (d' := FermionSector.speciesGaugeWeight f' l'))).piece 0
      = (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightU f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightU f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightL f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarE f' l'))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul (d := dV)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarE f l)
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightL f' l'))).piece 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.higgs_mul_fermion_mul_fermion_derivSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc:
The Yukawa product at mass weight eight, an underived Higgs tower against two underived
fermion towers, as a join over pairs of families.
declarations.statement:
lemma higgs_mul_fermion_mul_fermion_derivSubmodule_zero : ScalarSector.derivSubmodule 0
    * (FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0 * FermionSector.derivSubmodule 0)
    = ⨆ (f : Fin 3) (f' : Fin 3),
      (ScalarSector.higgsSubmodule 0 ⊔ ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmodule 0)
        * ((LinearMap.range (downSingletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjDownSingletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (upSingletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjUpSingletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (quarkDoubletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjQuarkDoubletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (leptonDoubletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjLeptonDoubletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (leptonSingletField f ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjLeptonSingletField f ![]))
          * (LinearMap.range (downSingletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjDownSingletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (upSingletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjUpSingletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (quarkDoubletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjQuarkDoubletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (leptonDoubletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjLeptonDoubletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (leptonSingletField f' ![]) ⊔
          LinearMap.range (conjLeptonSingletField f' ![])))

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece of the Yukawa sector at mass weight eight, the join, over pairs
of families, of the twelve blocks that hypercharge allows.  Of the two hundred ways of
choosing one Higgs symbol and two fermion species, only these twelve have vanishing total
hypercharge; the remaining one hundred and eighty-eight are killed by
`mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_neg_three` and
`mul_speciesGaugeWeight_mul_piece_zero_pos_three`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight.piece 0
      = ⨆ (f : Fin 3) (f' : Fin 3),
        (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightD f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightD f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarU f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightE f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.higgsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightE f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarL f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightQ f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarD f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightU f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarQ f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightU f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
              (d := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightL f ![])
              (d' := FermionSector.rangeGaugeWeightBarE f' ![]))).piece 0
        ⊔ (GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
            (d := ScalarSector.barHiggsSubmoduleGaugeWeight 0)
            (d' := GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeightEight_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
A gauge-invariant element of the Yukawa sector at mass weight eight joined with a
torus-stable `S` lies in the weight-zero piece joined with `S`, so the twelve blocks of
`sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero` are all that a Yukawa invariant can be
built from.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeightEight_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant
    {S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hS : ∀ (i : Fin 4) (y : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra), y ∈ S →
      repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 8
      ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) :
    x ∈ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight.piece 0 ⊔ S

modules.title: The Yukawa sector at mass weight eight
modules.doc:
The gauge- and Lorentz-invariant Yukawa terms of the Standard Model's covariant field algebra.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

This is the theorem the Yukawa sector exists for.  At mass weight eight the sector is one
Higgs tower against two underived fermion towers, and the claim proved here is that its
gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content, modulo a submodule `S` stable under both groups, is
exactly the span of the six Yukawa couplings over the nine family pairs.  Nothing else
survives, neither a fourth coupling, nor extra colour or isospin structure inside a surviving
block, nor an invariant carrying a free spinor index.

Three things are already done and are used as given.  Hypercharge has sieved the two
hundred blocks of the gauge weight decomposition down to twelve, in
`sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero`.  A gauge invariant of the sector lies in
that weight-zero piece modulo `S`, by `mem_sectorMassWeightEight_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant`.
And the six couplings, their index laws and their contractions are built in the `Families`
files, together with `yukawaSpan_le_inf`, which is the easy direction of the equivalence.

What is left is the reduction.  A block of the decomposition is a product of three symbol
ranges, and the classification of its invariants is three classifications in a row —
colour, then isospin, then Lorentz — each cutting the span down to the span of one
contraction.  The three groups are different, and the fifty-four surviving blocks have to
be reduced one at a time, so the argument is organised around a single relation
`ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W`, saying that a `σ`-invariant of `V ⊔ S` lies in `W ⊔ S` whenever `S` is
`σ`-stable. That relation composes, being transitive, antitone in its source, monotone in its
target, and closed under joins of stable sources, and each `GaugeGroup` or `LorentzGroup`
classification used here is an instance of it, packaged as an `InvariantReductionToSpan`.

## ii. Key results

- `sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero_le` : the weight-zero piece inside the six
  surviving block submodules.
- `reducesInvariantsTo_yukawaSpan` : the six blocks, over the nine family pairs, reduce to the
  Yukawa span.
- `reducesInvariantsTo_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight` : the sector at mass weight
  eight reduces to the Yukawa span.
- `mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the
  classification as an equivalence, in the form the sibling sectors state it in.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The symbol ranges as spans of components
- B. The block submodules and their stability
- C. The twelve surviving blocks as six submodules
- D. The blocks reduce to the Yukawa terms
- E. The classification of the invariants of mass weight eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The symbol ranges as spans of components

## B. The block submodules and their stability

A surviving block of the decomposition is the product of a Higgs range with two fermion
ranges, and this is the submodule the classification of that block runs inside.  All six
are carried into themselves by both groups, each factor being the range of an equivariant
symbol map with no derivative slots for the Lorentz group to mix, and a product of stable
submodules being stable.  That stability is what lets the six blocks — fifty-four of them
once the family pairs are counted — be reduced one at a time, each in turn joining the
error term of the others.

## C. The twelve surviving blocks as six submodules

The twelve blocks that hypercharge leaves come in six transposed pairs, and a pair is one
submodule: the two fermion factors commute as submodules, by `mul_comm_of_le_derivSubmodule`,
so exchanging them changes nothing.  Under the join over family pairs the transposed block
of `(f, f')` is the untransposed block of `(f', f)`, and the weight-zero piece of the sector
lands inside the join of the six.

## D. The blocks reduce to the Yukawa terms

Each block is classified in three stages, and each stage is the same move: one index law
holds at every value of the indices it does not see, so a family of steps is applied at
once by `InvariantReductionToSpan.reducesInvariantsTo_iSup`, and what comes out is the span of
the contractions, which is the source of the next stage. Colour first, then isospin, then Lorentz —
the order is forced, each contraction being a spectator of the ones after it.

The two lepton blocks have no colour index at all, so their first stage is
`InvariantReductionToSpan.ofFixed` rather than a classification: the block is already fixed by the
colour factor and the stage reduces it to itself. That keeps them in the same three-stage shape as
the four quark blocks.

## E. The classification of the invariants of mass weight eight

The two directions meet.  Forwards: the torus reduces the sector to its weight-zero piece,
the piece lies in the six block submodules, and the blocks reduce to the Yukawa span.
Backwards: `yukawaSpan_le_inf` says the Yukawa span is made of invariants of the right mass
weight to begin with, which turns the reduction into an equivalence rather than a one-way
inclusion.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero_le
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece of the Yukawa sector at mass weight eight lies in the join of the
six block submodules over the nine family pairs. The twelve blocks of
`sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero` become six because the two fermion factors
of a block commute, so the transposed block of `(f, f')` is the block of `(f', f)`; and
the weight refinement inside a block is dropped, hypercharge having already done its
work and colour, isospin and Lorentz being what decide the rest.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight_piece_zero_le :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sectorMassWeightEightGaugeWeight.piece 0 ≤
      LocalCovFieldAlgebra.blockSubmodule

The Yukawa sector at mass weight eight reduces, for the gauge and Lorentz groups
together, to the Yukawa span. Hypercharge puts an invariant in the weight-zero piece, the
piece lies in the six block submodules, and colour, isospin and Lorentz reduce each block
to its Yukawa term.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification of the Yukawa sector at mass weight eight as an equivalence. An
element of the sector joined with a submodule `S` stable under both groups is fixed by
both groups exactly when it is a combination of the six Yukawa couplings over the nine
family pairs up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGaugeGroupI g
      y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 8 ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.yukawaSpan

modules.title: The Yukawa invariants below mass weight eight
modules.doc:
No gauge- and Lorentz-invariant Yukawa term of the covariant field algebra sits below weight eight.

## i. Overview

Everything below is stated about the covariant field algebra `fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of the
Standard Model.

Mass weight eight is the first weight at which the Yukawa sector can carry an invariant.
It is the weight of `H ψ ψ`, one Higgs against two fermions. Below it the sector is nearly
empty — it vanishes outright below weight five and again at weight six — and the little
that survives, at weights five and seven, is barred from carrying an invariant by a parity
count.

The count is on spin, not on the number of covector indices as in the gauge sector. The
Higgs is a Lorentz scalar and a fermion carries one Weyl-spinor index, so each of the four
products surviving at weights five and seven, having exactly one fermion factor, is of
half-integer spin, and a half-integer spin carries no Lorentz invariant.

The count is run at the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`, where `Invariants/CentreEigenspace.lean` puts it. The
element `-1` covers the identity Lorentz transformation, so it acts by `+1` on the Higgs
derivative submodules and by `-1` on the fermion ones, and the Lorentz action on the
covariant field algebra of the Standard Model is by algebra maps, so the signs multiply over a
product. Section A does that multiplication for
the four products, and the peeling modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule `S` is
`mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one`.

Unlike the gauge-sector statement, the final statement needs no `0 < w`. The Yukawa sector
is a product of two non-empty sectors, so it already vanishes at weight zero and the
scalars never enter.

## ii. Key results

- `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_five_sup`,
  `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_seven_sup` : mass weights five and seven
  carry no Lorentz invariant, being of half-integer spin.
- `mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the
  classification below mass weight eight as an equivalence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Integer Higgs against half-integer fermion
- B. Mass weights five and seven
- C. The classification below mass weight eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Integer Higgs against half-integer fermion

The signs the two factors carry at the centre are already proved: the Higgs derivative
submodules carry `+1`, being Lorentz scalars with inert derivative slots, and the fermion
ones carry `-1`, the Weyl-spinor value index doing the work. The Lorentz action on the
covariant field algebra is by algebra maps, so the sign of a product is the product of the
signs, and each of the products surviving below weight eight has exactly one fermion
factor. The term with two
Higgs factors multiplies twice, `+1` against `+1` staying `+1` before the fermion turns the
total `-1`.

## B. Mass weights five and seven

Weight five is a single product, the Higgs field against the underived fermion towers.
Weight seven is a join of three: the Higgs field against the once-derived towers, the
once-derived Higgs field against the underived ones, and two Higgs fields against the
underived ones. Each of the four has exactly one fermion factor, so section A gives all of
them the sign `-1`, the join included, and the invariant is left in `S`.

## C. The classification below mass weight eight

The eight weights below eight are now settled: the sector vanishes below weight five and
at weight six, and weights five and seven are section B. So below weight eight the Yukawa
sector supplies no invariant beyond what `S` already carries, and the equivalences record
it.

No lower bound on the weight is needed, unlike the gauge-sector statement. The Yukawa
sector is the two-class sector of the Higgs and fermion generators, so both classes must
be present with a non-zero weight and the sector is already trivial at weight zero; the
scalars, which are what force `0 < w` there, never appear.

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_five_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight five carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule. A
Lorentz invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {scalar, fermion} 5 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. The
weight is one Higgs field against the underived fermion towers, of half-integer spin.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_five_sup
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 5
      ⊔ S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.doc:

Lorentz invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {scalar, fermion} 7 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. Each of the
three products making up the weight has a single fermion factor, so each is of
half-integer spin and so is their join.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_seven_sup
    (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)

      ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} 7

Below mass weight eight the Yukawa sector carries no Lorentz invariant. A Lorentz
invariant of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {scalar, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 8` lies in `S`. Weights
below five and weight six are trivial submodules, and weights five and seven are section
B.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_lt_eight_sup (w : ℕ)
    (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) {x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w
      ⊔ S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of the
gauge-sector statement `mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`.
An element of `fieldData.sectorMassWeight {scalar, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 8` is fixed by both
groups exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups. Gauge stability
of `S` is not needed, and neither is gauge invariance of `x`. The forward direction is
the spin parity argument, which uses the Lorentz group alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential. Below mass weight eight an element of
`fieldData.sectorMassWeight {scalar, fermion} w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of
`S` fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_higgs_fermion_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup g y ∈ S) (x : fieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ fieldData.sectorMassWeight {FieldKind.scalar, FieldKind.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ),
          repLorentzGroup g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup g x = x)
